records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have reviewed the requirements of storage of foodgrains in the country;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) whether Government have drafted proposals in this regard, if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION ( SHRI SHARAD YADAV )

(a),(b)&(c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE STARRED QUESTION NO.155 DUE FOR ANSWER ON 11-12-2003 IN THE RAJYA SABHA.

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The existing storage capacity available with various agencies is sufficient to meet the requirements of buffer stocks, Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) and other Welfare Schemes in the country.

(c) To meet the growing demand of storage capacity, the Government has announced a National Policy on handling, storage and transportation of foodgrains under which private sector participation is being encouraged for development of infrastructure for the integrated bulk handling, storage and transportation.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that only 5 percent youths under the age group of 20-24 years have capability of professional skill;

(b) if not, Government’s assessment in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that Government have assessed requirement of the skilled professional capability in the country; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR (SHRI SAHIB SINGH VERMA)

(a) & (b) Skill is acquired through formal vocational training and through informal means. It is estimated that only 5% of the labour force in the age group of 20-24 years have acquired skills through formal vocational training.

(c)& (d) In order to provide formal vocational training to the dropouts after 8th,10th & 12th standards, it is estimated that the requirements of skill training may be to the extent of 200 lakh per year.

records.qtitle: MONETARY ASSISTANCE RECEIVED BY TERRORISTS THROUGH HAWALA
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that separatists/terrorists of J&K receive illegal monetary assistance through `Hawala`;

(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that annual figure amounts to Rs.250 crores;

(c) if not, the information Government have in this regard; and

(d) the average annual illegal amount seized by the administration during the recent years which was meant for terrorists?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI I.D. SWAMI)

(a): Yes Sir, Hawala is one of the sources of funds for sustaining separatists/terrorists in J&K.

(b)&(c): It is not possible to quantify the exact amount involved. However, according to estimates of various agencies, the monthly flow of funds is believed to be between Rs.5 and 10 crore.

(d): As per information that has become available from various sources over Rs.4.00 crore in Indian currency and approximately $10.50 Lacs in foreign currency in addition to approximately Rs.11.50 Lacs in fake currency suspected to be meant for separatists/ terrorists have been seized during the recent years.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that `Prasar Bharati has been incurring continuous losses due to the functioning of Doordarshan;

(b) if so, whether these losses are being made up by Government for the last few years; and

(c) if so, the amount of losses has compensated by Government upto the 31st March, 2003?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)




(a), (b) & (c): Under Section 12 of Prasar Bharat Act, 1990, the primary duty of the Corporation is to organize and conduct public broadcasting services to inform, educate and entertain the public and to ensure a balanced development of broadcasting on radio and television. Therefore, Prasar Bharati is not being run on commercial basis and hence are not maintaining profit and loss account. However, the deficit between income and expenditure of Prasar Bharati is being met by the Government since accounts of Prasar Bharati were de-linked from Government. A total of Rs. 3368.65 crores has been provided by the Government to the Corporation from 1st April 2000 to March 2003.

(c) if so, the names of departments to which the said report belongs to and what has been mentioned in the report ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R.BAALU)

(a) The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee accorded conditional clearance for commercial cultivation of three Bt cotton hybrids developed by M/s Mahyco, Mumbai for a period of three years from April 2002 to March 2005 in six states namely Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

records.qtitle: USE OF GAS BY UREA PRODUCING UNITS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have formulated any scheme of promoting the use of gas in place of Naphtha as a fuel by urea producing units of the country;

(b) if so, the detailed outlines of the said scheme;

(c) total number of industrial units of the country under this scheme which are likely to use gas in place of Naphtha; and

(d) expenditure likely to be incurred by Government for the same?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (DR. CHHATTRA PAL SINGH)

(a) to (d): The primary consideration and goal of the new pricing scheme for urea units, made effective from 1.4.2003, is to encourage efficiency parameters of international standards based on the usage of the most efficient feedstock. Natural gas (NG)/ Liquefied Natural gas (LNG), being an efficient feedstock for the manufacture of urea, besides being a clean and cost effective source of energy, facilitating the switchover of the existing non-gas based urea units to NG/LNG for feedstock/fuel is being considered for Stage-III. Preliminary estimates have revealed that in case of naphtha based plants, the estimated cost of conversion would be of the order of Rs.20-25 crore, whereas in the case of FO/LSHS based plants, such cost would be of the order of Rs. 250 crore or more depending on the scope of revamp and engineering process. The cost differences are attributable to the size, vintage, technology of the plant etc.
At present, there are 14 non-gas based urea units. Their switchover to NG/LNG will depend on the availability of NG/LNG, delivered price of NG/LNG and the infrastructure available. The cost of conversion is to be financed by the respective units.

records.qtitle: DONATION TO CONSULTATIVE GROUP ON INTERNATIONAL AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH .
records.name: Kapil Sibal

(b) if so, the amount of regular donation being given annually to the institution;

(c) whether the operation of the said institute is being carried out from abroad;

(d) if so, the place of operation and the details of agricultural activities of the said institute;

(e) whether the country has got any advantage from the research conducted by this institution; and

(f) if so, the benefits accrued to Indian farmers from this institution for the development in the agriculture sector?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE
(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) US $ 7,50,000/-.

(c) & (d): The Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research (CGIAR) is housed in the headquarters of the World Bank at Washington, DC, USA. It supports a network of 16 International Agricultural Research Centres, also called as Future Harvest Centres. The mission of the CGIAR is to achieve sustainable food security and reduce poverty in developing countries through scientific research and research related activities in the fields of agriculture, forestry, fisheries, policy and environment and to realize this mission, the CGIAR have adopted a strategy comprising of the seven following elements, namely, (a) people and poverty focus, (b) modern science, (c) geographic priorities, (d) regional approach to research, (e) new partners in science, (f) task force approach and (g) catalytic role.

(e) & (f): The CGIAR, with its focus on public sector research, has been beneficial to the developing countries like India in the following ways. 
 

1.	Developing new varieties, particularly in rice, wheat, 
maize, pulses and nutrition cereals. 


2.	Supply of Germ Plasm of rice, wheat, maize, pulses and potato. 


3.	Technology Transfer. 


4. 	Support for Frontier Technology like GIS.  


5. 	Disease monitoring, containment and alerting across international 
borders.
6. 	Training of scientists by its various Centres has been beneficial in the 
	form of indirect benefit to the farmers.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRIMATI SUMITRA MAHAJAN)

(a) to (d) : ONGC-Videsh Limited (OVL) has so far invested US$ 921.31 million (Rs. 4238 crore, approximately) in the Sakhalin-I Project of Russia. Revision of cost estimates in oil and gas projects is a normal industry practice as the projects progress from the initial exploration phase to the development phase. During this process, costs and schedule get refined, based on factors such as reserve estimates, technological aspects and financial & economic parameters.
ONGC-Videsh Limited (OVL) has informed that in the case of Sakhalin-I Project, the current estimated reserves for oil and gas are higher as compared to the reserves estimated at the time of approval of the project, thus interalia necessitating higher costs which are not final as of today.
Further, OVL has informed that as per the present scenario, the expected rate of return between 10-12% still remains attractive.

(c) : The information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.
ANNEXURE
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2483 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 13.08.2003 The following PSUs/organizations are working under administrative control of Ministry of Power:- 

i)	Central Electricity Authority
ii)	National Thermal Power Corporation
iii)	National Hydro-electric Power Corporation
iv)	North Eastern Electric Power Corporation 
v)	Rural Electrification Corporation 
vi)	Power Finance Corporation 
vii)	Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. 
viii)	Power Trading Corporation
ix)	Tehri Hydro Development Corporation
x)	Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd. 
xi)	Damodar Valley Corporation
xii)	Bhakra Beas Management Board
xiii)	Central Power Research Institute
xiv)	National Power Training Institute
xv)	Bureau of Energy Efficiency 
xvi)	Central Electricity Regulatory Commission


Details about the above organizations such as their objectives/functions etc are 
available on this Ministry`s website (www.powermin.nic.in).  However, main 
responsibilities entrusted to each organization are as follows:-
Central Electricity Authority:	The Authority generally exercises such functions 
and performs such duties as prescribed under Section 73 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or 
by the issue of written directions of the Government in the matter of policy involving 
public interest under Section 75 of the Act.  


	The functions include rendering advice to Central Govt. on matters relating to the 
National Electricity Policy, formulation of short-term and perspective plans for 
development of the electricity system and coordination of the activities of the planning 
agencies for the optimal utilization of resources to sub-serve the interests of the national 
economy and provide reliable and affordable electricity for all consumers. 
National Thermal Power Corporation:	The corporation is engaged in 
operating/setting up of thermal/hydel power projects and gas based power projects. 
National Hydro-electric Power Corporation:	The corporation deals in 
construction, generation, operation and maintenance of Hydroelectric, Geo-thermal, Gas 
power Stations and Projects. 
North-eastern Electric Power Corporation:	The corporation is engaged in 
development of the enormous power potential of the North-Eastern Region of the country 
through execution of power generation projects. 


Rural Electrification Corporation:		The corporation, as a financial institution, 
supplements the resources of the SEBs/State Power Utilities/State Governments for 
various power projects including schemes for rural electrification, as are sponsored by the 
borrowing entities. 


Power Finance Corporation:	The mission of the corporation is to function as the 
prime Development Financial Institution dedicated to the growth and overall 
development of the Power Sector. 


Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd.:	The corporation supervise, operate and 
maintain Energy Transmission System.   Establish/operate all Regional Load Despatch 
Centres and Communication facilities and participate in long distance trunk 
telecommunication business ventures. 


Power Trading Corporation:	The corporation`s main function is to catalyse 
development of Mega Power Projects and other power projects by acting as a singly 
entity to enter into Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with Independent Power 
Producers (IPPs) on the one side and Multipartite PPAs  with users/SEBs under long term 
arrangement on the other.  PTC has also been mandated for power trading to optimally 
utilize the existing resources in the country as also promoting exchange of power with 
neighbouring countries. 


Tehri Hydro Development Corporation:	The corporation`s main function is to plan, 
promote and organize an integrated and efficient development of hydro resources of 
Bhagirathi river and its tributaries at Tehri. 


Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd. :	The corporation`s main function is to execute hydro 
power projects in Satluj basin within Himachal Pradesh. 


Damodar Valley Corporation:		DVC is committed to the economic and 
industrial growth of the Damodar Valley region which extends over an area of 24235 sq. 
kms in the States of Jharkhand and West Bengal. 


Bhakra Beas Management Board:		The Board is responsible for the 
administration, operation & maintenance of Bhakra Nangal project, Beas Sutlej Link 
Project and Pong Dam including Power Houses and a network of transmission lines and 
grid sub-stations. 


Central Power Research Institute:		CPRI functions as an National Power 
Research Organization and serve as a National Testing & certification Authority for 
electrical equipment used in power sector. 


National Power Training Institute:		The institute`s main function is Power 
Training.   


Bureau of Energy Efficiency:	The Bureau is responsible for spearheading the 
improvement of energy efficiency through various regulatory and promotional 
instruments. 


Central Electricity Regulatory Commission:   The Central Electricity Regulatory 
Commission (CERC), an independent statutory body with quasi judicial powers, was 
constituted on 25-7-1998 under the Electricity Regulatory Commission Act, 1998, since 
`repealed` and deemed to have been constituted under Section 76 of the Electricity Act, 
2003.   The functions of the Commission are:  (a)	To regulate the tariff of generating 
companies owned or controlled by the Central Government; (b)  To regulate inter-state 
transmission including tariff of the transmission entities;  (c) To promote competition, 
efficiency and economy in the sector; (d)  To regulate inter-State bulk sale of power;  (e)  
To aid and advise the Central Govt. in formulation of tariff policy and to frame guidelines 
relating to electricity tariff; (f)  To associate with the environmental regulatory agencies 
towards developing policies and procedures for environmental regulations for the power 
sector; and (g)  To arbitrate or adjudicate in matters relating to tariff.

records.qtitle: CAPTIVE POWER PROJECTS IN PRIVATE SECTOR .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that captive power projects are operating in private sector for power production in the country;

(b) if so, the production capacity of these projects as on March, 2003 along with assessment with regard to the average production cost;

(c) whether it is a fact that power is being produced in this sector more than the requirement; and

(d) if so, the details of the said surplus power?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

(a) : Yes Sir.

(b) : The overall capacity addition programme for the country does not take into account captive power plants and as such, details of captive power plants being set up by private sector are not available. However, as per available information, the all India captive installed capacity (1 MW and above) of select industries was 16156 MW as on 31.3.2001. Unlike the independent power plants (IPP) set up by private sector, captive power plants are not required to obtain Techno-Economic Clearance of the Central Electricity Authority(CEA) and therefore, details of the cost are not available. Moreover, the cost of production of electricity from different projects varies depending on the size and the type of the power plant, cost of fuel used, location and technology used etc. The cost of production also varies from time to time depending on the quantum of power generated and off-take of surplus power, if any.


(c) : The power generated by captive power plant is primarily used by the linked industrial unit(s). Surplus power, if any, can be made available to the State Electricity Boards (SEB) on mutually agreed terms and conditions.
On July 11, 2001, the Government of India (Ministry of Power) has circulated a Captive Power Policy prepared in consultation with the Central Electricity Authority, to all the State Governments and Union Territories, which recommends purchase of power by State Utilities from spare capacity in captive power plants.
In the conference of the State Power Ministers held at New Delhi on 5th August, 2002, a strategy was evolved to tackle the power demand during the then prevailing drought situation. The strategy evolved included, inter-alia, increase of generation from existing thermal power plants and utilization of spare capacity of captive power plants, etc.

(d) : The performance of captive power plants is not being monitored by the Central Government. However, as per available information, the electricity generated by captive power plants during the year 2000-2001 was 59637.96 GWH out of which, 3188.56 GWH was sold to State Electricity Boards / Utilities.

records.qtitle: POST PRODUCTION LOSS IN AGRICULTURE SECTOR .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that 25 percent of post production crop is assessed to be lost in agriculture sector of the country;

(b) if not, facts in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that such loss could be minimized with the use of advanced technology; and

(d) if so, facts in this regard and how it compares with loss in agriculture sector at international level?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)

(a)&(b): A Committee headed by Dr. V.G. Panse, in its report submitted in 1968, had estimated annual post harvest losses in the foodgrains in various stages at 9.33%. These included losses during threshing (1.68%), transportation (0.15%), processing (0.92%), rodents (2.50%), birds (0.85), insects

(2.55%) and moisture (0.68%). A survey conducted by Directorate of Marketing and inspection, during 1973-74, had estimated post harvest losses in foodgrains to be about 5% out of which the storages losses were estimated at about 2.7%. A joint survey conducted by the Indian Agricultural Statistics Research Institute and Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute during 1985-88 in Bulandshahar district of Uttar Pradesh had estimated total foodgrains losses at about

4.12% due to different factors at various post harvest stages. Losses during storage and transit of foodgrains in the organized sector is however, less than 0.5% and 1.5% respectively.
The high level Committee on Cold Storage and Storage constituted by Department of Agriculture & Cooperation under the Chairmanship of Shri JNL Srivastava, Additional Secretary, in its Report of February 1999 has estimated 25% to 30% post-harvest losses in horticultural produce depending upon the produce, season and the length of journey.

(c): Yes, Sir.


(d): In order to reduce losses to food-grains during the post harvest period, the Government of India had launched the Save Grain Campaign in 1969-70. The main thrust of activities of this Scheme is training, demonstration and publicity in the field of scientific storage of foodgrains at the farm level. Improvement of grain storage structure and popularization of scientific storage structures like metal bins, pucca kothis and RCC ring bins and other activities are carried out by the Save Grain Campaign for the benefit of farmers.
Foodgrains stocks at commercial level are stored by various agencies on scientific lines during which necessary prophylactic and curative measures are undertaken to reduce losses.
In order to promote scientific storage facilities in rural areas and to prevent quantitative and qualitative losses of the produce of the farmers, a Central Sector Scheme of construction/renovation of Rural Godowns titled `Grameen Bhandaran Yojana` is being implemented in the country since 2001-2002. Under the Scheme, Central Government is providing investment subsidy to individual farmers, Self Help Group (SHG), Cooperatives, Corporations, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committees etc. Subsidy is provided @25% of the capital cost of the project not exceeding Rs.50 .00 lakh for each storage project through National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

(NABARD) and National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). A higher subsidy of 33.3% of capital cost not exceeding Rs.60.00 lakhs is provided for beneficiaries belonging to SC/ST and for North-Eastern States and hilly areas. So far under the scheme, NABARD has sanctioned 995 projects with a capacity of 59.29 lakh tonnes. In addition, 1575 projects with a capacity of 7.42 lakh tonnes have been sanctioned by NCDC for construction of new rural godowns.
A Capital investment Subsidy Scheme for construction of cold storage is being implemented by National Horticulture Board (NHB) through NABARD and NCDC to enhance the storage capacity for perishable commodities. Under the scheme, back-ended capital investment subsidy is provided to the eligible organisation @ 25% of the project cost not exceeding Rs.50.00 lakh per project and @ 33.33% of the project cost upto a ceiling Rs.60.00 lakh per project for North Eastern States. The Board has, so far, approved assistance of Rs.208.17 crore under the scheme for creation of additional storage capacity of 31.79 lakh tonnes.
No study has been conducted to compare post harvest losses in India with other countries.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN SETHI)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (c) OF THE STARRED QUESTION NO + 234 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON

5.8.2003.

(a) Water being a State Subject, river valley projects involving storage of water in reservoirs of varying capacities are conceived, planned and executed by the respective State Governments according to their own priorities. As per information provided by the States to the Working Group on Major & Medium Irrigation Programme for the Tenth Five Year plan, 67 major and 130 medium Projects are planned to taken up during Tenth Five Year Plan for water utilization.

(b) The average annual flow in rivers of the country has been assessed as 1869 Billion Cubic Meter (BCM). Out of this, the average annual utilizable water is about 1122 BCM. Presently 605 BCM of water is being utilized for diverse purposes.

(c) As per the Tenth Five Year Plan document of the Planning Commission, it is expected that 103 major and 240 medium projects may be completed during the Tenth Five Year Plan. This includes the projects spilling over from the previous Plans to the Tenth Five Year Plan. The total live storage capacity of the existing reservoirs in the country is about 177 BCM. With the completion of ongoing projects, the live storage capacity is likely to further increase by about 75 BCM. Further, projects having additional live storage capacity of about 132 BCM are under formulation/consideration.

MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW & JUSTICE (SHRI P.C. THOMAS)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The canvas of Judicial reforms is very wide, encompassing wide spectrum of issues concerning different departments of me Government. A series of steps have been taken by the Government on the front of Judicial reforms. High Courts have been requested to implement the recommendations of the Malimath Committee to streamline procedure which will, inter-alia, expedite disposal of pending cases. Government have also been constantly reviewing the
accumulation of arrears in courts. Besides reviewing and increasing judge strength of High Courts every three years, Government have encouraged alternative modes of dispute resolution including conciliation, mediation and arbitration. Special tribunals like Central Administrative Tribunal, State Administrative Tribunals, Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, Labour Courts, Consumer Courts etc., have been set up to expedite the disposal of cases. Information Technology is being used in generation of causelists, providing information to the litigants/advocates etc., for speedy disposal of cases. A Pilot project has been started for Networking and Computerisation of City Courts in the four major metrocities of Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata and Mumbai to serve as a model. The project is aimed at augmenting capacities of courts and speeding up their disposal through better court management with the help of information technology. Civil Procedure Code has been amended and the amendments have been brought into force with effect from 1.07.2002 which, inter-alia, limit the number of adjournments which can be granted to a party to three, provide for speedy process service by speed post, courier services, fax or e-mail, authorise the court to fix time limit for oral arguments & provide for a number of other measures aimed at ensuring expeditious disposal of cases. Permanent Lok Adalats are being set up for expeditious resolution of disputes relating to public utilities. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme funds have also been provided for the use of Information Technology in the High Courts. Fast Track Courts have been set up to speed up the trial of delayed cases, and in particular the cases of under-trials who have been in jail for a long time. State Governments & Union Territories have been requested to fill up vacant posts of Judges/Magistrates & supporting staff in District/Subordinate Courts.

(c) & (d) Suggestions for improvement in the judicial system of the country are received from time to time and these are considered by the Government on their merits. Such suggestions relate to, inter-alia, speedy disposal of cases, appointment of Special Judicial Magistrates, creation of Fast Track Courts, establishment of more Family Courts and setting up of tribunals etc. The action taken by the Government have been enumerated in reply to Part (b).

records.qtitle: (clubbed) INTRODUCTION OF RASHTRIYA PUNERNIRMAN VAHINI PROJECT .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a)whether it is a fact that a project named `Rashtriya Punernirman Vahini` was introduced for the purpose of including the sense of social service in youth of the country;

(b)if so, the date on which the said scheme was introduced and names of States alongwith the places of the country where the said scheme is in force; and

(c)the number of youth included in the said scheme by June, 2003 and whether this scheme is now going to be discontinued?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS

(SHRI VIJAY GOEL)

(a) Yes, Sir. The Rashtriya Punarnirman Vahini Scheme was implemented to inculcate the spirit of patriotism and to raise the level of volunteerism in the society, especially among the youth. The Scheme provided an opportunity to youth to participate in the process of Nation Building and to involve the youth in various developmental programmes, which could bring about a socio-economic transformation of our society and the Nation.

(b) The Rashtriya Punarnirman Vahini scheme was initially launched on a pilot basis for two years in 80 districts of the country in the year 2000-01. However, due to various constraints, the scheme could be operationalised in 76 districts in 27 States of the country w.e.f. April, 2001. The scheme was extended to 40 more districts in 21 States in the month of June, 2002 . A statement showing the names of the states & the districts is annexed.

(c) A total of 11,600 youth volunteers were involved in the scheme for two years i.e. for 2001-02 & 2002-03. Since the scheme was launched w.e.f. April 2001 for two years only on pilot basis, the scheme is not in operation now.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that subsidy is provided on steel production in several steel producing countries of the world;

(b) if so, the names of the countries where there is still a system of providing subsidy on steel products by their respective Governments; and

(c) the names of the countries in which subsidy was provided during 2000-2001, 2001-2002 and first nine months 2002-2003 alongwith the amount thereof under this system?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (SHRI BRAJA KISHORE TRIPATHY) IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL

(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. In several steel producing countries of the world like USA, UK, Austria, France, Greece etc. specific as well as generic subsidies are provided.

(c) In accordance with the provisions of Article 25 of the Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures, WTO member countries are required to notify any specific subsidy granted or maintained in their territory. Certain countries have notified subsidies granted or maintained in their territories to the WTO. However, these notifications are not adequately detailed to provide information on the total amount of subsidies being provided by various countries on steel production. In any case, there is no obligation on the WTO Member countries to notify the non-specific subsidies.

records.qtitle: PRICE OF FERTILIZERS IN INTERNATIONAL MARKET
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that average prices of chemical fertilizers at the international market during the year 2002-03 were found less than that of average prices of the same in the Indian market;

(b) the average prices of all the chemical fertilizers at the Indian market as well as international market; and

(c) what are the factors for which prices of chemicals and fertilizers are found higher in the Indian market?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICAL AND FERTILIZERS

(DR. CHHATTRA PAL SINGH)


(a)&(b): The Maximum Retail Price (MRP) for urea as notified by the Government has been Rs.4830 per MT during the year 2002-03 which was lower than the average international price of $132.22 per MT (exchange rate of Rs.48.40). In case of DAP, the indicative MRP during the year 2002-03 has been Rs.9350 per MT, against this the average international price of DAP was $ 192.76 per MT and with the average rupee- dollar conversion rate, the average import price of DAP was approximately the same as the MRP in 2002-03 in the country. As regards Muriat of Potash (MOP), since there are no exploitable reserves of MOP in the country, its entire requirement is met from import. On the other hand, there are no imports of complex fertilizers and Single Super Phosphate (SSP) in the country.


(c): The main reason for the higher cost of production of urea in India is the costlier feedstock compared to the prevalent cost in the other exporting countries in the world. As regard DAP, the variation in the cost of indigenous DAP compared to imported DAP is primarily because of the reason that more than 90% of the raw material/intermediates required for its production are imported and their cost in the international market fluctuate depending on demand supply position.

records.qtitle: PEOPLE REPORTED MISSING IN J K
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that 3,744 people are reported to be missing in Jammu and Kashmir during last three years;

(b) if not, the facts in this regard;

(c) whether any action has been taken by Government to ascertain the whereabouts of these people; and

(d) if so, the information gathered about these people so far and the number of persons out of the same who are supposed to be out of the country even now?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)

(a)&(b): As per the State Government of Jammu & Kashmir, an estimated number of 3744 persons have been reported to be missing till date.

(c)&(d): State Government has informed that most among the missing persons have reportedly been allured by mentors of terrorism and they are believed to have gone across the LoC/IB for obtaining subversive training or are working with the terrorists as their guides/local trained militants over here. In recent past a number of such reported missing persons had been killed in encounters with SF/Police thereby substantiating that these missing persons had become terrorists.
In all the cases of missing/disappearance whenever the report is received at police station level, immediate cognizance is taken. In all such cases, missing reports are entered in the records of concerned police stations and missing files opened. The police at Thana level also make all efforts to trace such missing persons. Information is shared at appropriate levels to ensure tracing out the individuals.

(a)It is not possible to comment on whether the rate of tax on diesel & petrol in India is higher than that of America, France, UK, etc. as information relating to tax rates in these countries is not readily available.

(b) The rate of domestic taxes are determined by the need to generate revenue. In the case of diesel & petrol, the revenue generated is also used to subsidise kerosene and LPG. Basides, the cess is used for the purpose of funding road development. Thus the domestic tax rates do not have to be fixed on the basis of tax rates applicable in other countries.

records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY)

(a) & (b) : The Government had announced a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) scheme in April 2000. As per the policy, the Central Government is not to set up any new SEZs. The scheme, however, envisages setting up of SEZ in the public, private, joint sectors or by the State Governments. Further, existing Export Processing Zones could also be converted into Special Economic Zones. In accordance with the above policy, 8 Export Processing Zones located at Santa Cruz (Maharashtra), Cochin (Kerala), Kandla and Surat (Gujarat), Chennai (Tamil Nadu), Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Falta (West Bengal) and Noida (Uttar Pradesh) have been converted into SEZs.
Based on detailed project reports submitted by the State Governments/private promoters, 3 new SEZs have been granted formal approval. In addition, `in principle` approval has been granted for setting up of 15 new SEZs.

(c) & (d) : Value of production made by the units in the SEZs, percentage and amount of production exported in the years 2000-2001, 2001-2002 and in the first in the nine months in the year 2002-2003 are :

records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any suggestions to completely transform the Food Corporation of India with a view to reducing the expenditure of the corporation;

(b) if so, when and wherefrom Government have received the same; and

(c) the details of the suggestions and the extent to which reduction in expenditure is estimated to be achieved as a result thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI V. SREENIVASA PRASAD )

(a)&(b): The Administrative Staff College of India (Hyderabad), in its Report submitted in May 2001, has, inter alia, suggested that the Government and the FCI should consider policy changes and other measures to restructure the Food Corporation of India (FCI) to reduce the expenditure of the corporation.

(c): The major recommendations in the Report with regard to the restructuring of the FCI are that the Government and the FCI should consider the `unbundling` of the FCI operations, either functionally or spatially. This could be achieved either by dividing FCI operations by handing over procurement to State Governments, distribution to the railways and physical verification and storage to the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC). An alternative suggested is to create State level Corporations to carry out all the operations within the State. The Union level FCI would limit its procurement, storage etc. to the maintenance of the buffer stocks. The expected reduction of expenditure, on account of the proposed restructuring, has not been quantified in the Report.

records.qtitle: FAULTY TELEPHONE SERVICES OF MTNL DELHI .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the telephone services of the MTNL, Delhi have been found to be most faulty than that of other telephone services of the country;

(b) if so, the facts in this regard; and

(c) the immediate steps taken by Government with a view to improving the telephone services of MTNL and the likely improvement as a result thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRIMATI SUMITRA MAHAJAN)

(a) & (b): Sir, Fault rate in Delhi unit of MTNL is slightly on the higher side. The average fault rate per hundred per month in Delhi unit for the year 2002-03 (upto 31-01-2003) is 19.99, as against average of all India fault rate of 11.00 for the same period.
Not only the Telecom network of Delhi is one of the oldest where paper core underground cables still exists but due to very fast development of basic infrastructure like construction of flyovers, widening of road, digging by other utility services to maintain and meet growing demand of fast expanding population, there are more damages to underground cables. However, the fault rate for the month of February, 2003 has been brought down to 17.27 faults per 100 subscribers per month.

(c) The steps taken to improve the telephone services of MTNL are given in Annexure. 


Annexure


	MTNL, Delhi has initiated several measures to reduce the fault rate as listed below:
1.	All the electro mechanical exchanges & analog electronic 
exehanges in MTNL, Delhi have been replaced by digital electronic 
exchanges.
2.	Paper core underground cables are being replaced by Jelly filled 
cables/Optical fibre cables with Digital Loop Carriers (D.L.Cs.).

3.	For higher capacity primary cables and junction cables, duct 
systems has been introduced.
4.	Rehabilitation work in respect of leading in cables and rewiring 
of multi storeyed building is being done.
5.	Overhead wires are minimized by introducing 5 pair cables 
and wall Distribution Points (DPs).
6.	The junction network has been completely transferred to optical 
fibre cable links.
7.	Further improvement is being done by providing Synchronous 
Digital Hierarchy (SDH) systems connected on the ring architecture.
8.	Subscriber loop length being reduced by planning more Remote 
Subscriber Units (RSUs)/Remote Line Units(RLUs)/Digital Loop Carriers (DLCs).
9.	Wireless technologies like Cordect, Wireless in Local Loop (WLL) 
have been introduced.   Faults are monitored on daily basis by senior officers.
10.	Computerised fault reporting system is introduced, which helps in 
booking, testing and sending the faults to the concerned line staff.
11.	In addition to this, line staff is provided with pagers for easy 
communication and follow up with the testing staff for speedy clearance 
of faults.
12.	Managed leased Data Network system has been introduced to 
improve the performance of the leased circuits.
13.	MTNL has liberalized the policy to replace all telephone 
instruments older than 5 years or repaired more than 2 times.  This is 
being implemented in phases.  In the first phase, instruments more than 
eight years old are being replaced.

records.qtitle: INDIA AS CORRUPT NATION IN ASIA
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that India is said to be second most corrupt nation in Asia as per report; and

(c) if so, the facts in this regard and Government`s reaction thereto?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS. (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)

(a): Yes, Sir. The Hong Kong based Political and Economic Risk Consultancy Limited (PERCL) coordinates a team of researchers and analysts in the ASEAN countries, greater China and South Korea. It provides consultancy to some of the leading corporations and financial institutions.

(b): The PERCL invited responses from expatriate businessmen about their perception of the prevailing corruption in 12 Asian countries. India was one of the 12 countries surveyed by PERCL.



(c): The Government is fully alive to the need to root out corruption and to ensure transparency in its dealings as far as possible to build confidence among general public and also foreign investors. Government has introduced checks and balances for bringing more accountability and for ensuring efficiency in administration. The Secretary of each Department assisted by Chief Vigilance Officer has been made responsible for ensuring probity and integrity in his Department. Government has also taken several measures to ensure transparency such as setting up of 90 Facilitation Centers, as on 1.12.2002 in various Ministries/Departments/organization to provide information and assistance to the public regarding schemes and procedures of the organizations concerned. Also 71 Central Government organization have published Citizen`s Charters reflecting the commitment of the concerned Ministries, Departments or agencies to provide services within the timeframe specified. Some Ministries and Departments have also developed their own websites for promotion of e-governance. The Freedom of Information Act, 2002 has also been enacted for ensuring greater transparency, openness and accountability in the functioning of the public authorities.

records.qtitle: RESTRICTION ON TEXTILES IMPORT IN AMERICA AND EUROPEAN COUNTRIES H .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

(SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY)

(a) to (b) : Till December 31, 1994, the exports of textiles to certain developed countries including U.S.A., member countries of the European Union and Canada had been governed by bilateral textile agreements entered into between India and these countries under the aegis of the Multi-Fibre Arrangement (MFA), outside the rules of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). With effect from January 1, 1995, the quantitative restrictions (import quotas) in the bilateral agreements under the MFA, are being governed by the Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (ATC) contained in the Final Act of the Uruguay Round negotiations of the GATT. Presently, our textiles and clothing exports face restraints in U.S.A., European Union and Canada.
One of the central elements of the Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (ATC) is the four-stage process for the progressive integration of textiles and clothing products as specified in the Annex to the ATC into GATT 1994 over a ten-year transition period. The integration process has however not led to any meaningful removal of quotas by the restraining countries so far. India has raised the issue of lack of progressive liberalization in international trade in textiles bilaterally and also at the World Trade Organization. In accordance with ATC, all the textile quotas would be phased out and textile sector fully integrated into WTO by 1st January 2005.

(c) to (d): India is not maintaining any restriction on imports of textiles as no restrictions were being maintained by it under the former MFA on 31 December 1994. Further, quantitative restrictions that were maintained for balance of payment reasons have been removed on all products including textile products by 31st March 2001.

(a)to(c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 272 FOR 10.3.2003 .....
No national programme for the eradication of diseases is being implemented through the Indian Systems of Medicine.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that as per the Planning Commission Indian economy would be among one of the four major economies of the world by the year 2020;

(b) if so, the details in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that despite such economic development 13 per cent of Indian population in the country would be living Below Poverty Line at that time;

(d) if so, the facts in this regard; and

(e) whether it is a fact that the reasons for sustaining poverty in the country is that our plans are aiming at earning more and more money alone?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE

(SHRI S. B. MOOKHERJEE)

(a) & (b): The compounded effect of achieving the targeted annual GDP growth rate of

8.5 to 9 per cent over the next 20 years would result in a quadrupling of the real per capita income and almost eliminating the percentage of Indians living below the poverty line. This will raise India`s rank from around 11th today to 4th from the top in 2020 among 207 countries given in the World Development Report in terms of GDP.

(c) &(d): With the above achievement in economic development, India would attain a level of development on par with Upper Middle Income (UMI) countries. One of the key parameters of the development of UMI countries is that the population below the poverty line is 13 per cent. India Vision 2020 aims not only to reach those reference levels of UMI countries, but to surpass them in many areas including poverty.

(e): No, Sir. Indian Five Year Plans aim not only to increase incomes, but also to achieve significant improvements in social indicators.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any assessment has been made by the Government in respect of the number of workers working in the organised and unorganised sectors of the country, by the end of Ninth Five Year Plan;

(b) if so, the number thereof in the two sectors; and

(c) the estimated number of workers in the said sectors by the end of the Tenth Five Year Plan?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR

(SHRI VIJAY GOEL)
a) & b): Estimates of employment, unemployment and labour force are obtained through quinquennial labour force surveys conducted by National Sample Survey Organisation. The estimates of employment in the organised sector are obtained through Employment Market Information Programme of Directorate General of Employment & Training. As per the information available from these sources, estimated number of workers in the organised and unorganized sector in 1999-2000 were approximately 2.8 crore and 36.9 crore respectively.

(c): The report of the Special Group headed by Dr. S.P.Gupta, Member, Planning Commission, has proposed creation of 5 crore job opportunities over the 10th Plan period. Out of these, nearly 2 crore have to come from specific employment generation programmes and 3 crore from growth buoyancy.

records.qtitle: (clubbed)  RATIO BETWEEN ARMED FORCES AND CIVILIANS
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that every Jawan of each wing of armed forces has the responsibility of protecting 863 civilians;

(b) if not, the facts in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the ratio between the number of Jawans of armed forces and number of civilians is more in India as compared to that existing in other countries of the world; and

(d) if not, the facts in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI I.D.SWAMI)


(a ) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 211 FOR ANSWER ON 05.03.2003.

The Armed Forces have the responsibility of defending the country against external aggression and safeguarding its territorial integrity. The manpower strength of armed forces is governed by the overall force structure based on country`s security needs and is not determined on the basis of the civilian population of the country. There is no correlation in terms of the Armed Forces personnel strength and civilian population.
Government does not maintain data regarding ratio between the number of jawans of armed forces and number of civilians obtaining in other countries.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the plans proposed to increase the production of crude oil in the country; and

(b) the details of the percentage increase in the present production assessed after the implementation of these Plans?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)

(a) : several important steps have been taken to increase oil and gas production, which include the following :

(i) to improve the recovery factor from existing major fields by implementing Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR)/Improved Oil Recovery (IOR) schemes; in particular Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) has taken up 15 fields for this purpose at an estimated investment of Rs. 10,000 crore, which would also help in accelerating oil production from these fields.

(ii) to increase exploration efforts through the New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP). Under the three rounds of NELP, Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs) have been signed for 70 blocks.

(iii) to explore in new areas, especially in deep water and difficult frontier areas, as also explore in the deeper layers of the producing fields.

(iv) to develop faster the newly discovered fields and to step up the use of new technologies for seismic surveys, work over, stimulation operations, drilling of wells etc. in producing areas.

(b) : As a result of measures taken the crude oil production has shown an increase of about 3.3% during April-January 2003 over the corresponding period in 2001-02.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS

(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN)

(a) Yes Sir.

(b) The tax collection on import of crude oil during the first nine months of the current year (2002-2003) and corresponding period of last year are Rs. 4848 crore and Rs. 3803 crore respectively. During this period, the tax collection on import of crude oil has shown the increase of Rs. 1045 crore in 2002-2003 over 2001-2002. The marginal increase in exchange rate during said period was also a factor affecting the revenue collection from imported crude oil.
The figure are provisional.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI PON RADHAKRISHNAN )

(a)to(e): The Delhi Development Authority has reported that it has awarded the work for construction of 9000 Lower Income Group

(LIG) flats on Turn Key Basis to the pre-qualified construction agencies. These works have been awarded @ Rs.7,190/- (Rs. Seven thousand one hundred and ninety) per sqm. of the plinth area of dwelling unit in the year 2002. The average cost of construction of LIG flats during last year was Rs.5,400/- (Rs. Five thousand four hundred) per sqm. of the plinth area. The earlier cost, however, did not include certain items, which have been included in the projects awarded on Turn Key Basis and for which no extra payment is to be made. These are:

(ii) the preparation of Architectural and Structural designs, design of services and getting them approved from the Civic Agencies like MCD, DJB and DVB, maintenance of houses and services for a period of three years;

(iii) the filling of one meter depth, dual piping system for water supply, rain water harvesting, construction of electric sub-station and providing/laying High Tension and Low Tension lines and transfer of the services to the respective Civic Agencies.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE

(SHRI S.B. MOOKHERJEE)

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to the India Vision 2020 document, there is a plan to provide employment to each youth in the country;

(b) if not, the facts in this regard;

(c) the number of additional employment opportunities which would to be generated in the country by the year 2020; and

(d) the details of the different sector in the country in which people would be employed alongwith the number thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR

(SHRI VIJAY GOEL)

a) to d): According to India Vision 2020 report, India`s vision for 2020 must be founded on the premise of jobs for All and this will require a reorientation of national priorities, technology policy and government action. The report indicates that India needs to generate around 200 million additional employment opportunities over the next 20 years. It also identifies high employment potential sectors, like commercial agriculture, agro-industry and agri-business; forestation for pulp; fuel and power; retail and wholesale trade; tourism, housing and construction; IT and IT-enabled services; transport and communications; education, health and financial services.

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

(a) : Yes, Sir. Generation from the power plants located in Eastern Region is less than the installed capacity because of less demand in the region. However, 1200-1300 MW during peak period and about 2000 MW during off-peak period are being exported from Eastern Region to other regions.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) ACCUMULATION OF WATER IN THE GANGA BASIN .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is fact that additional water accumulates in Ganga river basin during the rainy season;

(b) if so, the quantum of such additional water;

(c) whether it is also a fact that large area of dry land can be made fertile by mixing this additional water in cauvery river water; and

(d) if so, the estimated area of land which can be made fertile?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)


(a) to (d) As most of the annual rainfall occurs during 90 to 100 days of monsoon season in intense spells, this results in generation of large quantity of water in the Ganga river basin during the rainy season. In 1980 the Ministry of Water Resources (then known as the Ministry of Irrigation) formulated a National Perspective Plan for Water Resources Development which envisages inter-linkages among Peninsular rivers and Himalayan rivers of transferring water from water surplus basins to water deficit areas for optimum utilisation of water resources. The Government of India established the National Water Development Agency (NWDA) in 1982 as an autonomous Society to carry out water balance and feasibility studies for the National Perspective Plan. Himayalan Rivers Development Component envisages construction of storage reservoirs on the main Ganga and the Brahmputra and their principal tributaries in India and Nepal along with inter-linking canal system to transfer surplus flows of the eastern tributaries of Ganga to the west, apart from linking of the main Brahamputra with the Ganga. As per the pre-feasibility studies carried out by NWDA about 98 Billion Cubic Meter of water is available for diversion to the water deficit areas from the tributaries of Ganga namely, Kosi, Sarda, Ghagra and Gandak as well as from main Ganga at Chunar. The Peninsular Rivers Development Component inter alia provides for inter- linking of Mahanadi-Godavari-Krishna-Pennar-Cauvery. The surplus waters available in Mahanadi and Godavari as also from the tributaries of Brahmputra via Ganga are proposed to be transferred to Cauvery basin after meeting the requirement of drought prone areas in Krishna and Pennar basins.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Co-operative sector has a crucial role in country`s development;

(b) if so, in which economic areas is the Co-operative sector playing a leading role; and

(c) the plans Government have to promote the Co-operative sector?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI AJIT SINGH)


(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 453 FOR 20/12/2002 REGARDING PROMOTION OF CO-OPERATIVE SECTOR.

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): Cooperative Sector plays leading role in the following economic areas:-

i) Disbursement of agricultural credit;
ii) Procurement and disbursement of agricultural inputs like fertilizer, seed, pesticides etc.;
iii) Marketing of consumer goods;
iv) Production and processing of sugar and oilseeds;
v) Procurement and marketing of cotton;
vi) Milk procurement and processing of milk products;
vii) Development and marketing of fisheries;
viii) Generation of employment in rural areas.

(c): Government of India has formulated the following plans to encourage the cooperative sector:-

i) Cooperative Reforms: The Central Government has enacted the new Multi State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 which aims at providing full functional autonomy and democratic management to the societies. It has also formulated a National Policy on Cooperatives in consultation with the State Governments. The Government is now pursuing with the State Governments to implement the legislative and policy reforms in cooperative sector. This will enable cooperative societies to work as self-reliant and democratically managed economic enterprises.
ii) NCDC Programme for Cooperative Development: In order to improve the income of the members of the cooperatives and for creation of various facilities, the Central Government has a scheme of assistance to NCDC programmes for cooperative development. The NCDC Amendment Act has been amended to enable it to finance more activities allied to agriculture like animal husbandry products such as milk, meat, skin, wool, and the service sector and industrial cooperatives including goods produced by the cottage and village industries. The Central Government is implementing the following schemes through NCDC for promotion of cooperatives:-

(a) Assistance for cooperative marketing, processing, storage programmes in cooperatively under/least developed States/UTs;

(b) Share capital participation in Growers Cooperative Spinning Mills;

(c) Integrated Cooperative Development Projects in selected Districts;

(d) Assistance to National Cooperative Federations;

(e) Rehabilitation of Cooperative Processing Units proposed for 10th Plan;

(f) Assistance for development of women cooperatives proposed for 10th Plan.

iii) Human Resource Development in Cooperative Sector: In order to professionalise the cooperative sector, the Central Government has initiated a number of human resource development programmes. It is implementing a Central Sector Scheme of Cooperative Education and Training through the National Cooperative Union of India (NCUI) and National Council of Cooperative Training (NCCT).
iv) Revamping of Cooperative Credit Structure: In order to revitalise and revamp the credit societies i.e. the cooperative banks, a scheme of revitalization of Cooperative Credit Structure has been finalised by the Central Government under which 60% financial assistance required would be given by the Central Government and 40% by the concerned State by way of bonds. This would be linked with cooperative reforms.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS

(SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a) to (d): The Government had constituted a Group of Ministers (GOM) on 8th March 2002 consisting of Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission, Minister of Chemicals & Fertilizers, Minister of Shipping, Minister of Commerce and Industry, Minister of Disinvestment, Minister of Agriculture and Minister of Finance. The name of Finance Minister was deleted from GOM on 24.9.2002. The GOM was constituted to examine the proposal for formulation of 7th and 8th pricing periods and to consider the Expenditure Reforms Commission (ERC)’s report on rationalizing fertilizer subsidies and give its recommendations.
The policy parameters for 7th and 8th pricing periods were approved by the competent authority on 16.5.2002, which were communicated to all urea units on 4.6.2002. The GOM has, in its meeting held on 9.10.2002, finalized its recommendations on ERC report. Formulation of new pricing policy for urea units based on GOM’s recommendations for replacing the existing Retention Price Scheme is under consideration of the Government. The proposed policy will be in the shape of Group Concession Scheme and is proposed to be introduced w.e.f 1.4.2003. The new policy will aim at greater transparency, uniformity and efficiency in subsidy disbursements to urea units and will induce urea manufacturers to take cost reduction measures on their own and be competitive.

records.qtitle: REDUCTION IN NUMBER OF WORKERS IN PSUS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn towards the decision of the public sector industries to reduce the number of workers;

(b) if so, the details of such public sector industrial establishment; and

(c) the percentage of workers going to be reduced in each establishment?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR

(SHRI ASHOK PRADHAN)

(a): The Government has introduced a Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) for the employees of Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) in order to effect rightsizing of these enterprises by rationalizing their surplus manpower for achieving better performance. This Scheme has been revised from time to time to enhance the Voluntary Retirement compensation to the employees.

(b): The names of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) which have introduced VRS upto 31.3.2001 is annexed.

(c): VRS is voluntary in nature and is based upon the option of individual employees and its acceptance by the management of the CPSEs. Such manpower rationalization is a continuous process. Hence, the percentage of employees likely to be reduced can not be qualified.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any assessment has been made by the Government in regard to the time taken in adjudication of rape cases after police investigation and the hearing in courts, in Delhi;

(b) if so, the average time taken for investigation in rape cases by police during 1999-2000 and 2000-2001; and

(c) the details of rape cases that came to light and the details of the cases referred to the court during these years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)
a. to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. ``
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION No. 410 TO BE ANSWERED ON 18.12.2002.
The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi have not made any formal study of the time taken in adjudication of rape cases. However, it normally takes the courts 1-4 years to decide such cases. The time taken for investigation for rape cases varies from case to case depending on the facts and circumstances of each case. However, the average time taken by Delhi Police to complete investigation in such cases reported during the last three years and upto 30th November, 2002 was about three months. The details regarding the number of rape cases reported to Delhi Police during the same period and their present status is indicated in the attached statement (Appendix-I).

(c) the findings thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI U.V. KRISHNAM RAJU )

(a): To check the alleged starvation deaths Central teams were sent to Rajasthan and Orissa.

(b): Shri B.B. Patnaik, Commercial Manager (CM), Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC), Head Quarter New Delhi & Dr. Ashok Kumar, Deputy Director, Storage and Research, Department of Food and Public Distribution visited Rajasthan on 22nd & 23rd October, 2002.
Shri B.B. Patnaik, CM, CWC, HQ, New Delhi, Shri K.M. Vaghela, Deputy Director, Department of Food & Public Distribution, New Delhi, Shri P.K. Mahapatra, Senior Regional Manager, and Shri Y.K. Das, Regional Manager, Food Corporation of India, Bhubaneswar, Orissa visited Orissa on 1st September, 2002.

(c): The team that visited Rajasthan has reported that the deaths in Suvans and Gangapur villages of Baran district could have been due to starvation coupled with malnutrition and lack of timely medical attention. The team observed wide-spread hardship, huger and malnutrition in remote areas due, mainly, to the failure of the Public Distribution System and the absence of employment opportunities.
As per the finding of the team that visited Orissa, the alleged deaths in Gajakupalli village of Muniguda Block in Rayagada District and Kuladera village of Keonjhar District did not appear to be due to starvation. Adequate quantity of foodgrains of fair average quality(FAQ) was found available at the fair price shops. However, it was noticed that certain poor families in utter distress were burrowing money from village money lenders by mortgaging their ration cards. The ration cards in most cases were with incomplete details.

records.qtitle: CONSTRUCTION OF SMALL HYDRO POWER PROJECTS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are contemplating to give incentives for the construction of the hydro power projects producing 50 to 75 megawatt of electricity;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and

(d) whether it is a fact that small power projects in the country are more beneficial than the big power projects?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI ANANT G. GEETE )


(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 317 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 11.12.2002 REGARDING CONSTRUCTION OF SMALL HYDRO-POWER PROJECTS.

(a) to (c) : There is no proposal to give incentives specifically for hydro power projects of 50 to 75 Megawatts capacity. However, the Ministry of Non- Conventional Energy Sources have announced various incentive schemes for the development of small hydro power projects up to 25 MW capacity. Details of these incentives are given in Annex.

(d) : The benefits and tariffs of smaller hydro-electric projects are not necessarily better than those of larger projects. The costs, benefits and tariffs are site specific for hydroelectric projects. Small hydro projects can be developed in a shorter time frame as well as at a lower capital investment and involve lesser environment and rehabilitation & resettlement problems. Small and mini hydro projects have the potential to provide energy in remote and hilly areas where extension of grid system is either not possible or is un-economical. Larger projects, particularly multi purpose projects provide tremendous benefits in the nature of power, irrigation, drinking water, flood control, and are also advantageous in terms of economy of scale besides providing peaking power even in the lean season, and opening up other economic opportunities in the areas of their location.

records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that power shortage in peak as well as general hours in the country can be brought to negligible level by bringing the losses in its distribution and transmission system at the international level;

(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that the power distribution and transmission losses at international level have been assessed at six per cent only; and

(c) if not, the percentage thereof and what is the Government`s time- bound scheme for bringing the above said power losses to the international level?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI ANANT G. GEETE )


(a) to (c) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 313 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 11.12.2002 REGARDING DISTRIBUTION AND TRANSMISSION LOSSES.


(a) : Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c) : The transmission and distribution (T&D) losses in the developed countries of the world are in the range of 6-11%. The level of T&D losses in the country is around 31% and is higher than that of the developed countries of the world. While the losses in Extra High Voltage network (EHV) about 4-5%, bulk of the losses occur in the sub-transmission and distribution systems.
The reasons for high T&D losses in the country are on account of:
i. weak and inadequate sub-transmission and distribution system due to low priority being given to these works ii. large scale rural electrification programme undertaken in the country resulting in long lines and extension of distribution network without strengthening the back-up transmission and sub-transmission system iii. too many transformation stages resulting in higher component of transformation losses iv. improper load management resulting in over loading of system v. low power factor due to pumping load in rural areas, and air conditioners, coolers and industrial loads in urban areas and inadequate reactive compensation at the load points vi. low quality of construction and inadequate maintenance of equipment vii. unmetered supply to agricultural pumps and small domestic connections to weaker sections of the society in some states viii. pilferage and theft of energy. In order to achieve commercial viability, Ministry of Power has formulated a six level intervention strategy that encompasses initiatives at national level, state level, SEB/Utility level, distribution circle level, feeder level and the consumer level. This six level intervention strategy will focus on accountability, deliverability and performance at all levels to rejuvenate the distribution sector, where the maximum interface with the ultimate customers exists, the highest value addition occurs, and eighty percent of total T&D losses including nearly all the commercial losses take place.
To give a strong impetus to the process of reforms, the Ministry of Power organized a Conference of Chief Ministers/ Power Ministers on Power Sector Reforms on 3rd March 2001. It was emphasised inter alia that commercial viability has to be achieved in distribution in 2-3 years through any or all of the following
- Creating profit centres with full accountability - Handing over local distribution to Panchayats/Local Bodies/Franchisees/ Users Association, wherever necessary - Privatisation of distribution
25 States have signed Memorandum of Understanding for undertaking reforms and restructuring in a time bound manner and linking the support of Government of India to achievement of predetermined milestones. To bring about commitment towards distribution reforms, State Electricity Boards/Utilities have been asked to sign a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) with Ministry of Power as a pre-requisite for release of Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (APDRP) funds. Till now 18 States have signed the MoA. A number of States have enacted anti-electricity theft legislation.
To reduce the transmission and distribution losses in a phased manner, the Government of India has launched the APDRP in February 2000. The APDRP includes upgradation of sub-transmission and distribution network, energy audit activities and metering in a phased manner.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that Government consider it necessary to increase the number of Judges in view of the increasing population of the country;

(b) if so, the estimated number of Judges required in the country at present; and

(c) the total number of Judges in position at present?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI K. JANA KRISHNAMURTHI)

(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT WITH REGARD TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 277 TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, THE 9th DECEMBER, 2002

(a) The Judge strength in Supreme Court is as per the Constitution of India. The Judge strength in the High Courts is reviewed once in three years as per prescribed norms on the basis of figures of institution, disposal and pendency of cases in each High Court. As regards District and Subordinate Courts, the Judge strength is worked out by State Governments in consultation with the concerned High Courts. However, the Supreme Court, in its Judgment of 21st March, 2002, in All India Judges` Association & Ors Vs. Union of India & Ors, has directed that an increase in the judge strength from the existing ratio of 10.5 or 13 per 10 lakh people to 50 judges per 10 lakh people should be effected and implemented within a period of five years in a phased manner to be determined and directed by the Union Ministry of Law. The Central Government has filed applications before the Supreme Court, seeking modification of its directions for increase in Judge strength on the basis of population in respect of Union territories and permit the Union Government to determine the appropriate judge strength based on the relevant factors including pendency of cases. The matter is sub judice.

(b) An estimated 51,351 Judges would be required to be in position on the basis of population as per Census 2001.

(c) As per available information, the total number of Judges in position at present is 15,095.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that separate prices have been fixed by Government and the State Governments for purchasing sugarcane;

(b) if so, the prices fixed by the Central Government and the sugarcane growing States at present; and

(c) the reasons for the variations in the said prices?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI SHARAD YADAV )

(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE STARRED QUESTION NO.258 DUE FOR ANSWER ON 05-12-2002 IN THE RAJYA SABHA.
Under the provisions of the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, the power to fix the sugarcane prices vests with the Central Government. The Central Government, in terms of clause 3 of the said Order, fixes the Statutory Minimum Price (SMP) of sugarcane payable by sugar factories for each sugar season (October - September). The Central Government has fixed the SMP for 2002-03 sugar season at Rs.64.50 per quintal linked to a basic recovery level of

8.5%, subject to premium of 76 paise for every 0.1% point increase in recovery above that level.

2. State Governments have no power to fix prices of sugarcane.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )


(a) : Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c) : The rate at which electricity was purchased, the quantum of electricity purchased and the quantum of electricity generated by different State Electricity Boards

(SEBs)/Electricity Departments (EDs) in the country during 1998-99 are given in Annexure. Data for the year 2002-03 is not yet available and will be compiled after the year is over.

records.qtitle: LOANS OF FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO DABHOL POWER PROJECT .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Dabhol Power Project was started with the loans advanced by the financial institutions of the country;

(b) if so, the total amount spent so far by these institutions on the maintenance and running, along with the cost of construction of the project; and

(c) the percentage of the said amount of the total expenditure made thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )


(a) : The Dabhol power project was constructed using a mix of equity and loan funds. The equity was brought in by the sponsors viz. Enron, General Electric, Bechtel and the Maharashtra Power Development Corporation Limited (MPDCL). The loan funds were advanced by a consortium of off-shore banks and Indian Financial Institutions/Banks (IFIs).


(b) & (c) : The exposure of the IFIs as on date aggregates Rs.6551 crores (Rs.3292 crores by way of fund based assistance and Rs.3259 crores by way of guarantees). Phase-I of the project had commenced commercial operations in May, 1999, while Phase- II was under construction. Phase-II of the project was complete to the extent of around 92% as on 31.5.2001. Due to certain commercial disputes between Dabhol Power Company (DPC) and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB), MSEB stopped taking power from Phase-I from 29th May, 2001 and construction of Phase-II was suspended due to termination of construction contracts on 17th June, 2001. From June, 2001 onwards, the expenditure on asset preservation, security and payment of insurance premia, was being incurred out of funds available in the accounts of DPC. From September, 2002 onwards, after depletion of funds in the accounts of DPC, the principal IFIs have been incurring this expenditure. As on December 2, 2002, IFIs have incurred an expenditure of Rs.7.26 crores for asset preservation, security and insurance premia.

records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that terrorist incidents have been taking place in the various States of the country for the last three years;

(b) if so, the names of the States in which terrorist incidents, which are cross-border instigated, occurred between January, 1999 to October, 2002; and

(c) the dates on which these incidents occurred and the number of civilians and the security forces killed due to these incidents?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI CH.VIDYASAGAR RAO)

(a): Yes Sir.

(b): Pakistan sponsored terrorist activities have taken place mainly in J&K. However, some isolated incidents have also occurred in Gujarat, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.

(c): Since `Public order` and `Police` are State subjects, the Central Government as such does not maintain such statistics. However, as per available information, 3294 civilians and 1661 security forces were killed in J&K alone during 1999 to 2002 (October).
``
