records.qtitle: (clubbed) INDIA S PETITION AGAINST HUGE SUBSIDY PROVIDED BY USA H
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
:

(a) whether it is a fact that India has filed petition in the WTO against the huge subsidy being provided by the USA;

(b) if so, the details thereof and the issues objected to by India; and

(c) by when a decision in the matter is likely to be taken by the WTO?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )


(a) to (c): No, Sir. However, Brazil has sought consultations with the USA regarding subsidies being given by it to upland cotton. In accordance with the provisions of the Understanding on Rules and Procedures Governing the Settlement of Disputes (DSU) of the World Trade Organization (WTO), India has notified the consulting countries of it`s desire to be joined in the consultations as a third party. Further action will be taken in accordance with the provisions of the DSU.
Besides, in the context of the on-going negotiations in agriculture under the Doha Work Programme of the WTO, India has proposed substantial reductions in all trade-distorting domestic support and the elimination of export subsidies by developed countries. The negotiations are scheduled to conclude by 1 January 2005.

records.qtitle: EMPLOYMENT OF RETIRED RAILWAY EMPLOYEES IN COMMERCIAL INSTITUTIONS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of retired railway employees are employed with commercial institutions, contracting with the Railways ;

(b) if, so the details thereof and the posts held by each of them formerly ;

(c) whether it is also a fact that they give undue benefits to the private enterprises because of their earlier knowledge and acquaintance and affect the working of the Railways ; and

(d) if so, Government’s reaction thereto and the steps taken to check the same? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI BANDARU DATTATRAYA)


(a) to (d) : Only Group ‘A’ officers are required to seek prior permission from the Government for getting employed with a private firm during the first two years following retirement and Group ‘B’ officers are required to inform the Railway in such cases. Apart from this, there is no restriction or condition in the retired Railway employees accepting commercial employment with firms including those contracting with the Railways. Therefore, it is not possible to maintain information regarding all such employees employed with commercial institutions. In view of this, it is also not possible to have a feed back on such retired employees giving undue benefit, if any, to others.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a) to (c): Government is in the process of formulation of new pricing policy for urea units keeping in view the recommendations of Expenditure Reforms Commission for replacing the existing Retention Price Scheme. records.qtitle: GROWTH RATE FOR TENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN .
records.name: Kapil Sibal

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE

(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) to (c) : The Approach Paper to the Tenth Five Year Plan as approved by the National Development Council (NDC) envisages an annual average growth target of 8 per cent for the nation. A commitment has also been made in the Approach Paper to break up the growth target State-wise, taking into account the potentials and constraints of each State, since it is not necessary for each State to grow individually at an annual average rate of 8 per cent in order to make the national growth target achievable. The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07), which would contain the State-wise growth target, is yet to be approved by the National Development Council.

(a) whether it is a fact that as per reports of National Human Rights Commission, 666 deaths have taken place in police custody during the last six months in various States of the country; b. if not, the details of facts in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that most of such deaths have occurred in Uttar Pradesh and if so, the number thereof; and

(d) whether Government have prepared any national scheme for police reforms in the light of above mentioned facts?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( SHRI CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)

(a) & (b): As reported by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), the number of deaths in police custody during the last six months from 1.5.2002 to 31.10.2002 is 94. The details are given in Annexure.

(c): 13 deaths have been reported from the State of Maharashtra which is the highest number of deaths. 9 deaths have been reported from the State of Uttar Pradesh during the last six months.

(d): The NHRC has directed the concerned authorities to take necessary steps to curb the occurrence of custodial deaths. Besides, the Police are being sensitized on human rights through appropriate training programmes both at the induction level as well as mid-career stage. ``

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE & COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI GINGEE. N. RAMACHANDRAN)

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government’s attention has been drawn towards the fact that according to the Planning Commission the number of non-school going children in the age group of 6 to 14 years is 80 million;

(b) if so, whether Government confirms this figure;

(c) if not, the assessment of Government in this regard; and

(d) the number of schools or classes required to be introduced in the country for such children?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(PROF. RITA VERMA)

(a) to (d): According to the Draft Approach Paper to the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007) circulated by the Planning Commission in May, 2001, it was stated that out of approximately 200 million children in the age group 6-14 years only 120 million are in schools. However, as per the latest figures available in the Selected Educational Statistics, brought out by this Ministry for the year 2000-01, out of the projected child population of 19.2 crores in the age-group 6- 14, 15.7 crores have been enrolled in schools. According to an estimate prepared by the Government under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), there would be a requirement of 11.35 lakh additional class rooms in the next 10 years for 100% enrolment (allowing for a class room for every teacher in primary/upper primary schools and a room for the Head Master in upper primary school).

(a)to(c): The Government has approved foreign investment of Rs. 1532 crores during the period March, 1998 to July 2002 in the various sectors of food processing. records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have declared a long term policy for chemical fertilizers, which would be brought into force from the next financial year;

(b) if not, the facts in this regard; and

(c) the salient features of this policy as a result of which the interest of the consumers, manufacturers and traders is likely to be protected to greater extent?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS

(SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a) to (c): The new pricing policy for urea units, being formulated keeping in view the recommendations of Expenditure Reforms Commission, is proposed to be introduced w.e.f.

1.4.2003 and will replace the existing Retention Price Scheme. The new policy will be in the shape of Group Concession Scheme, which will aim at greater transparency, uniformity and efficiency in subsidy disbursements to urea manufacturing units and will induce urea manufacturers to take cost reduction measures on their own and be competitive. The farmers would continue to get urea at statutorily notified Maximum Retail Price.

records.qtitle: TH SESSION OF INDIAN LABOUR CONFERENCE .

MINISTER OF LABOUR (SHRI SAHIB SINGH VERMA)

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.57 FOR 21.11.2002 REGARDING BY SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND SHRI RAM JETHMALANI REGARDING 38TH SESSION OF INDIAN LABOUR CONFERENCE

(b) & (c): During the discussions the representatives of social partners expressed their views which were divergent in respect of many recommendations. (a) to (c) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.32 FOR ANSWER ON 20.11.2002 ASKED BY S/SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND RAM JETHMALANI REGARDING INVESTMENT IN NALCO.

(a) to (b) Yes, Sir. NALCO is a public sector industrial undertaking. It was established on 7th January in the year 1981 and commissioned in 1987. To begin with, the total capital invested by Government of India in NALCO was Rs.1288.62 crore. Subsequently, between 1991 and 1994 the Govt. of India disinvested 12.85% of paid up capital and during the year 1999 the company reduced its capital by 50 per cent. Thus, as on 31st March, 2002, the paid up equity capital of NALCO was Rs. 644.31 crore.

(c) The Government has received an amount of Rs.739.82 crore as dividend upto March, 2002 from NALCO. In addition, dividend amounting to Rs.224.61 crore for the financial year 2001-02 has become payable to the Government.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) GUIDELINES FOR APPROVAL OF FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN PRINT MEDIA .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have fixed any guidelines for the approval of foreign investment in print media; and

(b) if so, the details of such guidelines and whether the proposal of foreign investment would be considered in the light of these guidelines or the procedure of taking decision on case to case basis would be followed?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING

(SMT. SUSHMA SWARAJ)

(a) & (b): The Government have issued guidelines for approval of proposals for publication of Indian editions of foreign scientific, technical and speciality magazines/periodicals/journals and for foreign investment upto 74% in Indian entities publishing scientific, technical and speciality magazines/periodicals/journals. A copy of the guidelines is at Annexure. Guidelines regarding FDI in News and Current Affairs have not been issued so far.

ANNEXURE TO PART b) OF THE RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.86 FOR ANSWER ON 18.11.2002 GUIDELINES FOR:

(i)	PUBLICATION OF INDIAN EDITIONS OF FOREIGN TECHNICAL/SCIENTIFIC/SPECIALITY 
MAGAZINES/JOURNALS/PERIODICALS; AND 
(ii)	FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN INDIAN ENTITIES PUBLISHING 
SCIENTIFIC/TECHNICAL/SPECIALITY MAGAZINES/JOURNALS/PERIODICALS


PREAMBLE



	The Union Government has decided to allow: 

(i)	publication of Indian editions of foreign scientific, technical and speciality 
magazines/periodicals/journals; and  

(ii)	foreign investment upto 74% in Indian entities publishing scientific/technical 
and speciality magazines/periodicals/journals. 


1.	Application


(i)	An application shall be made to the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
in the prescribed format to determine the nature of contents of the publication 

(ii)	Application fee of Rs. 5000/- (Rupees Five thousand only) shall have to be 
deposited through a Demand Draft in favour of the Pay & Accounts Officer, 
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, payable at New Delhi.


2.	Processing


(i)	The application shall be processed by the Ministry of I&B, after due inter-
Ministerial consultations, to decide whether the proposed publication is 
covered under the category of scientific, technical or speciality 
magazine/periodical/journal. Representatives of the concerned 
Ministries/specialist bodies and language experts, as found necessary will be 
associated in this task. In appropriate cases, the Ministry of I&B will issue:


a)	An approval, subject to compliance with the provisions of the 
Press and Registration of Books Act and Rules made thereunder 
for publication of the foreign journal; or


b)        A No Objection Certificate (NOC) for foreign investment, a copy 
of which would be sent to RNI/SIA/RBI and the applicant. 

(ii)	 Determination of category assigned to the publication(s) is liable for review 
by the Ministry of I&B if the contents of the publication(s) undergo change at 
a later date.  

(iii)	           a)	In cases where both FDI and FII investment is envisaged, the 
applicant may approach the FIPB/RBI for clearance after obtaining the No 
Objection Certificate from the Ministry of I&B.


b)	In cases involving only portfolio investment, the applicant may 
approach the Reserve Bank of India, for further clearance, if any, 
after obtaining the No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of 
I&B.


c)	The Ministry of I&B will keep the Secretariat for Industrial 
Assistance and the Reserve Bank of India informed of the FDI 
projected by the Company and the balance permissible foreign 
investment on the portfolio investment route, while communicating 
the No Objection. 


3.	 Title of the Publication


Title verification shall continue to be done by the Press Registrar as per 
existing procedure.


4.	Foreign Investment 
(i)	Total foreign investment upto 74% may be allowed. Guidelines of the 
Ministry of Finance on FDI and portfolio investment would apply subject to 
the overall ceiling of 74% mentioned above. 
(ii)	All cases involving Foreign Investment shall be handled by the prescribed 
agencies, viz. FDI on the government approval route through the mechanism 
of the FIPB and portfolio investment by the RBI.

records.qtitle: (clubbed)   TIME BOUND PROGRAMME FOR DISINVESTMENT OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that any time-bound programme for disinvestment of industries under Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises has been fixed;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether Government have laid down any criteria for priority disinvestment; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION AND MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

(a) & (b) Disinvestment is an ongoing process and individual public sector undertakings are taken up for disinvestment on the basis of reports of the Disinvestment Commission and the proposals of the Ministry of Disinvestment after inter-ministerial consultations. So far 12 PSUs and 3 hotels of Hotel Corporation of India Ltd. (HCI) and 100% Government equity in 18 hotel properties and one hotel (on lease-cum management contract) of ITDC have been disinvested through the process of strategic sale. 54 cases are at various stages of processing for disinvestment by this Ministry. Of these 13 PSUs and 2 hotels of HCI and 4 hotels of ITDC are expected to be finalised in the current year.

(c) & (d) All PSUs classified as non-strategic can be taken up for disinvestment to a level of 26% or lower, if necessary, as decided on a case by case. The priority for disinvestment is determined keeping in view market conditions, the nature of disinvestment and any other factor, which is likely to impact the realisable value.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have identified heavy industries which have been selected for disinvestment;

(b) if so, the names of the industries for which decision has been taken to make disinvestment and when; and

(c) the basis of the priority fixed for disinvestment?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION AND MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY

(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

(a) As per the policy of disinvestment, the Government has classified Public Sector Undertakings as `Strategic` and `Non-Strategic`. The following industries have been identified as `Strategic` industries.

i) Arms & Ammunitions and the allied items of defence equipment, defence air-crafts and warships;
ii) Atomic Energy (except in the areas related to the generation of nuclear power and applications of radiation and radio-isotopes to agriculture medicine and non-strategic industries);
iii) Railway Transport.

All other Public Sector Undertakings are considered as `Non-Strategic` for which disinvestment of Government equity to a level of 26% or lower, if necessary, is decided on a case by case basis.

(b) Disinvestment is an ongoing process and individual public sector undertakings are taken up for disinvestment on the basis of reports of the Disinvestment Commission and the proposals of the Ministry of Disinvestment after inter-ministerial consultations on a case by case basis. So far 12 PSUs and 3 hotels of Hotel Corporation of India Ltd. (HCI) and 100% Government equity in 18 hotel properties and one hotel (on lease-cum-management contract) of ITDC have been disinvested through the process of strategic sale. 54 cases are at various stages of processing for disinvestment in this Ministry, and the same are given in Annexure I.

(c) The priority for disinvestment is determined keeping in view market conditions, the nature of disinvestment and any other factor, which is likely to impact the realisable value.

records.name: Ram Jethmalani

(b) if so, the names of those PSUs;

(c) the details of the assessment made with regard to their movable and immovable properties; and

(d) the amount collected as a result of their disinvestment?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DISINVESTMENT AND MINISTER OF DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION

(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

(a) Disinvestment in public sector undertakings is being undertaken as per the declared policy of bringing down Government shareholding in non-strategic public sector undertakings to 26% or lower. The PSUs are selected based on this criteria and not on whether the company is in production or not. Of the 32 PSUs on which the Ministry of Disinvestment is working at present, all are producing and providing services.

(b) to (d) Bharat Leather Corporation Limited is one PSU in which production has stopped. The asset valuation of a company under disinvestment is undertaken through an independent Asset Valuer before inviting financial bids. Accordingly, the asset valuation of Bharat Leather Corporation Limited would be undertaken at the appropriate stage.

records.qtitle: IMPACT OF US FARM SUBSIDY ON INDIAN FARMERS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news item published in The Business Lines on 28th June, 2002 under caption, `U.S. release $ 100m for farm exports`;

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that 100 million dollars are being given by U.S.A. as subsidy to promote export of foodgrains; and

(c) if so, the estimates with regard to its likely impact on Indian farmers?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)


(a)to(c): Yes Sir. In the US Farm Security and Rural Investment Act, 2002, there is a provision of US $ 100 million for the year 2002, under `Market Access Programme`. Reports are indicating that the subsidies indicated in the US Farm Security and Rural Investment Act, 2002, will have a price depressing effect on the world markets. This will have a negative effect for developing countries as well.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI SURESH PRABHU )


(a) to (c) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 341 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 07.08.2002 REGARDING ELECTRICITY GENERATED BY VARIOUS FUELS.

(a) to (c) : Electricity in India is generated through various sources, such as, coal, hydro, gas, diesel, nuclear etc. Electricity is also available through renewable sources like wind, solar photovoltaic, biomass, energy from wastes, etc. 
		As on 31.03.2002, the installed capacity from various sources was as 
follows: -


Type of Fuel	Installed Capacity (MW)

		The per unit cost of generation of power from various sources (2000-
01) was as follows :

location etc.)	1200 - 2000

The Government has undertaken a number of measures for accelerating the pace of hydropower development in the country with the ultimate objective of fully developing the feasible hydro potential in the country, as this is a renewable source of energy with no fuel cost. As can be seen from the above table, the cost of generation from coal is quite low. The cost of generation from nuclear sources is expected to come down over time to international levels as the plans for having 20,000 MW of nuclear capacity by 2020 are implemented. Gas and Naphtha are relatively costly options.
The following are the salient features of the comprehensive strategy evolved for the full development of the hydro potential in the country: -
? Central Electricity Authority has completed a ranking study of all the identified hydro potential sites in the major river basins of the country. This ranking study forms the basis for prioritizing the development of the hydro sites.
? Active role of the states in selection, prioritization and monitoring of execution of projects specially in view of the critical responsibility of the States in land acquisition and rehabilitation and resettlement.
? In pursuance of the ranking study an International Round Table is being organized where developers, countries with strength in hydro power development, multi lateral agencies and financial institutions would be invited with the objective of identifying projects for the preparation of DPRs and subsequent development.
? A Committee has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Shri Harish Salve, Solicitor General of India to suggest ways and means for increasing transparency and streamlining contract management in hydro projects. This is aimed at reduction in time and cost over runs associated with hydro projects and in turn to lower capital costs.
? A Three Stage clearance process for new hydro projects has been introduced. This facilitates thorough preparation of DPRs so as to minimize possibilities of geological surprises with land acquisition and proper development of infrastructure including roads and bridges being done in parallel after establishment of feasibility and commercial viability of a project. Development of necessary infrastructure before award of major contract packages is expected to result in reduction of the gestation period of hydro projects and consequently lower costs.
? An effective system of review of catchment area treatment as well as compensatory afforestation has been introduced. In addition, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for compensatory afforestation has been planned which would create a land bank from which credits could be taken for large power projects. These measures are designed to take care of environmental concerns relating to large hydro projects.

records.qtitle: EXPENDITURE ON T D OF POWER .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made an assessment of expenditure incurred on transmission and distribution of power;

(b) if so, the amount being spent per unit by electricity boards in each State on transmission and distribution of electricity;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the said amount of expenditure is much more than the amount of expenditure incurred at international level; and

(d) if so, the average expenditure at international level?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

(a) & (b) : According to the Annual Report of the Planning Commission on the Working of State Electricity Boards (SEBs) and Electricity Departments (EDs) (June, 2002), the outlay on transmission & distribution in various States during the period 1992-93 to 2000-2001 is enclosed as Annex. The per unit cost of transmission varies according to the location of the generating stations, quantum of power flows apart from the investments made.

(c) & (d) : It may not be appropriate to compare the investment made on transmission and distribution in our country with that of other countries. The transmission & distribution system in our country is still at the developmental stage wherein large areas are still required to be electrified and hence huge investment is required in this sector.
As per the report of Rajyadhaksha Committee on Power (1980), the thumb rule for investment ratio of expenditure on generation, Transmission & Distribution and rural electrification should be 4:2:1:1 between generation on one hand and the transmission and distribution (including rural electrification) on the other. The actual ratio of investment on generation and Transmission & Distribution (including RE) has been less than 1:1 except during the first plan period as adequate resources were not available for investment on system improvement schemes.

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN SETHI)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) to (d) The Central Ground Water Board, under the Ministry of Water Resources had implemented demonstrative rain water harvesting and recharge projects in the country, under its Central Sector Scheme for Study of Recharge to Ground Water on “pilot basis” during IX Five Year Plan, at a cost of Rs.23.48 crore. Under this schemes, a total number of 174 projects were approved for implementation in 27 States/Union Territories. The Government has prepared a Central Sector Scheme of Recharge to Ground Water, at an estimated cost of Rs.150 crore for inclusion in the X Five Year Plan. The scheme is at consultation stage. As such, no funds have so far been allocated to the States under the scheme during the current financial year.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is ample rain water available in the country;

(b) if so, whether rain water harvesting reserves have been set up in each State of the country; and

(c) if so, the storage capacity of each of the rain water harvesting reserves set up in each of such States in the country ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN SETHI)

(a) India receives an average annual precipitation of 4000 Billion Cubic Metre (BCM) which includes rainfall and snow. Out of this, 3,000 BCM occurs during monsoon. The average annual flow in various rivers of the country is assessed at 1869 BCM. Out of this, utilizable flow by conventional methods is estimated at 690 BCM. In addition about 200-250 BCM can be utilised through inter- basin water transfer from the surplus river basins to the deficit water basins.

(b) & (c) No, Sir. Water being a State subject, it is for the concerned State Government to take steps in this regard. The Ministry of Water Resources has, however, circulated a Manual on Artificial Recharge of Ground Water to the States/Union Territories to enable them to formulate area specific artificial recharge scheme to check the declining trend in ground water levels. State-wise estimated availability of rain water for ground water recharge, as assessed by the Central Ground Water Board, is given in the enclosed Statement.

records.qtitle: DECLINE IN BASIC AMENITIES IN METROPOLITAN CITIES
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the basic amenities are declining day by day in metropolitan cities due to continuous increase in the population;

(b) if so, whether any assessment has been made regarding the lack of drinking water, sanitation,schools, electricity and transportation in these cities; and

(c) if so, the details in this regard, city-wise?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI ANANTH KUMAR )


(a),(b)&(c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.

.PA STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.204 FOR 29.7.2002 REGARDING DECLINE IN BASIC AMENITIES IN METROPOLITAN CITIES.
.SP2 The number of metropolitan cities and urban agglomerations has increased from 23 in 1991 to 35 in 2001. The population in these cities has also grown from 70,996,726 in 1991 to 107,813,906 in 2001 as per the Census of India. Consequently, there has been pressure on the basic amenities in the Metropolitan Cities. The development of urban infrastructure by the cities have not kept pace with the growth in population. As per Entry Nos. 6 & 17 of List II - State List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, public health, sanitation & water supply are the responsibility of the State Governments. Central Government, however, supplements the efforts of State Governments through policy formulation, technical guidance & Central assistance through the Centrally Sponsored Schemes for urban infrastructure development in the areas of water supply, sanitation & urban transportation. The Central Government also assists State Governments in development of urban infrastructure with the support of multinational/bilateral agencies. As per study conducted by the Central Pollution Control Board in 1994-95, the 23 metro cities (as per 1991 census) had per capita drinking water supply availability ranging from 74 Litres Per Capita Per Day (lpcd) in Madurai upto 341 lpcd in Delhi. Within a City, there has been variation in the availability of drinking water from area to area. City-wise details are at Annexure. National Institute of Urban Affairs has been entrusted with a study to assess the status of water supply, sanitation and solid waste management in 300 cities & towns, including the metropolitan cities. The report is yet to be finalized.

(c) how much amount has already been spent out of the estimated amount till March, 2002; and

(d) the number of projects, out of them which have been discontinued without completion of job?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL )


(a)to(d): The Centrally sponsored scheme for Infrastructure Development in Mega Cities was launched in 1993-94. The scheme is applicable to five mega cities namely Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad and Bangalore. As per available information 418 projects at an estimated cost of Rs.3648.25 crore have been sanctioned by the respective State level Sanctioning Committee. An expenditure of Rs. 2024.70 crore has been incurred upto 31.3.2002 in completion/implementation of the projects.
As per available information, 23 projects/schemes were dropped during the 9th Five Year Plan.

records.qtitle: LOANS TO SMALL AND MARGINAL FARMERS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) the percentage of small and marginal farmers among the total number of farmers in the country;

(b) whether it is a fact that this percentage is about 76;

(c) whether it is a fact that small and marginal section of farmers are being provided only 27 percent of total loans being disbursed for agriculture; and

(d) if not, the annual percentage of loans extended to this section of farmers during the last three years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI AJIT SINGH)


(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 181 FOR 26/07/2002 REGARDING LOANS TO SMALL AND MARGINAL FARMERS.

(a)&(b): As per Agricultural Census, 1990-91, the marginal and small holdings constituted 78.2 per cent (59.4% marginal and 18.8 per cent small), of the total operational holdings in the country. However, these two categories accounted for about 32% of the total operated area.

(c)&(d): As per information available from the Reserve Bank of India, out of the total institutional credit taken for agricultural purposes from various sources, the small and marginal farmers were extended credit to the tune of 48.2 per cent during 1995-96, 48.7 per cent during 1996-97 and 47.25 per cent during 1997-98, respectively.

records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the average annual rate of said expansion during the last three years;

(c) the number of units in food processing industry functioning in the country at the end of March, 2002; and

(d) what was the total capital investment in said units?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

( SHRI N.T. SHANMUGAM )

(a) & (b): As per the recent study conducted by the national Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), food processing industries have been growing at 5.8% per annum during the 9th Plan Period.

(c) & (d): Since food processing industries are both in the organised and unorganized sectors, information on the number of units and their capital investment is not maintained centrally. However, as per the Report of Annual Survey of Industries for 1998 – 99, the number of factories in the Food Beverage sector was 23,831 and the invested capital thereon was about Rs. 52,630.00 Crores.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Central Vigilance Commission has identified hundred of departments of various Ministries as areas of corruption;

(b) if so, the names of such departments;

(c) whether Government have so far taken any effective steps to make the functioning of these departments corruption-free; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
(THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE. (SMT.VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a)&(b): The Central Vigilance Commission(CVC) has not identified any Department of the Government as area of corruption.

(c)&(d): The Government is fully alive to ensure the corruption free functioning of the Government Departments. Polices in this regard have been formulated and constantly monitored for their effective implementation. Necessary modifications are also carried out from time to time in order to make them more effective and responsive to the needs of a changing environment. The Government has also set up Information and Facilitation Counters (IFCs) in various Ministries/Departments to provide information regarding procedures and schemes of concerned organizations to ensure greater transparency and for eliminating corruption. Besides, the Secretary of the concerned Department, assisted by Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO), is made responsible for ensuring probity and integrity in that Department.

records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Bill related to Right to Information to common citizen is pending for a long time;

(b) if so, when the decision was taken to pass the Bill; and

(c) whether Government would bring the said Bill for consideration and passing in the House during the present Monsoon session?
records.ans_text:
(THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE. (SMT.VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a), (b) & (c): With a view to introducing greater transparency and openness in the functioning of Government and public bodies, Government had introduced the `Freedom of Information Bill, 2000`in the Lok Sabha on 25th July,2000. The Bill, as introduced in the Lok Sabha and pending therein, was referred to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs for examination and report thereon. The Standing Committee presented its Report to both the Houses of Parliament on 25th July, 2001. The recommendations made by the Committee in its Report have been examined and efforts are being made to bring up the Bill for consideration of the House at the earliest.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made any assessment of the production-rate of foodgrains in all the States;

(b) if so, the details of production-rate of wheat, paddy, sugarcane and cotton in each State;

(c) whether Government have identified the States where possibilities to increase the production-rate exist; and

(d) if so, which are those States and to what extent the production-rate can be increased there?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)


(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): The State-wise yield rates of wheat, paddy, sugarcane and cotton for the years 1998-99, 1999-2000 and 2000-01 are given in the Annexures I to IV respectively.

(c): Yes, Sir.

(d): Productivity depends on several factors like level of technology, timely application of inputs, farm management skills etc. Given the existing level of technology, according to the assessment of Indian Council of Agricultural Research, there is possibility of increasing the yield rate of wheat in the states of West Bengal, Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh. In case of paddy, the average yield can be increased in the states of West Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the rate of human resource development in the States has been distinct in the country during nineties;

(b) if so, what has been the annual rate of human resource development in each of the States during nineties;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the rate of human resource development in those States has been more where per capita income is more; and

(d) if not, the facts in this regard? ANSWER THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES,
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE

(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) & (b): The National Human Development Report (NHDR) – 2001 prepared by the Planning Commission and released by the Prime Minister on April 23rd, 2002 has presented a Human Development Index (HDI) for all States and UTs for the early eighties (using data for 1981 to 1983) and the early nineties (using data for 1991 to 1993-94) and only for major States for 2001 due to the non-availability, so far, of the required data for all States/UTs from the Census 2001. The Report does not separately estimate yearly rates of growth in human development.

(c) & (d): From the analysis it turns out that for the economically better off States, as well as for the poor States, attainments on HDI and income levels show a direct correspondence. In other words, the poor States are also the States with relatively poor performance on HDI. Similarly, the economically better-off States are also the ones with relatively better performance on the HDI. However, the relation between the HDI and the level of development does not show any correspondence among the middle-income States.

records.qtitle: SETTING UP OF FAST TRACK COURTS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government had taken a decision to set-up Fast Track Courts throughout the country for early disposal of the pending cases in the courts;

(b) if so, the total number thereof and by when these courts were to be set-up;

(c) the total funds allocated for implementation of the said scheme; and

(d) the amount spent, out of the total allocated funds, till December, 2001?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW,JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY)
a): Yes, Sir.
b) The Eleventh Finance Commission had recommended that 1734 Fast Track Courts be established in the country. Out of these, 1074 Fast Track Courts have already been established, of which 627 Fast Track Courts have started functioning.

(c): The total funds allocated for the implementation of Fast Track Courts is Rs. 502.90 crore.

(d): An amount of Rs. 168 crore had been released by the Ministry of Finance to the State Governments under this scheme, till December, 2001.

records.qtitle: INCREASING PAY OF PERSONS ENGAGED IN THE MANAGERIAL WORK IN COMPANIES.
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the limit of increasing monthly pay of persons engaged in the managerial work of companies has been increased by Government;

(b) if so, what has been the limit so far and the increased limit now; and

(c) the reasons for taking this decision by Government.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE & COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY)


(a) for the companies having no profits or inadequate profits, limits under schedule XIII to the Companies Act, 1956 have been revised.

(b) Based on effective capital of the company, earlier limits were Rs.75,000/- to Rs.2,00,000/- per month. These have now been revised to Rs.1,50,000/- to Rs.4,00,000/- per month and linked to good corporate governance practices.

(c) The decision was taken as a liberalizing measure and to encourage good corporate governance. The inflation that has taken place since the previous limits were fixed, was also taken into consideration.

records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have decided to started computer education system in 60,000 schools under modified Students Computer Programme, to provide computer education in the country ;

(b) if so in which States, these 60,000 schools have been selected, giving the State wise number thereof; and

(c) the average number of students who would get computer education annually in these schools?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(PROF. RITA VERMA)


(a) to (c): The Department of Secondary and Higher Education has launched a revised Computer Literacy and Studies in Schools (CLASS) scheme to impart computer education to the students of Government and Government aided schools. Under the scheme. financial assistance is being provided to State/Uts on the basis of Computer Education Plans (CEPs) submitted by the States/Uts. Besides the KVS and NVS would convert one school per State/UT into a SMART school for which a grant of not more than Rs.25 Lakhs would be given per SMART school. Kendriya Vidyalayas and Navodaya Vidyalayas would also be given funds at the rate of Rs.15,000/- per neighbourhood school to impart computer literacy to 10 neighbourhood school to cover 10,000 such schools over a period of three years.
So far, nineteen States/Uts have been released funds under the scheme, on the basis of CEPs submitted by them. the names of States/Uts and the number of schools which have been granted financial assistance under the revised CLASS scheme is Annexed.

records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made any permanent arrangement for commercial production of new seeds of foodgrains developed during the past few years;

(b) if so, the details of this arrangement together with the names of the seeds which have been made available for commercial production under this arrangement, during the last three yeas; and

(c) the average annual quantum of availability of such seeds?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b)&(c): Indents for production of breeder seeds of newly developed varieties are given to Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR ) for production. The breeder seed so produced is allotted to various seed producing Agencies for further multiplication and commercial production. The crop-wise quantity of breeder seed allotted for multiplication during the last three years is enclosed at Annexure-I. The crop and variety-wise quantity of certified and quality seeds made available for commercial production during last three years is enclosed at Annexure-II.

records.qtitle: MONITORING MECHANISM FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF PMGY .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have also set up any monitoring mechanism for effective implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana;

(b) If so, the details thereof; and

(c) the States where this mechanism has already been set up ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE


(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE)


(a): Yes, Sir.

(b) and (c): Both physical and financial monitoring of Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) were being carried out by the concerned central ministries as per the guidelines issued by them. This was applicable to all the States, since the PMGY is being implemented in the entire country.
Planning Commission intends to directly monitor PMGY from the current year 2002-03.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) DEPOSITING OF PROVIDENT FUND BY COMPANIES .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have detected some irregularities being committed by the companies in different States by not depositing the amount of their share in the Provident Funds of their employees well in time;

(b) if so, the names of those erring companies which are not depositing the amount of their shares in the Provident Funds of their employees well in time in each State; and

(c) the financial loss suffered by the employees in each State due to these irregularities?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR (SHRI MUNI LALL)

(a) to (c): Some of the establishments have defaulted in the payment of the statutory Provident Fund dues throughout the country. As on 31.3.2002, the total default was Rs.1,336 crores out of which 77.32% is unrealizable being the amount locked up in court stays and establishments registered with BIFR, etc. Wherever any default is detected, all the actions as per law are taken against the defaulting establishments. Because of the persistent efforts of the Employees Provident Fund Organization, an amount of Rs.858 crore was collected during the year 2001-2002.

records.qtitle: ASSESSMENT OF EXPENDITURE INCURRED ON TRANSMISSION OF POWER .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made an assessment with regard to expenditure incurred on transmission of power in various States of the country;

(b) if so, the expenditure incurred by each State on transmission of each unit of power;

(c) whether this expenditure can be reduced by improving technology; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )


(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENT

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION NO.608 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 08.05.2002 REGARDING ASSESSMENT OF EXPENDITURE INCURRED ON TRANSMISSION OF POWER.

(a) & (b) : The investment (tentative) made during the IX Plan period for transmission in various States in the Country is given in the Annexure. The per unit cost of transmission varies according to the location of the generating stations, quantum of power flows apart from the investments made.

(c) & (d) : The transmission capability of the existing lines/networks may be enhanced by providing the following facilities:



1)	Installation of  Series Capacitors on the transmission lines
2)	Flexible AC Transmission System devices (FACTS)
3)	 Upgradation to next higher voltage level.



The above technological improvements help in reducing the 
overall expenditure on transmission of power by enhancing the capability of 
the existing line and would result in comparatively less investment per unit 
of transfer capacity.



Upgradation of technology of transmission and reduction of 
cost is being given high priority by Power Grid Corporation of India.  States 
are also being urged to increase their investments in Sub-transmission and 
distribution.

records.qtitle: RESPONSIBILITY FOR CULTIVATION OF BARREN LAND .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the responsibility for making the entire wasteland in the country cultivable has ben entrusted to an institute by Government by integrating all the existing plans;

(b) if so, the name of such institute and the reasons for giving preference to the above institute for such responsibility; and

(c) by when the wasteland is targeted to be made cultivable together with the area o the same?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT

(SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K. PATIL)
a) No Sir.
b) Question does not arise.
c) As per Wastelands Atlas of India 2000 (brought out by the Department of Land Rsources in Collaboration with National Remote Sensing Agency, Hyderabad employing Satellit Remote Sensing Technologies), the total extent of wastelands in the country is 63.85 m. ha. Wastelands are degraded lands, which are currently under-utilized and are deteriorating for lack of appropriat water and soil management or on account of natural cuases. Therefore, agricultural operations are gnerally not feasible on such lands at the first stage of development. The Department of Land Resources has the mandate to develop wastelands rather than to convert wastelands into cultivable lands. It is implementing three major Schemes viz. the Integrated Wastelands Development programme (IWDP), the Drought Prone Areas Progrmme (DPAP) and the Desert Development Programme

(DDP)for development of wstelands/degrded lands on watershed basis w.e.f.

1.4.1995. New projects covering 139.73 lac hectares have been taken up under these Schemes from 1.4.95 to 31.3.2002.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI GINGEE N.RAMACHANDRAN)

(a), (b) & (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (A), (B) AND (C) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 592 TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 7TH MAY, 2002.

(a): Excise duty is levied by the Central Government at the stage of manufacture of cotton yarn, cotton fabrics and ready-made garments of cotton.

(b): Details of excise duties levied on cotton textiles and textile products are as given below:-

(1) Cotton yarn - 9.2% ad valorem [ 8% Basic Excise duty (BED)+ 15% of BED as Additional Excise Duty (Textiles and Textile Articles);

(2) Cotton fabrics - 12% ad valorem [8% BED + 4% Additional Excise Duty in lieu of sales tax]

(3) Cotton ready made garments - 12% ad valorem
However, CENVAT credit of the basic excise duty paid at the earlier stage can be availed for discharging duty liability at the subsequent stages in the production chain. Thus there is no cascading effect of excise duties on account of imposition of duty at various stages of manufacture. Further in the case of readymade garments, exemption from excise duty is available for small scale units upto a turnover limit of Rs. One crore in a year subject to certain conditions. Clothing accessories and undergarments are, however, fully exempt from excise duty.

(c): Prices of ready made garments are determined by market forces. The impact of excise duty on the prices of ready made garments is limited to the value addition at the garment manufacturing stage.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) APPOINTMENT OF JUDGES ON POPULATION BASIS
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that one of the reasons for delay in disposing cases in the country is insufficient number of Judges;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto;

(c) the number of people for which a Judge is appointed in the country, at present; and

(d) how many Judges must be appointed on the basis of population to facilitate the smooth functioning of judicial system?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Both the Government and the judiciary are concerned with the insufficient number of judges. The Judge strength in the High Courts is reviewed once in three years. The Judge strength in the District/Subordinate Court is worked out on the basis of yardsticks fixed by the concerned High Courts. The posts of
Judges/Judicial Officers along-with supporting staff are created by the concerned State Governments. These posts are also filled up by the concerned State Govemments/UT Administration/High Courts as per their rules and procedure.

(c) At present, there is one judge for a population of 74,571.

(d) The Eleventh Law Commission in its 120th Report on `Manpower Planning in Judiciary: A Blue Print` in July, 1987, has recommended that the present strength of 10.5 Judges per million population be increased to 50 Judges per million population in a phased manner. The 120th Report of the Law Commission which had recommended increase in the number of Judicial Officers was circulated amongst all the State Govemments/UT Administrations/ High Courts for necessary action at their end. The Department-related Parliamentry Standing Committee on Home Affairs in its 85th Report on `Law`s Delays: Arrears in Courts` has endorsed the Law Commission`s recommendations and suggested that variations can be made for different jurisdictions on the basis of pendency, rate of disposal and other relevant factors in consultation with the judiciary. The Supreme court in its judgment dated 21.3.2002 in W.P.(Civil) No. 1022/89. All India Judges Association Vs. Union of India & others has suggested that the increase in the judge strength to 50 judges per 10 lakh people should be effected and implemented with the filling up of the posts in a phased manner to be determined and directed by the Union Ministry of Law, but this process should be completed and the increased vacancies and posts filled within a period of five years from today.

(d) Government`s plan to meet the shortage of physicians?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a) to (d) As per information available with the Government a total of 5,56,463 Allopathic doctors have been registered with the Medical Council of India. Besides, there are around six lakh Indian systems of Medicine and Homoeopathic doctors registered with their respective Councils. The norm for availability of doctors to the population in the country, has been recommended to be as 1:2000 by the Bhore Committee. As per the statistics worked out by the Medical Council of India, the availability of Allopathic doctors is at present in the ratio of 1:1800. If the practitioners of Indian Systems of Medicines and Homoeopathy are also taken into account the ratio of availability of doctors to the population will work out much favourably. Though there is no shortage in the aggregate number of doctors produced, there is an imbalance in the availability of doctors between different regions in the country.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

( PROF. CHAMAN LAL GUPTA )

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the table of the House. Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (d) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.467 due for answer on 26th April, 2002.

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c): The present processing capacity of fruits & vegetables in the organized sector is about 2 per cent. As per National Council for Applied Economic Research (NCAER) Report, during the 9th Plan, there has been a growth of about 4% in this sector. The installed capacity for processing of fruits and vegetables at the end of the 9th Five Year Plan in the organized sector has been 21.5 lakh tonnes. The Ministry of Food processing Industries is operating plan schemes to provide financial incentives to the food processing industries. The schemes are :
Scheme for Infrastructure Development.
Scheme for Technology Up-gradation, establishment and Modernization of Food processing Industries.
Scheme for Quality Assurance, Codex Standards and Research & Development.
Scheme for Human Resources Development.
Scheme for strengthening of institutions.
For the Tenth Plan an allocation of Rs. 650 crores has been earmarked for the operation of the schemes of the Ministry. The growth in the fruit & vegetable processing sector is projected at 8.9% if GDP grows at 6% per annum during the Tenth Plan. In case GDP grows at 8% as per the approach paper of the Planning Commission, the likely growth in this sector is projected at 11.7%. The installed capacity in the organized sector is likely to increase from 21.5 lakh tonnes to 33 lakh tonnes in case of 6% GDP growth and to 37.4 lakh tonnes in case of 8% GDP growth.

(d): Taking into account the above growth rate as well as factors such as replacement costs, modernization and improvements in the existing industry, etc., the total investment in this sector has been estimated to increase from Rs. 305 crores during the Ninth Plan to Rs. 1146 crores during the Tenth Plan (at 2001 – 2002 prices) in case of GDP growth of 6% and Rs. 1774 crores in case of GDP growth of 8%.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is fact that the Education Commission had recommended in 1964-65 that it was essential to spend 6 percent of the total GDP annually on education;

(b) if so, whether such amount is still not being spent on education, even after a lapse of nearly four decades; and

(c) if so, the reasons therefor and by when that much amount is likely to be spent on Education in future?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(PROF. RITA VERMA)


(a) to (c): The Kothari Commission on Education (1964-66) had recommended that educational expenditure should rise from 2.9% in 1965-66 to 6% in 1985-86. However, the allocation and expenditure on education has not so far reached this level due to competing priorities and resource constraint. Constant and continuous efforts are made to raise the allocation and expenditure on education subject to overall availability of resources.

records.qtitle: EMPLOYMENT THROUGH LABOUR INTENSIVE TECHNOLOGY IN FPIS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
:

(a) whether it is a fact that there are potentials for creating maximum employment opportunities in the Food Processing Industries by encouraging labour-intensive technology; if so, Government’s reaction in this regard;

(b) the institutes entrusted with exploring such technology during the last three years;

(c) the status of research undertaken by those institutes; and

(d) what facilities Government had decided to give to that industry to encourage the use of labour – intensive technology, during the last three years?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES

( PROF. CHAMAN LAL GUPTA )

(a): As per the Report of the Annual Survey of Industries 1997 – 98, employment in Food Processing Industries was 38,784 for investment of Rs. 1000 crores, which is comparatively higher than that in
(i) heavy industry and
(ii) agriculture and allied industries.

(b): The following Institutions among others, who had developed labour intensive technology in different sectors of Food Processing have been assisted under this Ministry’s Plan Scheme.

1. Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (CIFT), Kochi.

(Fisheries)

2. Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI), Mysore. (Pulse Milling)

3. Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar, Uttar Pradesh. (Meat & Poultry)


(c): The CIFT had developed labour intensive technology for :

1. Fish curing

2. Development of ready-to-serve products like fish cutlets, fish wafers etc.
The CFTRI had developed a mini dal mill as well as technologies for ready-to-serve products and for increasing the shelf-life.
The IVRI had developed technology to be adopted by small scale entrepreneurs with considerable manual input for meat products. Preparation of chicken nuggets and chicken patties on cottage scale basis are some of the technologies developed, which are labour intensive.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the work of production from the already-explored oil and natural gas reserves in our country has not been started so far;

(b) if so, what is the percentage of production being made from these reserves at present; and

(c) the reasons for not starting production from all these reserves so far?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS (SHRI RAM NAIK)


(a) to (c): After the exploration phase, starting of production from any area depends on techno-commercial factors such as, the reservoir characteristics, the quality of hydrocarbons, the prices of oil and gas, the infrastructure availability and the logistics. There is also a lead time between a discovery during exploration phase and the production of hydrocarbons. The reserves from the areas where appraisal is under progress, or which are not viable for production at present, are not significant, around 5% or so.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any effective steps have been taken to explore the possibilities of development of Indian Systems of Medicines;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps proposed to be taken by Government to provide the benefits of India Systems of Medicines to the general public?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)

(a)&(b): In order to develop the Indian Systems of Medicine and Homoeopathy, the Government in 1995 established an independent Department of ISM&H in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Department of ISM&H has already implemented schemes for the development and cultivation of medicinal plants, preparation of agro-techniques, upgradation of undergraduate/post-graduate institutions, standardization of drugs, encouraging intra-mural and extra-mural research and dissemination of information through information, education and communication.

(c): The Government has taken the following steps to provide the benefits of Indian Systems of Medicine to the general public as under:

(i) Speciality units have been opened in two Central Government hospitals in Delhi viz. Unani in Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital and Homoeopathic & Ayurvedic in Safdarjung Hospital.

(ii) As Health is a State subject, in various meetings with the State Health Minister/Health Secretaries, the Government have impressed upon them to start OPDs on similar lines in the Government hospitals and dispensaries in their States.

(iii) Essential drugs list of Homoeopathy, Ayurveda and Unani drugs have been circulated to all the State Governments.

(iv) The State Governments have been advised to fill up the posts of Doctors of these systems in Primary Health Centres, Community Health Centres, Government hospitals and dispensaries in the States and to provide adequate medicines at the Centres under the Pradhan Mantri Gramin Vikas Yojna.

records.qtitle: DUTIES ON INDIAN STEEL IMPORTS BY US .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text: to answer to Unstarred Question 2111, given in the Rajya Sabha on 7th December, 2001, and state how many times the rates of import duty on steel were increased by USA during the period from March, 1998 to February, 2002, and how much the same has been increased in each case alongwith the details of its effect on the steel trade of India?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (SHRI BRAJA KISHORE TRIPATHY) OF THE MINISTRY OF STEEL
A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 395 TO BE ANSWERED ON 19/04/2002 TABLED BY S/SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND RAJIV RANJAN SINGH `LALAN` REGARDING DUTIES ON INDIAN STEEL IMPORTS BY US
The reply to Unstarred Question 2111 given in the Rajya Sabha on 7th December 2001 gives information on the anti dumping and countervailing anti subsidy duties imposed by the US against import of steel from India and not on the structure of import duty on steel existing in USA. The details of the anti dumping and countervailing investigations conducted by USA against import of steel items from India since April 99 are as given below:

(i) Cut-to-length Carbon Steel Plates:
Nature of investigation Status/Details
Anti-dumping & Anti-Subsidy (Countervailing) US had initiated investigation in March, 1999. SAIL was the targeted company. Final duties (Anti-dumping 72.49%) (Anti-subsidy 12.8%) were imposed by US in February 2000. GOI has taken up the matter with the Dispute Settlement Body of WTO. A panel has been constituted to examine the issues in this dispute. First submission by GOI has been made before the Panel on 19th November, 2001. According to the schedule of the Panel, the final report would be circulated to WTO members by June, 2002.

(ii) Hot-rolled Steel Flat Products :
Nature of investigation Status/Details
Anti-dumping & Anti-subsidy (Countervailing) In December, 2000, the US DOC initiated these investigations. In November, 2001 US authorities have announced the final determination. The Anti-dumping duties (companywise) ranging from 36.53% to 44.40% and Anti-subsidy duties (companywise)ranging from 9.17% to 31.89% have been imposed in respect of the exports from India.

(iii) Cold Rolled Steel Products :
Nature of investigation Status/Details
Anti-dumping & Anti-Subsidy (Countervailing) In October 2001 the US ITC instituted AD/CVD investigations against import of certain cold-rolled steel products imported into USA from 20 countries including India. The preliminary determination was due on 7th March 2002. However in keeping with the petitioners request the US DOC has postponed the preliminary determination until 26.4.2002.
In addition to the above the US President announced temporary safeguard measures on 5th March 2002 against import of certain steel products and imposing tariff of 8% to 30% and tariff rate quotas. India has been excluded from the safeguard action except in the category of carbon flanges for which the tafiff will be 13% (first year) 10% (second year) and 7% (third year).

records.qtitle: (clubbed) PERMISSION FOR MODIFIED BT COTTON SEED .
records.name: R.P. GOENKA
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a final decision has been taken to allow farmers to cultivate genetically modified Bt Cotton seeds which reportedly had the potential to dramatically improve crops, while cutting down the use of pesticides;

(b) whether the approval has been granted for a limited period only; if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) the broad parameters/conditionalities laid down, if any, for growing any specific GM Cotton crop; and

(d) if the
records.ans_text:
to part (a) above be in the negative, the reasons therefor and the present status of consideration?
ANSWER
MINISTER FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R.BAALU)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The approval is granted for a period of three years so as to facilitate re-consideration of the matter.

(c) The broad parameters/conditionalities laid down interalia included:

(i) Every field where Bt cotton is planted shall be fully surrounded by a belt of land called `refuge` in which the same non-Bt cotton variety shall be sown. The size of the refuge belt should be such as to take at least five rows of non-Bt cotton or shall be 20% of total sown area whichever is more.

(ii) To facilitate this, each packet of seeds of the approved varieties should also contain a separate packet of the seeds of the same non-Bt cotton variety which is sufficient for planting in the refuge defined above.

(iii) Each packet should be appropriately labeled indicating the contents and the description of the Bt hybrid including the name of the transgenes, the GEAC approval reference, physical and genetic purity of the seeds. The packet should also contain detailed directions for use including sowing pattern, pest management, suitability of agro-climatic conditions etc., in vernacular language.

(iv) MAHYCO will enter into agreements with their dealers/agents, that will specify the requirements from dealers/agents to provide details about the sale of seeds, acreage cultivated, and State/Regions where Bt cotton is sown.

(v) MAHYCO will prepare annual reports by 31st March each year on the use of Bt cotton hybrid varieties by dealers, acreage, locality (State and Region) and submit the same in electronic form to GEAC, if asked for by the GEAC.

(d) Does not arise.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) AMERICAN INFLUENCE IN STOPPING PAKISTAN SPONSORED CROSS BORDER TERRORISM .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have used American influence in stopping Pakistan in for menting cross-border terrorism;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) whether any change has been seen in Pakistan`s policy towards terrorism after these efforts by India?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a)&(b) Government has kept the international community, including the United States, informed about Pakistani involvement in fomenting cross border terrorism in India, particularly in the context of the global campaign against terrorism. There is now increasing realization of the fact that despite professions to the contrary, Pakistan remains deeply involved with terrorist groups. The widespread consensus in the international community is that there is no justification for terrorism, which must be eradicated wherever it exits.

(c) While Pakistan has taken some cosmetic and superficial measures as part of their so-called `crack down` against terrorist groups in Pakistan, its sponsorship of cross border terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir and other parts of India has continued unabated. The Pakistani leaders including its President have also reverted to Pakistan`s time-worn and untenable formulations on terrorism, including seeking to justify continued terrorist violence in Jammu & Kashmir.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have got formulated any guidelines for preparing unanimously acceptable formula with regard to water sharing;

(b) if so, the details of the said guidelines;

(c) when these guidelines were prepared;

(d) whether action has been taken to bring consensus of all the States on these directions; and

(e) if so, the details of the action taken and when such an action was taken alongwith the result thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN SETHI)

(a) to (e) The draft National Policy Guidelines for Water Allocation amongst States were formulated by the National Water Board in 1994 and were discussed by the Board during its 6th and special meetings held on 17th March, 1994, 16th & 22nd June, 1994 respectively. The Guidelines enumerate various concepts and definitions related to rivers, river valleys and river basins, co-basins States, watersheds and catchments, storage, withdrawal, consumptive use and utilisation. The broad objective of the guidelines is to optimally harness the inter-State river waters for the betterment of the people of the co-basin States/Union Territories to the extent such development are not detrimental to the interests of other co-basin States. General principles incorporated in the guidelines for allocation of water are; equitable apportionment, allocation amongst states vis-a-vis allocation amongst uses, right of water use, inter-basin diversion, protection of existing

uses, existing inter-state agreements, parties to the process of allocation, water quality, long distance water transfer

(LDWT) etc. The Guidelines also enumerate various factors for equitable distribution of water such as contribution of each of the basin states in the water resources of the basin, demand made by the states and its practicability for utilisation, availability of alternative sources etc. It also has provision for review of the allocation once made. The draft guidelines were considered by National Water Resources Council (NWRC) during its 3rd meeting held on 6th February, 1996. The States expressed divergent views on these guidelines. The draft guidelines were reviewed by the National Water Board in its 8th and 9th meetings held on 6th November, 1996 and 19th November, 1997 respectively. After detailed deliberations and certain modifications, a majority of the members of the Board arrived at a broad consensus in its 9th meeting. The draft guidelines so modified were placed before NWRC in its 4th meeting held on 7th July, 2000 where no consensus could be arrived at. The National Water Resources Council in its 5th meeting held on 1st April, 2002 has again referred the draft guidelines to the National Water Board for having a re-look and arriving at a consensus on the draft guidelines.

(a) whether Government have taken any decision for implementation of a scheme, at National level, for saving the country`s rivers from pollution;

(b) if so, the details of that scheme and when the decision to implement that scheme was taken; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS (SHRI T. R. BAALU)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. The National River Conservation Plan which includes Ganga Action Plan Phase II was approved during the period April, 1993 to October, 1996, to take up pollution abatement works in 152 towns along the polluted stretches of 27 rivers spread over 16 States. The present approved cost of works under National River Conservation Plan that are under implementation is Rs. 3329 crore. The schemes of pollution abatement taken up under the National River Conservation Plan are i) interception & diversion works to capture the raw sewage flowing into the river through open drains and divert them for treatment,
(ii) sewage treatment plants for treating the diverted sewage,
(iii) low cost sanitation works to prevent open defecation on river banks,
(iv) electric and improved wood based crematoria to conserve the use of wood and
(v) river front development works such as improvement of bathing ghats etc.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN COST OF AGRICULTURE PRODUCTION .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the main problem of agriculture is the situation arising due to incessant increase in cost of production;

(b) if so, the reaction of Government thereto;

(c) whether it is also a fact that Indian Society of Agricultural Science and Indian Council of Agricultural Research have realized the need for comprehensive charges in research work, keeping in view the agriculture aspect of WTO; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)

(a)&(b): No Sir. The cost of production of agricultural crops depends on cost of cultivation and productivity. Accordingly in case the productivity increases at a higher rate than the increase in cost of cultivation, the cost of production of such crops may actually decline. Conversely, the cost of production may increase. Thus seen over a period of time, the cost of production shows a fluctuating pattern.

(c)&(d): The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has been continuously pursuing the work of agricultural research and scientists are being apprised of the different agreements relating to agriculture in the WTO. ICAR has prepared its Draft 10th Five Year Plan keeping in view the WTO.

(c)to

Further
records.ans_text:
the Minister of Law, Justice and Company Affairs has by his lettr dated the 4th April, 2001 requested Chief Ministers of all States and Chief Justices of all High Courts to fill up the existing vacancies in subordinate jucidiary as one of the main reasons for delay in the disposal of cases in courts is the large number of vacant posts of judicial officers in the District/Subordinagte Courts. The members of the State Judicial Service are governed by these rules and regulations. The Delhi High Court has initiated `Unit Scheme` under which judicial officers will be assessed by according graded priority for disposal of old cases according to the year of pendency.
Department-related Parliament Standing Committee on Home Affair, has since given their Report on judicial reforms on 31st December, 2001. records.qtitle: (clubbed) BAN ON STEEL IMPORTS BY FOREIGN COUNTRIES .
records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite being members of World Trade Organization, many countries have adopted measures to impose ban on steel imports in their respective countries;

(b) if so, which are those countries and the measures adopted by them to discourage import of steel in their respective countries;

(c) whether these measures amount to flouting of rules of World Trade Organisation; and

(d) if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR STEEL (SHRI BRAJA KISHORE TRIPATHY)

(a)&b): Yes, Sir. Various countries including the US, EC and Canada have taken measures such as imposition of anti dumping and countervailing duties, safeguard action & monitoring of imports to discourage import of steel in their countries.

(c)&(d): The application of some of these measures is inconsistent with the WTO agreements. Government of India has challenged the imposition of anti-dumping & countervailing duty by the US on import of Cut-to-Length Carbon Steel Plates from India. It has taken the dispute to the Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) of the WTO. The DSB has constituted a panel to examine this issue.

records.name: Ram Jethmalani
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government had announced New Telecom Policy in 1999;

(b) is so, the targets fixed for setting up of telephone network in the country under the policy:

(c) whether telephone system has been expanded on the basis of said targets ; and

(d) if so, the details with regard to achievement of the targets?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) The targets fixed for setting up of telephone network in the country under the New Telecom Policy-1999 (NTP-99) are as follows:-

(i) Make available telephone on demand by the year 2002 and sustain it thereafter so as to achieve a teledensity of 7 by the year 2005 and 15 by the year 2010.

(ii) Encourage development of telecom in rural areas making it more affordable by suitable tariff structure and making rural communication mandatory for all fixed service providers.

(iii) Increase rural tele-density from the current level of 0.4 to 4 by the year 2010 and provide reliable transmission media in all rural areas.

(iv) Achieve telecom coverage of all villages in the country and provide reliable media to all exchanges by the year 2002.

(v) Provide Internet access to all district headquarters by the year 2000.

(vi) Provide high speed data and multimedia capability using technologies including Integrated Services Digital network (ISDN) to all towns with a population greater than 2 lac by the year 2002.

(c) & (d) Yes, Sir. The telephone system is being expanded by Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. (BSNL), Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd. (MTNL) and other licensed private operators to achieve the NTP-99 targets. The details are as follows:-

(i) 414.47 lakh Direct Exchange Lines (DELs) both (fixed and cellular) have been provided as on 31.01.2002.

(ii) Teledensity as on 31.01.2002 including fixed and mobile phones provided by BSNL, MTNL and other licensed Private Operators has reached 4.04 per 100 persons.

(iii) 4,29,515 villages out of the total of 6,07,491 villages have been provided with Village Public Telephones (VPTs) as on 31.01.2002.

(iv) 28,533 out of a total of 33,071 exchanges are already provided with reliable media as on 31.01.2002. The remaining exchanges are being covered progressively during the current year.

(v) Internet access is available to all District Headquarters.
