MINISTER OF STATE FOR STEEL (SHRI BRAJA KISHORE TRIPATHY)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b)&(c): Manpower in Steel Authority of India Ltd. (SAIL) is proposed to be brought down to around 1 lakh by the end of the financial year 2004-05. This is proposed to be done through introduction of Voluntary Retirement Scheme, natural and other separations and minimal recruitment.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the NCERT has decided to conduct an All-India survey for school education;

(b) if so, regarding which different contexts the information would be collected;

(c) by when the above work has been decided to be completed; and

(d) the expenditure likely to be incurred thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(PROF. RITA VERMA)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): Contexts in which information to be collected include:-

(i) To up-date database of the 6th survey that can be shared with different agencies.

(ii)To assess the present position of educational facilities at different school in respect of coverage of school-going population, enrolment general, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes children and girls in particular with special reference to “Universalisation of Elementary Education”.

(iii) To assess the availability of physical facilities in schools, like school building, play ground, furniture etc.

(iv) To assess the availability of basic amenities in schools, like drinking water, urinals, medical check-up etc.

(v) To assess the availability of Pre-primary education in terms of number of children enrolled and teachers working in them.

(vi) Availability of schools for disabled children and disability-wise enrolment in them.

(vii) To assess the income and expenditure on school education (at the district level)

(viii) Availability of science laboratories and libraries in secondary and higher secondary schools.

(ix) Subject-wise enrolment in academic stream at Higher Secondary stage.

(c): Target date for completion of Survey is 31st March, 2004.

(d): The expenditure likely to be incurred on the survey is Rs.10.86 crores.

records.qtitle: ENFORCING QUOTA SYSTEM ON TEXTILE IMPORT .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that in many countries in the world which are members of WTO also a restriction has been imposed by enforcing quota system on textile import;

(b) if so, the names of these countries and whether Government have taken any action to and this quota system; and

(c) if so, what action has been taken and when ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES

(SHRI V. DHANANJAY KUMAR)

(a) to (c) Till December 31, 1994, the exports of textiles to certain developed countries (e.g. US; member countries of EU; Canada) had been governed by bilateral textile agreements entered into between India and these countries under the aegis of the Multi-Fibre Arrangement (MFA), outside the rules of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). With effect from January 1, 1995, the quantitative restrictions (import quotas) in the bilateral agreements under the MFA, are being governed by the Agreement on Textiles and Clothing (ATC) contained in the Final Act of the Uruguay Round negotiations of the GATT. Presently, our textiles and clothing items face restraints in USA, European Union and Canada. Quotas by themselves are trade restrictive.
As per ATC, the textile quotas would be phased out and textile sector fully integrated into WTO by 1st January 2005. The Government has been raising the issues of meaningful integration including enhanced quota, under WTO Agreement on Textile and Clothing at various fora.

records.qtitle: DEVALUATION OF RUPEE AGAINST U.S. DOLLAR
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that value of rupee has been decreasing constantly over the last few years in the country;

(b) if so, to what extent the value of Indian rupee has decreased against U.S. dollar from March, 1998 to February 2002; and

(c) what has been its effects on India`s foreign trade?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE


( SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL )


(a) The exchange rate of the rupee against the US dollar, effective from March 1993, is largely market determined. Under this system, the rupee-dollar rate moves in both directions on a day-to-day basis depending on the demand for and supply of foreign exchange in the market and short-term factors. The rupee-dollar rate is also influenced to some extent by the strength of the US dollar in the international currency markets.

(b) The rupee depreciated by 18.8 percent against the US dollar from the monthly average of Rs 39.50 per U.S. dollar in March 1998 to the average of Rs. 48.66 in February, 2002 (upto 21-2-2002).

(c) The depreciation of rupee, given other things, is expected to help promote exports and strengthen our efforts at cost-effective import substitution.

records.name: Kapil Sibal

(b) if so, when such discussions were held and at what levels; and

(c) the reasons that the quota system is still prevailing in these countries for export of textiles and by when it will come to an end under the WTO agreement ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TEXTILES

(SHRI KASHIRAM RANA)


(a) No, Sir.

(b) Does not arise.

(c) Textile imports in the European Union (EU) are governed by bilateral quotas under the Multi-Fibre Arrangement (MFA), which has since 1.1.1995, become part of the Agreement on Textiles & Clothing (ATC) contained in the Final Act of the Uruguay Round negotiations of the GATT. As per ATC, all quotas governing the textiles and clothing trade would be phased out by 1st January 2005.

( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )


(a) : Yes, Sir. As per the provisional data available from the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics (DGCI&S), Calcutta, India`s exports have increased to US $ 44.56 billion during 2000-01 from US $ 18.14 billion during 1990-91. records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been a constant decrease in the cultivated land holding of farmers in the country during the last many years;

(b) if so, the average size of the cultivated land-holding in the country at present;

(c) whether it is a fact that cultivation in this size of a holding has become economically unviable; and

(d) if so, Government reaction in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN YADAV)


(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. As per Agricultural Censuses 1970-71, 1976-77, 1980-81, 1985-86 and 1990-91, the average size per holding (in hectare) was 2.28, 2.00, 1.84, 1.69 and 1.55 respectively. The latest all-India results of Agricultural Census relate to agricultural year 1990-91.

(c) & (d): The viability of an agricultural holding depends upon a variety of factors including agro-climatic, level of use of agricultural input, availability of irrigation facilities, crop variety sown and the entrepreneurial skill of the farmer. No conclusive evidence is available regarding relationship between size of the holding and its economic viability.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:

records.ans_text:

(SHRI V. DHANANJAY KUMAR)


(a) to (c) Textile imports in USA are governed by bilateral textile agreements entered into between India and other countries under the aegis of the Multi-Fibre Arrangement (MFA) which has since 1.1.1995, become part of the Agreement on Textiles & Clothing (ATC) contained in the Final Act of the Uruguay Round negotiations of the GATT. Quotas by themselves are trade restrictive.
As per ATC, the textile quotas would be phased out by 1st January 2005.

records.qtitle: DELEGATION TO USA TO SEEK COOPERATION IN RESOLVING TERRORISM .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it has been decided to send a delegation under the leadership of Home Minister to the USA for seeking cooperation in resolving the problems of terrorism;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether any offer has been made by the USA so far for providing active cooperation to eliminate terrorism from India; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. Home Minister is expected to visit the United States at the invitation of the US Government as part of the process of strengthening India-US bilateral cooperation on counter-terrorism.

(c) & (d): India and the United States have an ongoing cooperation in combating terrorism through a Joint Working Group on Counter-terrorism. Besides sharing of information and assessment on terrorist groups in this region, the United States provides assistance through anti-terrorism training for law enforcement agencies in India, capacity building for consequence management and support for strengthening institutional structure in the country for combating terrorism. During the visit of Prime Minister to Washington from 7-9 November, 2001, the two sides agreed to launch a new initiative on cyber-terrorism. The two countries also coordinate efforts on counter-terrorism initiatives in the United Nations, including on a Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism, sponsored by India.
On 5th October, 2001 the White House spokesman had stated at a press briefing that President Bush had condemned the terrorist attack in Srinagar on 1st October, 2001 and that the President had also said that `Terrorism must end everywhere, and that includes in Kashmir`. Besides Harkat-ul-Mujahideen, which had been notified by the US State Department as a Foreign Terrorist Organisation, the US Department of Treasury has notified Jaish-e-Mohammad as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist, along with Harkat-ul-Mujahideen and some other Pakistan-based organisations and individuals.

(a) to (d) 171 major and 259 medium ongoing projects spilled into IX plan. An amount of Rs. 61, 013 crores has been spent on the construction of these projects up to the end of March, 2000. (e) Water being a State subject, the concerned State Governments are primarily responsible for planning, funding and execution etc. of all types of irrigation projects / schemes including flood control and drainage from their own resources and as per their own priorities.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that some State Governments have demanded for their partnership in the Doordarshan or for a separate TV Channel;

(b) if so, the state Governments which have made such demand;

(c) when the demands were received by Government from these State Governments; and

(d) the decision Government have taken thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SMT. SUSHMA SWARAJ)

(a),(b),(c) & (d) : The Governments of Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal have suggested that the State governments be allowed to have their own TV channels. The matter has also been raised in the Inter State Council. In this connection, it may be noted that `broadcasting` is a subject included in the Union List under the Constitution. With the coming into force of the Prasar Bharati Act, even the Central Government no longer runs Doordarshan and AIR.
Prasar Bharati is a national entity. Its responsibilities are defined under Section 12 of the Act and thses keep in view the requirements of the country as a whole.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country can be declared as flood free by strengthening, water management system in the country;

(b) if so, what is Government’s reaction thereto;

(c) whether Government have taken any steps so far in this direction;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) by when the country would be made flood free?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a),(b) & (e) Flood is a natural phenomenon. Complete protection to all flood affected areas against all magnitudes of flood is neither practically feasible nor economically viable. Reasonable protection against flood using judicious combination of structural and non- structural measures is the strategy adopted for flood management.

(c) & (d) Flood Management being a State subject, flood control schemes are planned, funded and executed by the State Governments themselves out of their own resources and as per their own priorities. Central Government renders assistance that are technical, catalytical and promotional in nature. The Government of India has set up Ganga Flood Control Commission to tackle the flood problem in Ganga basin, which has prepared comprehensive plans for flood management for all the 23 river systems of Ganga basin. Similarly, the Brahmaputra Board set up by the Government of India under an Act of Parliament has prepared Master Plan for main Brahmaputra and Barak Valley inter alia to control floods in North Eastern region. These plans have been forwarded to respective State

Governments for preparing detailed schemes based on ground surveys and for implementation. The Central Government has also set up 159 flood forecasting Stations on major interstate rivers which give timely warning to all flood affected regions in various States. The Government of India constituted several expert committees to study the problem of floods in the country. The Rashtriya Barh Ayog (RBA) set up in 1976 examined the problem in detail and submitted its report in 1980. The recommendations of RBA, which form the framework for flood management strategy in the country, were forwarded to all the state Governments for implementation. Further, a number of other Expert Committees/Task Forces were constituted from time to time to examine the area/region specific problems relating to floods, whose recommendations were also sent to the respective State Governments for implementation.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, Government’s assessment in this regard ; and

(c) the estimated percentage of additional profit likely to be achieved by oilseed extraction industry, by using this new machine ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AND SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY(DR. MURLI MANHOR JOSHI)

(a) Yes Sir, the Mechanical Engineering Research and Development Organization(MERADO), Ludhiana, a centre of Central Mechanical Engineering Research Institute(CMERI), Durgapur which is a constituent Institute of CSIR, have developed an efficient oil expeller which minimizes the residual oil left in the oil cakes.

(b)&(c) : Demonstration units of the MERADO oil expeller have been installed with the State Oil Federations in the state of Punjab , Haryana and Madhya Pradesh. The knowhow for the manufacture of the oil expeller has been licensed to units in Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh. The MERADO oil expeller leaves around 1% less oil in the residue as compared to the conventional expellers used by the oilseed extraction industry.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI V. SREENIVASA PRASAD )

(a)&(b): Yes, Sir. The domestic production of oilseeds is short of the total requirement of Solvent Extraction Industry. In order to enhance utilization of capacity of the Solvent Extraction Industry, Government has allowed import of oilseeds and oil bearing materials except coconut/copra under Open General License (OGL).

(c): There are 785 Solvent Extraction Plants having annual capacity of 337 lakhs MT in terms of oil bearing materials in the country. The requirement of the Solvent Extraction Industry for full utilization of the installed capacity is, therefore, 337 lakhs MT in terms of oil bearing materials including oilseeds.

records.qtitle: DECISION TAKEN BY NATIONAL WATER RESOURCES COUNCIL .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the meeting of National Water Resources Council was held in May, 2001;

(b) if so, the main issue undertaken for consideration and decision in the meeting;

(c) whether any final decision was taken on this main issue after consideration; and

(d) if so, the details of the decision?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a) to (d) The last 4th meeting of National Water Resources Council was held on 7th July, 2000 under the chairmanship of the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India. The deliberations established a consensus among the States on most of the important issues contained in the proposed draft updated National Water Policy and proposed draft National Policy Guidelines for Water Allocation amongst the States. However, some areas were found needing further more discussions. In order to examine and for achieving greater convergence and agreement on these issues as well, a Working Group of Irrigation/Water Resources Ministers of all the States/Union Territories under the Chairmanship of the Hon’ble Union Minister of Water Resources was constituted on 9th October, 2000. The first meeting of the Working Group was held on 22nd May, 2001 wherein the draft updated National Water Policy was deliberated upon to arrive at near consensus. The Working Group was unanimous on all the provisions of the draft policy except provisions on “Setting up of River Basin Organizations” and Water Allocation amongst States.” A Core Group under the Chairmanship of Union Minister of State for Water Resources with the Irrigation/Water Resources Ministers from Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Goa, Karnataka, Punjab, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu as its members was constituted to arrive at a consensus on the above two provisions of the draft updated National Water Policy. The Core Group has submitted its report which would be discussed in the next meeting of the Working Group. After finalisation of the draft policy by the Working Group, the same would be considered by the National Water Resources Council for its approval.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is fact that Government had taken a decision about two years ago to wind up Disinvestment Commission constituted in the past years;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether any fresh Commission has recently been constituted under the Chairmanship of Dr. R.H. Patel;

(d) if so, the names of other members of the Commission;

(e) the basis/criteria for appointing these persons in the Commission; and

(f) the functions of the Commission?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING, STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES

(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

(a) and (b) The Chairman of the Disinvestment Commission demitted his office at the end of his tenure on 30.11.1999.

(c) Yes, Sir. The Commission has been reconstituted on 24th July, 2001.

(d) The names of the other members of the Commission are in the process of finalisation.

(e) The criteria for appointment of the members of the Commission are that persons of eminence and expertise from sectors such as finance, industry, management, economics are given representation.

(f) The terms of reference of the Commission are as under:

(i) It shall be an advisory body and its role and function would be to advise the Government on Disinvestment in those public sector units that are referred to it by the Government.

(ii) It shall also advise the Government on any other matter relating to disinvestment as may specifically be referred to it by the Government, and also carry out any such other activities relating to disinvestment as may be assigned to it by the Government.

(iii) In making its recommendations, it will also take into consideration the interest of workers, employees and other stakeholders, in the public sector units(s).

(iv) The final decision on the recommendations of the Disinvestment Commission will vest with the Government.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS AND PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS

( SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL )

(a) : Yes, Sir.

(b) : Indian Railways has a large shelf of ongoing Railway projects and in March 2001, 281 projects were under construction pertaining to New Lines, Gauge Conversion, Doubling, Metropolitan Transport Projects and Railway Electrification plan heads with an anticipated cost of over Rs. 45,000 Crores. Progress of these projects is dependent on availability of funds from year to year.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a) to (d) The geographical area of the country has been divided into 20 river basins. Area North of Ladakh, not draining into Indus, and areas of Andaman, Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands do not fall in any of these basins. These areas constitute 36,758 square kilometer which is 1.12% of the total geographical area of the country. Requirement of water is closely related to population, demand for food, production of industrial items, production of energy and preserving ecology. The area of North Ladakh remains snow-bound round the year and is largely uninhabited having negligible water requirement. The requirement of water for Andaman, Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands is of the order of 950 million cubic meter which is met by harnessing the abundant rainfall in these areas.

records.name: Kapil Sibal

(a) whether it is a fact that production of agricultural products came down during 2000- 2001, in comparison to 1999-2000;

(b) if so, the details of agricultural products and the estimated decline in production of each of them;

(c) the details of agricultural products whose production increased in 2000-2001, in comparison to 1999-2000; and

(d) the extent of such increase and the reasons behind the decrease and increase, respectively, in case of the said agricultural products?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SHRIPAD Y. NAIK)

(a)to(d): According to advance estimates of production for 2000-01, the production of foodgrains, total oilseeds and commercial crops such as cotton is expected to be lower than that of the final estimates for 1999-2000. However, it is likely to be higher in case of certain crops such as bajra, maize, barley, other kharif pulses, groundnut and sugarcane during 2000-01 compared to the preceding year. The crop-wise details of expected decrease/increase are annexed.
The year 2000-01 experienced adverse weather conditions. The overall rainfall during monsoon 2000 was deficient by 8% and this deficiency accentuated during the subsequent seasons. Deficient rains adversely affected the irrigation potential also. Since only 38.4% of net area sown is irrigated, these weather aberrations adversely affected agriculture production and productivity and hence there is lower production of those crops which require more water, There is marginal increase in production of certain coarse cereals, other kharif pulses, and groundnut as they can better withstand moisture stress.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of round of talks have been held between India and Pakistan over the years; and

(b) if so, when, where and at which levels the same were held and what have been the main issues during each round of talks?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) India is committed to establishing peaceful, friendly and cooperative relations with Pakistan. While working towards this objective, over the last three years (July 1997-July 2001) the following have been the significant bilateral meetings between India and Pakistan:

(i) In 1998, India initiated the Composite Dialogue involving bilateral discussions at the official level on 8 identified subjects. The Composite Dialogue seeks to build trust and confidence, establish a stable structure of cooperation and address outstanding issues between the two countries. Discussions on Peace & Security including CBMs (Foreign Secretary level), and Jammu & Kashmir (Foreign Secretary level) were held at Islamabad from 16 to 18 October 1998. Discussions on Siachen (Defence Secretary), Sir Creek (Surveyor General/Additional Secretary), Tulbul (Secretaries Water & Power), Terrorism and Drug Trafficking (Home/Interior Secretaries), Economic and Commercial Cooperation(Commerce Secretaries), and Friendly Exchanges (Secretaries, Culture) were held at New Delhi from 5 to 13 November 1998.

(ii) In February 1999, Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee visited Lahore on the inaugural Delhi-Lahore bus service. During the visit the Lahore Declaration was signed by the Prime Ministers of India and Pakistan, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed by the Foreign Secretaries of both countries, and both sides issued a Joint Statement.

(iii) In March 1999, External Affairs Minister, Shri Jaswant Singh met his Pakistani counterpart at Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka on the margins of the SAARC Council of Ministers meeting and discussed matters pertaining to follow-up of the Prime Minister`s Lahore visit held earlier in the year. The Foreign Secretaries also met.

(iv) In July 2001, President Pervez Musharraf visited India on an invitation from Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The Summit level meeting contributed to a better understanding of each sides view point. The entire gamut of our relations were discussed during these talks. India emphasised the need to build an atmosphere of trust for progress on all outstanding issues including Jammu & Kashmir. We also focussed on cross border terrorism and conveyed that India had the resolve, strength and stamina to counter terrorism and violence till it was decisively crushed.
In addition to the above meetings, in June 1999, External Affairs Minister Shri Jaswant Singh met his Pakistani counterpart Mr. Sartaj Aziz at New Delhi, during the Kargil conflict. During this meeting Pakistan was told in clear terms that Pakistan`s armed intrusion and aggression at Kargil has to be vacated.

records.qtitle: POWER GENERATION THROUGH CAPTIVE POWER PROJECTS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that certain industries are generating power in the country through captive power projects to fulfil their fuel related needs;

(b) if so, total quantity of power being generated through this medium in the country and the installed generation capacity of these projects;

(c) whether a decision has been taken to earmark the surplus power produced by these projects for the use of common men through the medium of power grid;

(d) if so, the details thereof; and

(e) the average generation cost of these projects?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )


(a): Yes, Sir.


(b): Details regarding the total installed capacity and the quantity of power being generated by captive power plants are not available as under Section 44 of the Electricity

(Supply) Act, 1948, the State Electricity Boards give consent to setting up of captive power plants by various industries. However, as per information available with the Central Electricity Authority, as on March 31, 1999, 20 selected industries (having an installed capacity of 1 MW and above) have set up a captive generating capacity of 13,932 MW in the country which generated 48354 GwHr of power. Details are given in the Annexure.

(c) & (d): On July 11, 2001 the Ministry of Power has circulated a Captive Power Policy prepared by the Ministry of Power in consultation with the CEA to all the State Governments and Union Territories. In this policy, the following has been reiterated:
If captive plant is of Hydro or cogeneration, such plant, irrespective of its size, may be permitted liberally.
If captive power plant is based on coal or liquid fuel or gas such plant may be allowed and capacity of the plant permitted up to 200% of the requirement of industry (If the State is deficit in power).
Captive power plant may be allowed if State/SEB or successor entity are unable to supply the required power supply. Such a captive power plant can be considered for the uninterrupted power supply to the industry even if the State is surplus in power.
If the industry requires quality power supply which is not available, the proposal for installation of the captive power plant can be considered.
If the cost of generation from captive power plant is found to be lower, the proposal may be considered after examining the cost and tariff.
Units in Special Economic Zone (SEZs) and/industrial entities may be allowed to set up captive power plants liberally.
Banking facilities are proposed to be provided to CPPs. The rates for banking may be determined on mutually agreed terms.
Prior approval of SEB has to be obtained for wheeling of power. Wheeling will be done to any service (HT or LT). Wheeling charges may be worked out based on pooled rates worked out by Central/State Transmission Utility of that region.
The tariff for sale of power from thermal CPPs, may be fixed after mutual discussion and could be based on pooled variable charge of thermal power stations operating in the SEB plus some percentage of the pooled variable charges as incentive. Tariff could also be based on the highest variable cost in the system or actual variable cost of CPP, whichever is lower and some percentage of the variable cost as an incentive.
Third party sale is also permissible with the approval of SEB.

(e) : It is not practical or meaningful to compute the average cost of the captive power projects as their cost is dependent on various factors like the type of project, viz. Hydro or thermal, fuel used, viz. coal, liquid fuel, natural gas, etc distance of the project from the fuel source, technology used, the mode of financing etc.

Minister of State in the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (Shri Santosh Kumar Gangwar)

(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (c) of Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No.1079 to be answered on 31.7.2001 regarding indigenous production of crude oil

(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. Several important steps have been taken to increase crude oil production in the country, which include :

(i) To improve the recovery factor from existing major fields by implementing Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR)/Improved Oil Recovery (IOR) schemes; in particular Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) has taken up 15 fields for this purpose at an estimated investment of Rs. 10,000 crore, which would also help in accelerating oil production from these fields.

(ii) To increase exploration efforts through the New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP). Under the first round of NELP, Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs) have been signed for 24 blocks in which works are in progress. Additionally, another 25 blocks have been offered under the second round of NELP, of which PSCs have been signed on17.7.2001 for 23 blocks.

(iii) To attract technology and investment; PSCs for 9 discovered fields, 8 in Gujarat and 1 in Assam, were signed on 23.2.2001 with consortia of Indian and foreign companies.

(iv) To explore in new areas, especially in deep water and difficult frontier areas, as also explore in the deeper layers of the producing fields.

(v) To develop faster the newly discovered fields and to step up the use of new technologies for seismic surveys, work over, stimulation operations, drilling of wells etc. in producing areas.
In any field, generally a combination of various efforts are implemented simultaneously and thus it is difficult to attribute oil gain to any individual effort. The Enhanced Oil Recovery/Improved Oil Recovery schemes are long term measures, the implementation of which takes about 4 to 5 years and the gain therefrom is spread over the next twenty years or so. However, with various efforts undertaken the declining trend of crude oil production has been arrested with more production in 2000-01 as compared to the previous year.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

( CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO )

(a) & (b): The Peace Initiative comprising restrictions on security forces initiating combat operations against terrorists in Jammu & Kashmir was announced by Government keeping in view the longing for peace and normalcy amongst the people of J&K and with the hope that terrorist outfits will appreciate this and all violence in the State and infiltration across the Line of Control and the International Border will cease and an atmosphere conducive for holding dialogue would be created. However terrorist groups have not recognised the imperatives of peace, dialogue and cooperation and have not shunned violence thereby hindering the peace process and inflicting misery upon the people. In view of this the cease-fire was not extended further beyond May 31st 2001.
In North Eastern States, Government has entered into cease-fire with NSCN(K) for a period of one year with effect from 28th April, 2001. The cease-fire is valid in the State of Nagaland. Cease-fire with NSCN(I/M) which is in currency since 1.8.1997 has been further extended for a period of one year with effect from 1st August, 2001. The extension of cease-fire is without territorial limits. However the extension of area is being reviewed Government is committed to holding talks to restoration of peace with all those militant groups who give up the path of violence.

records.qtitle: DECLINE IN NUMBER OF PERSONS SEEKING H B VISA .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been continuous decline in the number of persons seeking H1-B visa clearance from USA during the last few years;

(b) if so, the number of such persons during the years 1998, 1999 and 2000; and

(c) whether the number of such persons is likely to decline further during the year 2001 and if so, the estimated number thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)

(a) No, Sir.

(b) For fiscal year 1998 (October 1997 to September 1998), the limit of H1-B visas was 65,000, which was exhausted by May 1998.
For fiscal year 1999 (October 1998 to September 1999) the limit was increased to 115,000 visas, which was used up by June 1999.
For fiscal year 2000 (October 1999 to September 2000), the limit was 115,000 visas, which was reached by 21st March 2000.

(c) Recent slowdown in the U.S. economy, and the announced retrenchments in some of the major U.S. IT companies has led to a decline in demand for professionals with H1-B visa. However, 72,000 H1-B visas had been granted till March 31, 2001, whilst 60,000 applications are currently under consideration. It might be added that between 40-50% of persons receiving H1-B visas are estimated to be Indian nationals.

(a) whether Government have taken any action to assess impact on the information technology industry of India after USA`s proposal to make deduction in the information technology;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN) (a),(b) and (c): The Government has been in close touch with the IT Software Industry Associations, prominent Indian Software Companies, the Embassy of India in the US and leading experts in the field to make an assessment of the impact of the slow down in the US economy on the Information Technology Industry. While there is general agreement that the slow down in the US economy is having an adverse impact on the Indian Software Industry, there are different opinions about the extent of the decline in business and the duration for which this decline will continue. The principal impact being faced by the Indian Software Sector is increased pressure on margins. A solution for dealing with the situation that has found favour with industry is making pro- active efforts to develop and exploit markets in countries such as Germany, France, Italy, Australia, Japan etc. The Ministry of Information Technology has cooperation agreement with these countries which provide for exploring opportunities to develop bilateral trade and efforts have been mounted to enable Indian Companies to explore these markets more fully.

records.qtitle: NON PAYMENT OF DUES TO DPC .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that on account of non-payment of its electricity bills, Dabhol Power Company has approached the International Judicial system for recovery of the pending amount of electricity bills upto December, 2000;

(b) if so, what is the reason of approaching the International Judicial system in a case of non-payment of electricity bills in the country;

(c) whether any agreement for approaching the International Judicial system had already been entered with Dabhol Power Company; and

(d) if so, what other terms were accepted in the agreement?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

(a) & (b) : Dabhol Power Company has served notices of conciliation and arbitration as per the provisions of the counter guarantee issued by the Government of India, on account of non-payment of its December, 2000 bill by the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) and the Government of Maharashtra.

(c) & (d) : As per the Government of India (GOI) counter guarantee issued to the Dabhol power project on 15.9.1994, arbitration proceedings, if any, arising out of dispute, shall be held in London, England. Clause 13 of the counter guarantee which deals with the `Settlement of Disputes` provides as follows :-
Any dispute or difference (each a `dispute`) arising out of or in connection with this Guarantee shall, regardless of the nature of the dispute, be referred to the dispute resolution procedure in this section.


(A) The parties shall first seek an amicable settlement of the disputes by conciliation.

(i) Such conciliation shall take place in accordance with UNCITRAL Conciliation Rules (the `Conciliation Rules`) as at present in force and shall be conducted by three conciliators (or such lesser number as the parties may agree) to be appointed according to the Conciliation Rules.

(ii) Any meetings with the conciliators shall be held at New Delhi, India.

(iii) Each of the parties hereby gives for the purpose of the conciliation, undertakings and assurances as contained in the Conciliation Rules including an undertaking to promptly deposit its share of advance for payment of the costs as estimated by the conciliators.

(B) Any dispute that remains unresolved in accordance with the procedure outlined above in sub-paragraph 13(a), within sixty days or within such period as may be extended by the parties with mutual consent, shall be resolved by arbitration.

(i) Such arbitration shall be in accordance with the provisions of the UNCITRAL Arbitration Rules (the `Arbitration Rules`) as at present in force and shall be conducted by three arbitrators to be appointed according to the Arbitration Rules.

(ii) The arbitration proceedings shall be held in London, England.

(iii) the third arbitrator appointed pursuant to this paragraph shall not be a national of India or of the United States.

(iv) The language of any conciliation and/or arbitration proceedings shall be English.

(v) Amounts due under any arbitration award shall be paid within 30 (thirty) days of the award and interest shall accrue thereafter on unpaid amounts under the award at the rate referred to in paragraph 1 (of the counter guarantee).

(vi) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Guarantee, the law governing this arbitration agreement shall be the law of the place where the arbitration proceedings are held.

(vii) Any award given pursuant to arbitration in London, England, under clause
(ii) shall be governed by the New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards of 1958.

(viii) If at any time, there are arbitration awards in favour of the Company under each of this Guarantee and the Government of Maharashtra (GOM) Guarantee which remain unpaid, then any proceedings in India for enforcement, attachment or execution which the Company may initiate with respect to the award under this Guarantee shall be initiated not earlier than 30 (thirty) days after enforcement, attachment or execution is initiated with respect to the award under the GOM Guarantee.

.

records.qtitle: LOSSES SUFFERED BY BANKS DUE TO RECESSION IN SHARE MARKETS
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a)whether it is a fact that several nationalised banks have to suffer economic losses as of artificial recession brought into the share market;

(b)if so, names of such banks alongwih the extent of loss suffered by them;

(c) whether Governmen have idenified identified the persons responsible for this economic` loss;

(d) if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a)&(b) Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued detailed guidelines to all commercial banks on banks investments in shares and financing of equities. These guidelines, inter-alia, stipulate that subjec to the overall exposure to sensitive sectors, a bank`s exposure to capital market by way of invesmens in shares, debentures and units of mutual funds (other than debt funds) through primary orsecondary markets should not exceed 5% of its total outstandings domestic credit as on 31st Marchof the previous year. These guidelines also stipulate that, as a prudential measure, banks` investment in equities etc. should not normally exceed 20% of its net worth. RBI has reported that the total exposure of the Banking System by way of investment in the capital market, as on 31st January, 2001, stood at Rs. 8770.55 crore, which formed1.97%ofthebanks` ousandings advances. RBI has further reported that the banks also lend against the securities like shares debentures etc. and the total exposure of the banks in this category was less than 2% of their advances. According to RBI, although the exact loss incurred by banks is not readily available, it is no expeced to be large.

(c)&(d): RBI has reported that the loss in investment and lending operations arise mainly on account of fall in the market value of the securities, for which margins are usually kept. The banks also take the personal guarantee of the borrowers to cover losses on account of fall in the value of securities. The banks also make provisions in their books to meet the fall in the market value of securities. However, banks have their own internal guidelines to ensure prevention of irregularities/frauds and fix saff accountability.

records.qtitle: HANDING OVER THE TICKET DISTRIBUTION TO PRIVATE SECTOR .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that it has been decided to hand over ticket distribution work in the Railways to the private sector;

(b) if so, what are the facts in this regard and the percentage of ticket distribution work in the country, presently being handled by the private sector; and

(c) what are the details of factors responsible for taking a decision to hand over ticket distribution work to the private sector ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)

(a) to (c): Distribution of tickets through private parties is not a new phenomena and the system of issue of tickets by private parties such as Out Agents, City Booking Agents, Rail Tourist Agents, Halt Agents, etc. are already there since long time. Besides, RTSAs are appointed to purchase the tickets on behalf of those passengers who do not want to go to reservation office to purchase the tickets. It is difficult to calculate the percentage of ticket distribution work presently being handled by the private parties as no such data is being maintained and the number of Out Agencies, City Booing Agencies etc. changes from time to time. To proliferate retail railway ticketing through the use of Service Providers and terminal operators so that there is saving in the cost for the railways in this regard and for improvement in customer service, Indian Railway has entered into an Memorandum of Understanding with Indian Catering & Tourism Corporation Ltd. (IRCTC) to facilitate railway ticketing.

records.qn_text:

(b) if so, when it was constituted and what was the aim of its setting up;

(c) whether Government have reviewed its functioning during the last years; and

(d) if so, the detailed report of review?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING

(SMT. SUSHMA SWARAJ)


(a) & (b): The Press Council of India was constituted in 1979 under the Press Council Act, 1978 for the purpose of preserving the freedom of the Press and of maintaining and improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.

records.qtitle: GAP BETWEEN PRODUCTION AND EXPORT OF TEXTILES .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that 15 per cent of the total production of the country is produced under the textile industry while its share in the overall export is 30 per cent.

(b) if not, the facts in this regard;

(c) whether there is need to increase production to reduce the gap between production and export; and

(d) if so, Government`s reaction thereon ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES

(SHRI V. DHANANJAY KUMAR)

(a) & (b) The textile sector contributes about 14% to the industrial production and about 35% of exports of the country.

(c) &(d) The Government has been taking several steps from time to time to increase production and productivity of textile sector. Some of the important initiatives are as under: -
1) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUF) has been made operational from 1-4-1999 to facilitate the modernisation and Upgradation of this sector. 2) Government has recently launched Technology Mission for Cotton. One of the important ingredients of the Mission is to improve cotton processing facilities by upgrading/modernising the existing ginning and pressing factories. 3) Allowing foreign equity participation upto 100%, through automatic route, in the textile sector with certain exceptions. 4) The facility to import capital goods under Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme at 5% concessional rate of duty. 5) The woven segment of ready-made garments has been de-reserved from SSI Sector. 6) To prepare and sensitise our textile and garment industry to conform to the ecological requirements of importing countries by providing facilities by way of eco-testing laboratories. 7) National Institute for Fashion Technology (NIFT), its six branches and Apparel Training & Design Centres (ATDCs) are running various courses/ programmes to meet skilled manpower requirements of textile industry in the field of design, merchandising and marketing. 8) The New Exporters` Entitlement (Quota) Policies announced for the period 2000-2004 to provide stability and continuity and encourage competitiveness in textile exports. 9) The National Textile Policy 2000 has recently been announced to provide the policy direction for orderly and sustained development and growth of the textile industry in a harmonious way and to give a thrust to textile exports.
Besides the above, a comprehensive package for the textile industry has been announced in the Union Budget (2001-02) proposals, which include:-
- A provision for introduction of a new `Apparel Park Scheme. - Excise duty on textile items has been rationalised to a single rate of 16% CENVAT. However, cotton yarn including sewing thread would continue at the effective rate of 8% duty. - Reduction in customs duty from 15% to 5% on 159 specified textile and garment machineries. - 10% surcharge on imports has been withdrawn. - Weaving, processing and garment machinery, which are covered under TUFS, have been extended the facility of accelerated depreciation at the rate of 50%.

records.name: Kapil Sibal

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that a number of investigation agencies have felt the need to make it effective; and

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION ( SHRI BANDARU DATTATREYA ) (a): The Ministry of Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation has been implementing a Centrally sponsored Urban Poverty Alleviation programme called `Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY)` with effect from 01.12.1997 on all India basis to provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed or underemployed poor

records.qtitle: DELAY IN HEARING OF COURT CASES
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have identified the reasons for delay in hearing of court cases;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether steps have also been taken by Government to address this problem; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS AND SHIPPING

(SHRI ARUN JAITLEY)
.SP2

(a)&(b) The delay in hearing of cases in courts is due to various complex factors. These include vacant posts of judges, frequent adjournments, lawyers, strike etc.

(c)&(d) Various steps have been taken by the Government and the Judiciary to speed up the disposal of cases such as filling up of vacancies of judges, simplification of rules and procedures on the basis of the advice and recommendations of expert bodies, like the Law Commission, the Malimath Committee etc.
The Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act 1999, inter alia, stipulates that adjournments shall not be granted more than three times to a party during the hearing of the suit. The relevant amendments are awaiting notification.

records.qtitle: POLICY REGARDING UTILIZATION OF DISINVESTMENT FUND.
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether any fixed policy has been formulated by Government regarding the utilization of funds received through disinvestment;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) whether Government propose to earmark any fixed amount, out of that fund, to be used for developmental schemes of various sectors like education, health and public amenities etc.?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF 		STATE IN THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING, STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER 	OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES 
	(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)
	
	(a)	Yes, Sir.
	
	(b) 	It has been clearly stated in the budget speech for the year 2000-01 that the 		entire receipt from disinvestment and privatisation will be used for meeting expenditure 	in social sectors, restructuring of PSUs and retiring public debt. 
	
	(c )   The disinvestment proceeds are deposited in the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) 	like any other receipt of the Government of India. The expenditure out of the CFI include 	outlays for restructuring of public sector enterprises, social sectors like education, 		health and family welfare etc. As mentioned by the Finance Minister in his budget speech 	for the year 2001-2002, out of the estimated receipt of Rs.12,000 crore from 			disinvestment during 2001-2002, an amount of Rs.7000 crore will be used for providing 		restructuring assistance to PSUs, safety net to workers and reduction of debt burden. 		Contingent upon realisation of the anticipated receipt of Rs.12,000 crore, a sum of 		Rs.5,000 crore will be used to provide additional budgetary support for the Plan 		primarily in the social and infrastructure sectors.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any assessment has been made by Government about the quantity of water available from rivers of the Ganga basin;

(b) if so, the quantity of water flowing annually in the rivers of this basin alongwith the names of the same;

(c) the assessment regarding the quantity of water that can be utilised from each river; and

(d) the quantity of water being used from each river at present?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a) to (d) Yes Sir. The mean annual run off in river Ganga in India is estimated to be 501.6 Billion Cubic Metres

(BCM). Some of the major tributaries of river Ganga are Ramganga, Yamuna, Tons, Gomati, Ghagra, Son, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda. An assessment of the quantity of Water that can be utilised and the quantity that is being utilised has not been made separately for each tributary of Ganga. For the basin as whole, the quantity of water that can be utilised annually is estimated to tbe 250 BCM. During the year 2000, the utilisation was estimated to be 150.8 BCM for irrigatio; 7.9 BCM for domestic use and 5.9 BCM for industrial use.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been average rain fall in the monsoon seasons in the country during the last three years;

(b) if so, the quantity of water being available through the rain fall in the country;

(c) whether Government have made any assessment with regard to the harvesting of this rain water; and

(d) if so, the estimated quantity of such harvested rain water out of the total rain water?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a) Yes Sir, the South-West monsoon rainfall is defined as ‘Normal’ when the rainfall received in the country as a whole is within 90% to 110% of the long term average. In the years 1998, 1999 and 2000 the rainfall in South West monsoon was 105%, 96% and 92% respectively of the long term average.

(b),(c) & (d) India receives an average annual precipitation of 4000 Billion Cubic Meter (BCM) which includes rainfall and snow. Out of this, 3,000 BCM occurs during monsoon. The average annual flow in various rivers of the country is assessed at 1869 BCM. Out of this, utilizable flow by conventional methods is estimated at 690 BCM. In addition, about 200 to 250 BCM can be utilized through interbasin water transfer from the surplus river basins to the deficit river basins. A live storage capacity of 177 BCM has been created by construction of large dams and medium projects upto 1995. Projects to add an additional capacity of about 75 BCM are under construction and 132 BCM are under planning. It has also been estimated that about 24 BCM of rainwater is stored in 3.5 lakh minor irrigation tanks. Further, 432 BCM of ground water is replenishable out of which 154 BCM is being used. Government of India is also promoting rainwater harvesting through Watershed Management Program, Artificial recharge of ground water and rooftop rainwater harvesting under various schemes. An assessment of the total quantity of rainwater harvested through these means is not made.

records.qtitle: DISINVESTMENT OF PUBLIC SECTOR INDUSTRIAL INSTITUTIONS
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that a comprehensive scheme has been formulated to disinvest all public sector industrial units;

(b) if so, when the said scheme was formulated and what are the details thereof;

(c) by when the scheme is targeted to be introduced; and

(d) the estimated amount likely to accrue through disinvestment ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING, STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

(a) Disinvestment of the Government equity in the Central Public Sector Enterprises is being carried out in accordance with the disinvestment policy of the Government as enunciated from time to time. Its main elements are: · Restructuring and reviving potentially viable PSUs; · Closing down PSUs, which cannot be revived; · Bringing down Government equity in all non-strategic PSUs to 26% or lower, if necessary; and · Fully protect the interests of workers It has also been decided that the Strategic Public Sector Enterprises would be those in the areas of:
1) Arms and ammunitions and the allied items of defence equipment, defence air-crafts and warships 2) Atomic energy (except in the areas related to the generation of nuclear power and applications of radiation and radio-isotopes to agriculture medicine and non-strategic industries) 3) Railway transport
Moreover, for the non-strategic Public Sector Enterprises, the reduction of Government share to 26% would not be automatic and the manner and pace of doing so would be worked out on a case to case basis. A decision in regard to the percentage of disinvestment i.e., Government share going down to less than 51% or to 26%, would be taken on the following considerations:

(i) Whether the Industrial sector requires the presence of the public sector as a countervailing force to prevent concentration of power in private hands, and

(ii) Whether the Industrial sector requires a proper regulatory mechanism to protect the consumer interests before Public Sector Enterprises are privatised.
No separate scheme has been formulated to disinvest all public sector industrial units.

(b) & (c ) Do not arise in view of a above.

(e) The realization from disinvestment of equity depends on various factors like market conditions, financial performance of the company, terms and conditions of sale, interest of the investor(s) / buyer (s), advise of the professional consultants etc. No estimates of amounts likely to accrue from disinvestment can, therefore, be made.

(a) whether it is a fact that there is a need for comprehensive reform in technical education in the country;

(b) if so, whether Government have prepared any draft scheme for the said reforms; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and what decision has been taken by Government for getting assistance from private sector to implement this scheme?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

(DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI)



(a) to (c) : A statement is laid on the Table of the House.









STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.56 (H) FOR 23.02.2001 ASKED BY SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND DR. D.MASTHAN REGARDING REFORMS IN TECHNICAL EDUCATION

`Reforms in technical education in the country is a continuous process and this is achieved through the implementation of the National Policy on Education (NPE) and the Programme of Action (PoA). It includes coordinated and planned development of technical education as embodied in the All India Council for Technical Education Act, 1987. For the development of technical education, AICTE runs several schemes such as Modernisation and Removal of Obsolescence, Thrust Area Programme in Technical Education, Research and Development Programme, Entrepreneurship and Management Development Programme, Early Faculty Induction Programme, Quality Improvement Programme, strengthening of National Board of Accreditation, etc. An All India Board of IT Education has also been constituted under AICTE.
Apart from the initiatives on the part of the AICTE, recent initiatives taken to strengthen the technical education system include strengthening and consolidation of infrastrcutural facilities in Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Indian Institutes of Management

(IIMs), Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Regional Engineering Colleges (RECs) etc; establishment of more IITs, IIMs and Engineering Colleges; establishment of Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIIT) at Allahabad and Indian Institute of Information Technology & Management (IIITM) at Gwalior; National Programme for HRD in IT, Review of Postgraduate Education; increase of students intake in engineering and technical institutions; increasing output of information technology manpower; mobilization of private initiatives; development of technologies in emerging areas and their transfer to user agencies through technology development missions; transfer of techno-economic advances in technical education and appropriate technologies to rural people through expansion of Community Polytechnics; Scheme for upgrading existing polytechnics to integrate the physically disabled in the main stream of technical and vocational education; modernization of institutions and development of R&D base; Technician Education Project; modernization of libraries and switch over to electronic libraries with interconnectivity; etc. RECs are being strengthened as per the Mashelkar Committee recommendations to become world class institutions

(Centres of Excellence). Furthermore, technical education system will also work for improving the productivity of the informal sector of the economy.
Private Sector is involved substantially in running of technical institutes, some of which are of very good quality, under the overall supervision of AICTE. `

records.qtitle: CBI FINDING ABOUT MATCH TELECAST RIGHTS BY BCCI .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the CBI has revealed in its report that TV telecast rights for matches played in India had been given by the Board of Control for Cricket at lower rate;

(b) whether it is also a fact that the Board had received a guarantee money to the tune of Rs. 1.5 crore by giving TV telecast rights of matches played under World Cup, 1999 whereas England had received Rs. 26 crore for the same; and

(c) if so, what are facts in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS

(SHRI PON. RADHAKIRISHNAN)

(a) to (c): In its Report on Match Fixing and Related Malpractices, Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has indicated that this enquiry has not looked into the matter of grant of television rights since this issue is being dealt with separately. The report of CBI on this issue has not been received, so far. However, CBI has informed separately that it has recently registered 5 cases against DD officials and others. Three of them relate to cricket pertaining to telecast rights of Independence Cup, 1997, ICC Knock Out Tournament, 1998 and delay in purchase of telecast rights of World Cup, 1999. In its report on Match Fixing, CBI has, however, indicated that BCCI has received guarantee money of Rs. 1.5 Crores for World Cup, 1999 whereas hosts received Rs. 26 Crores for television rights over India for the series and thus India has undersold itself due to reasons not satisfactorily explained by BCCI.

MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING AND DEPARTMENT OF PENSION AND PENSIONERS` WELFARE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a) : Yes, Sir. Union Public Service Commission conducts about a dozen competitive examinations every year for recruitment to services/posts under the Government of India.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are considering to revise the prices of chemical fertilizers in the country ;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor ; and

(c) what percentage of profit is fixed for producers while fixing fertilizer prices, at present?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS

(SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA) ______________________________________________________________________________

(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.


Statement referred to in reply to the parts (a) to (c) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 382 to be answered on 15.12.2000.

(a) and (b): Government fixes the farm gate price of urea and gives maximum indicative price for DAP, MOP and complex fertilizers. No revision of these prices is envisaged at this juncture.

(c): Producers of indigenous urea and DAP/complex fertilizers get subsidy/concessions to bridge the gap between the selling price at which they are required to sell and their cost of production depending on the calculations made under Retention Price-cum-Subsidy Scheme in case of urea and the Concession Scheme in operation for DAP/complex fertilizers. A 12% post-tax return on net worth is built into the RPS. Similarly in the case of indigenous DAP, 12% post-tax return on net worth is envisaged while determining the cost of production under the Concession Scheme. For complex grade fertilizers and SSP, the rate of concession is determined taking into account their nutrient content and the concession on per unit of nutrients in indigenous DAP and MOP.

records.qtitle: FLOW OF WASTE MATERIALS IN GANGA AND YAMUNA .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that waste materials, debris, and dirty water of the cities and towns is flowing into the waters of Ganga and Yamuna rivers at many places;

(b) if so, the estimated quantity of waste materials merging every day into the said rives, separate; and

(c) the estimated percentage of dirty water, in the water generally flowing every day in the said rivers?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT & FORESTS

(SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. According to the survey conducted by Central Pollution Control Board, the waste water of the cities and towns is flowing into the waters of Ganga and Yamuna rivers at many places. The estimated quantity of wastewater discharged into these rivers is about 5300 million liters per day.

(c) The percentage of wastewater over the total fresh water flowing into these rivers is not estimated as it varies on day to day basis. However, both the rivers suffer for want of minimum flow needed to maintain the desired river regime. For example, in Yamuna river in its stretch from Tajewala to Etawah, there is no perennial flow during non-monsoon months of the year and what is seen flowing in the river particularly in Delhi is the wastewater of the city discharged in partly treated and partly untreated condition. Similarly, the river Ganga has low flow conditions from Hardwar downstream to Varanasi.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.min_name: SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND RURAL AND AGRO INDUSTR
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that small scale industries have been included under priority sector for providing loans to them by the financial institutions, particularly by the banks in the country;

(b) if so, the percentage of loans meant for the small scale industries out of the total loans to be provided as per the directions issued in this regard;

(c) whether it is also a fact that these directions are not being followed;

(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(e) the average percentage of loans being provided to the small scale industries at present?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES

(SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): No separate target is fixed for lending to Small Scale Industries (SSIs) for loans to be advanced by Indian banks. Advances to SSIs are included in the overall target of 40% under priority sector to be achieved by banks. However, in order to ensure that banks do not ignore the credit needs of smaller units among SSIs, it has been stipulated that banks should lend at least 40% of their advances to SSI sector to those units whose investment in plant and machinery is upto Rs. 5 lakh and 20% to those units whose investment in plant and machinery is between Rs. 5 lakh and Rs. 25 lakh. The foreign banks in India have been given by the Reserve Bank of India a target of 10% of net bank credit to be achieved by them for loans to SSIs. As at the end of March 2000, they have achieved the target and the percentage stood at 10.23.

(c): No, Sir.

(d): Does not arise.

(e): As per the Reserve Bank of India, as on 31st March, 2000, public sector banks net credit to Small Scale Sector was 15.63% of their total net bank credit.

records.qtitle: TERRORIST TRAINING CAMPS IN PAKISTAN AND POK .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Pakistan has set up camps for training the terrorists in its country and Pak occupied Kashmir;

(b) if so, the locations of these camps;

(c) the number of terrorists trained in these camps so far; and

(d) whether Government will take any steps to destroy these camps?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)


(a) to (d): A large number of such training camps have been set up in Pakistan/Pak occupied Kashmir. These camps are located along the International Border/Line of Control and also in some depth areas. Some camps are established on a temporary basis. Therefore, their numbers keep fluctuating. A large number of militants have received training at various camps. While our security forces take all suitable steps to contain and control infiltration, any action beyond the LoC/IB by the Indian security forces is not being contemplated.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether after bringing about an improvement in transmission system, Government have connected each of the 250 MW power generating projects in such a manner, so that the generated power can easily be transmitted in those areas of the country facing power shortage at the time of requirement;

(b) if so, Government`s reaction thereto; and

(c) if not, whether it is also a fact that in the absence of adequate transmission system power production has to be stopped sometimes in the project?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

(SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA)

(a) to (c): The power system in the country has been developed on regional basis comprising of Northern, Western, Southern, Eastern and North-Eastern Regional Grids. The transmission system for evacuation and utilization of power from generating units including 250 MW units are planned for utilization in a regional grid system in which the generating unit is located.
At present Eastern and North Eastern Regions are operating in synchronism and it is proposed to interconnect Northern, Eastern and North Eastern Regions by the end of the 10th Plan and to interconnect all the regions and operate them as a National Grid by the end of the 11th Plan.
At present, POWERGRID has a capacity to transfer 4350 MW of power on inter-regional basis, which is likely to increase to 14,000 MW by the end of 2007 and 30,000 MW by 2012.
On account of low load development in the constituent states of Eastern Regional system, certain power stations have to be operated at lower PLF. Efforts are being made to transfer surplus power from this region to the adjoining regions and on the basis of existing inter regional system about 1000 MW power is being transferred at present to the adjoining regions. This capacity would increase further with the commissioning of 400 KV Biharshariff to Allahabad Line in 2001.

records.qtitle: ABOLITION OF GOVERNMENT MONOPOLY IN PETROLEUM SECTOR .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have made any assessment to abolish its monopoly in petroleum industry by making it competitive for bringing down the prices of petroleum products in the country;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) if not, the reasons therefor;

(d) whether Government will take a decision immediately to abolish its monopoly for bringing down the prices of petroleum products in the country and making their prices competitive; and

(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS

(SHRI E. PONNUSWAMY)

(a) to (e): Government in November 1997, decided the details of phasing of dismantling programme of administered pricing mechanism (APM) for moving towards a competitive market in the petroleum sector. Accordingly, the petroleum sector is scheduled for full deregulation from April 2002 onwards. Pursuant to the said decision, the consumer prices of all petroleum products except petrol, diesel, ATF, kerosene for public distribution system and domestic LPG have been decontrolled and the retention pricing system has been abolished for the refineries with effect from 1.4.1998. As per the programme, the price of domestic LPG is to be suitably adjusted to reach subsidy level at 15% of import parity during the year 2000-01. Suitable adjustment in prices of kerosene for public distribution would be made to reach subsidy level at 33.33% of the import parity. On full deregulation, 2002 onwards, the subsidy on kerosene for public distribution and LPG domestic will be transferred to the fiscal budget of the Government. The domestic consumer prices would depend on the oil and product prices in the international market.

records.qtitle: EFFECT OF IMPORT ON INDIGENOUS TRADE
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that many items were permitted to be imported into the country over the last few months;

(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that due to this there was a massive increase in imports in the country resulting in economic crisis in the indigenous trade; and

(c) if so, whether Government propose to gather extensive information in this regard and issue a White Paper?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY

( SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH )


(a) to (c ) India has been following a consistent policy for gradual removal of restrictions on imports since 1991. Tariff line- wise import policy was first announced on 31.3.1996. As on that date, import of 6161tariff lines (at 10 digit level) out of the total number of 10202 was free. Import restrictions on 488 tariff lines were removed during the period 1.4.96 to 31.3.97. Further 391 tariff lines (at 8 digit level) were freed during the period 1.4.97 to 13.4.98 and 894 tariff lines (at 8 digit level) were freed on 1.4.99. Import restrictions on 714 tariff lines were removed on 31.3.2000. The removal of restriction as carried out on 31.03.2000 was a part of the consistent policy being followed since 1991.
The rate of growth in import of country`s non-petroleum non-gold items has not shown any significant increase. It was 6.88% in 1997-98, 4.04% in 1998-99, 5.47% in 1999-2000. These imports have shown a negative growth of 1.85% during the period April-Sept., 2000-2001. Nevertheless, significant increase has been noticed in the import of certain consumer goods such as umbrellas, locks, writing instruments, battery cells, toys, footwear etc. The Government is closely monitoring the situation and appropriate measures as necessary are being taken. Some of the measures taken recently include:

(i) Import duties on a number of items have been increased, for example, the duty on arecanut has been raised from 35% to 100%, on poultry products from 35% to 100%, on wheat from 0% to 50%, on skimmed milk powder from 0% to 60%, on apple from 35% to 50%, and on rice from 0% to 80%.

(ii) Suo-moto anti-dumping investigations have been initiated in respect of import of battery cells, battery operated toys and sports shoes.

(iii) Import of all packaged commodities have been made subject to compliance of all the conditions of the Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodity ) Order, 1977, as applicable on domestic producers.

(iv) Import of 131 products has been made subject to compliance of the mandatory Indian quality standards as applicable to domestic goods. For compliance of this requirement all manufacturers/ exporters of these products to India shall be required to register themselves with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). The list of 131 products includes various food preservatives and additives, milk powder, infant milk food, certain kinds of cement, household and similar electrical appliances, gas cylinders and multipurpose dry batteries.
Since, the situation is being closely monitored and necessary action as warranted ia being taken, there is no proposal to issue a White Paper on the subject for the present.

MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS

(SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA) ______________________________________________________________________________

(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.



STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.182 BY DR.D.MASTHAN AND SHRI KAPIL SIBAL TO BE ANSWERED ON 1.12.2000



(a) to (d) : The Expenditure Reforms Commission (ERC), in its 2nd Report Part-I, submitted in September 2000 has recommended rationalisation of fertilizer subsidies and dismantling of the controlled system in a phased manner. It has further recommended that the existing Retention Price-cum-Subsidy Scheme needs to be replaced by an easily enforceable system that provides incentives to the manufacturers to be cost efficient and ensures a desired level of self sufficiency with minimal support from the Government.
The Report of the ERC is under examination by the Department of Fertilizers and inter- ministerial consultation will be held soon to finalise the views of the Government on the recommendation of the ERC.
However, the issues pertaining to reassessment of capacities of urea manufacturing units, also referred to in the ERC Report, have been referred to a Committee headed by Dr. Y.K. Alagh for suitable advice and recommendation.
The Government has meanwhile taken corrective action by undertaking interim reassessment of capacity of high capacity utilisation urea units w.e.f. 1.4.2000 which would reduce the subsidy outgo by approximately Rs. 450 crore per annum under the existing Retention Price-cum-Subsidy Scheme.
The Government is in the process of formulating a new pricing policy, to replace the existing Retention Price -cum-Subsidy Scheme, keeping in view the recommendations made by the High Powered Committee headed by Prof. C.H. Hanumantha Rao and the Expenditure Reforms Commission headed by Shri K.P. Geethakrishnan.
