records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that an experiment production of transgenic cotton was carried out in various regions of the country;

(b) if so, the names of institutes which carried out such experiment and the regions where that land was located;

(c) whether agro-scientists had conducted any study about the post-experiment impacts; and

(d) if so, the names of these scientists and the details of their study report ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY

( PROF. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI )


(a), (b),(c) and (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 446 TO BE ANSWERED ON 25.08.2000-REGARDING PRODUCTION OF TRANSGENIC COTTON.____
Contained limited field experiments on transgenic cotton were carried out in various regions of the country. These experiments were not for production of transgenic cotton but were for evaluation of transgenic characters in cotton plants i.e. the effect of an introduced transgene that codes for a protein (Bt protein), produced by Bacillus thuringiensis, a bacterium commonly occurring in nature. During 1998-2000, evaluation of agronomic performance and on-farm trials for transgenic cotton to ascertain the yield, morphological characteristics, persistence, germination rate and pest load were carried out by the scientists of M/s. Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds Co. Ltd. (MAHYCO), Mumbai in private lands and State Agricultural Universities in the State of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu. The institutes were Acharya NG Ranga Agricultural University, Rajendra Nagar, at its Regional Research Station, Lamb, Guntur, as well as at Warangal in Andhra Pradesh; Punjab Rao Krishi Vidyapeeth at Akola; and Marathwada Agricultural University, Parbhani in Maharashtra. The effect of Bt cottonseeds on goats as model was studied at the Indian Toxicological Research Centre (ITRC), Lucknow and Bt protein was not found to be toxic. The agro-scientists of MAHYCO had conducted detailed post-harvest observations on the impact of Bt cotton cultivars at Jalna in Maharashtra; Dharwad in Karnataka; Hyderabad in Andhra Pradesh and Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu. A team of over 20 scientists of R & D laboratory of MAHYCO led by Dr. Usha Zehr, Dr. S. K. Mukherjee and others conducted these experiments. It was concluded from these studies that there was significant increase in the yield from transgenic plants. There was also noticeable reduction in the spraying of chemical pesticides for bollworms, a major pest of cotton. The residues of Bt protein in soil were either non-existent or were extremely low and did not have any effect on the microbial populations of the soil samples. The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee has approved on 30th June 2000, large scale field trials with scientific monitoring in some States. Work has started in the States of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

( SHRI SRIRAM CHAUHAN )

(a),(b) & (c): The Administrative Staff College of India, Hyderabad has been engaged to study the cost of acquisition and distribution of wheat and rice by the Food Corporation of India so as to arrive at ways and means to reduce its Economic Cost of wheat and rice. The final report of the College is expected by the end of September, 2000 only.
However, in the meanwhile the Expenditure Reforms Commission which was set up by the Government of India in February, 2000 has re-viewed the methodology of allocation of distribution cost between stocks maintained by the Food Corporation of India for distribution through Public Distribution System and buffer stocks. The Commission has made three important changes in the methodology.

(i) At present, only, the annual accretion to the buffer stocks is reckoned for allocation of distribution cost. However, considering that it would be necessary for Government to rotate the stocks held as buffer stocks over a two to three year period in the interest of maintaining quality, the Commission has recommended that transport cost and transit losses to the extent of one-third of the opening stocks of buffer be charged to the buffer carrying cost.

(ii) The Commission has felt that carry-over charges, namely, charges paid to the State agencies involved in the procurement of wheat beyond 30th June every year, should be part of the buffer carrying cost rather than economic cost of wheat for public distribution.

(iii) The Commission has also recommended that the economic cost should be estimated on the basis of pooling of opening stocks available with the Food Corporation of India in the beginning of the year and stocks procured during the current year, rather than being based on the minimum support price of the current year.
On account of these changes in the methodology, which have been accepted by Government, the economic cost of wheat and rice for public distribution have been revised to Rs.830 per quintal for wheat instead of Rs.900 per quintal as before and to Rs.1,130 per quintal for rice instead of Rs.1,180 per quintal as originally estimated.

records.qtitle: EXTENT OF COMMUNICATION FACILITIES IN THE RURAL AREAS VIS VIS URBAN AREAS
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the rural areas in the country have lesser communication facilities as compared to the urban areas;

(b) if so, what is Government`s reaction thereto;

(c) whether the attention of the Department of Communications has been drawn towards the same; and

(d) if so, when and what assurance has been given by the Department of Communications to provide the communication facilities in the rural areas?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)

(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.402 FOR 22ND AUGUST, 2000 REGARDING EXTENT OF COMMUNICATION FACILITIES IN RURAL AREAS VIS-À-VIS URBAN AREAS

1. Although it is a fact that the urban telephone connections are higher as compared to rural areas, this is mainly due to the fact that earlier the demand for telephones was less in rural areas. However, now the demand for rural areas is also coming up and Department is making all out efforts to cope up with the demand of the rural areas.

2. The telecom facilities in rural areas have progressed considerably over the last few years. Presently, Department of Telecom Operations is operating 2,74,20,192 Direct Exchange Lines (DELs) in the country out of which 49,26,287 DELs are working in rural areas. This is being done through 28,204 telephone exchanges in the country out of which 21,879 are in rural areas. In addition, out of 6.07 lakh villages, Public Telephones have been provided in 3,76,886 villages. It is further planned to provide a total of 57.9 lakh lines in the country (including MTNL) in the current financial year 2000-2001, out of which 14.2 lakh lines will be in rural areas through the existing exchanges in rural areas as well as 3,431 new exchanges planned for opening in rural areas. It is also planned to provide 19 lakh lines in rural areas during 2001-2002.

3. The Government has decided as a policy, to make available Telephone on Demand by the end of Ninth Five Year Plan in the entire country which includes both rural as well as urban areas along with the contribution of private sector. The Government has also envisaged that all the exchanges in the country will be covered with reliable transmission media by the end of Ninth Plan. The New Telecom Policy - 1999 also envisages that each village in the country will have at least one Public Telephone by the end of Ninth Five Year Plan along with the contribution from Private Sector. All out efforts are being made to achieve these targets.

(c) the annual average amount utilized by Indian exporters abroad in the past few years?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY ( SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)
(a) & (b) Exporters are allowed to retain a portion of their receipts in foreign exchange in Exchange Earners` Foreign Currency (EEFC) Account with authorized dealers, in India. Exporters can freely use the funds held in their EEFC accounts for all transactions of current account in nature. 100% Export Oriented Units and units in Export Processing Zones/ Software Technology Parks/Electronic Hardware Technology Parks are allowed to credit upto 35% of their export earning to EEFC accounts. Other exporters can credit 25% of their export earnings to EEFC accounts. Authorised Dealers are permitted to open and maintain such EEFC accounts.
(c) The Reserve Bank of India does not compile information regarding the amount utilized by Indian exporters abroad out of their EEFC balances.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have launched Joint Forest Management Programme for conservation and promotion of forests in the country;

(b) if so, whether any targets have also been fixed for the programme; and

(c) if so, the details of the targets and the estimate of the total amount to be spent to achieve those targets?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMNET AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) and (c): In accordance with the provisions of the National Forest Policy,1988, Government of India had issued guidelines to all the state governments on June 1, 1990 for involving village communities in the regeneration and protection of degraded forest lands under the Joint Forest Management (JFM) Programme. After a review of the JFM activities, the Central Government have issued fresh guidelines on 21st February 2000 to further strengthen the JFM programme in the country. No specific targets have been fixed for the programme, as it is a continuing and evolving process. The programme has picked up quite well during the last 10 years and as reported by various State Governments as on 1.1.2000, 10.249 million hectare of forests area is being managed in collaboration with 36,130 JFM Committees in 22 states. Central Government have requested the State Governments to involve the JFM Committees in all the afforestation programmes. Under the Centrally sponsored schemes of the Ministry, an amount of Rs.477.50 crore has been earmarked during the ninth plan period on afforestation activities and JFM is an integral component in the implementation of these schemes.

records.qtitle: COMMERCIAL AREA OF UNUTILISED RAILWAY LAND
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have formulated a scheme to generate additional income by making commercial area on railway land;

(b) if so, the unused land available at present with railways;

(c): the area of such land which can be developed as commercial area and income can be earned therefrom; and

(d): the names of such cities where such land is available, alongwith the area thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS

(SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)

(a): In view of the declining budgetary support from the General Exchequer in the last decade or so, Railways have decided to utilise air-space over its identified vacant land/stations requiring re-building.

(b): About 0.25 lakh Hectare .

(c) & (d) : Railways have identified a few stations and vacant plots in Mumbai, Delhi, Calcutta, Chennai, Bangalore and Hyderabad in the First Phase, with the intention to extend commercial development of railway land/air-space to all other parts of the country in phases and after gaining experience. The commercial potential of each site varies widely from place to place and from location to location. As the endeavour is going to continue for a long time, it is difficult to assess the total income out of this venture.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is less production of pulses as against their demands in the country continuously for the last so many years;

(b) if so, whether Government have formulated any action plan to make the country self sufficient in the field of production of pulses;

(c) if so, the outlines of that action plan and whether any time limit has been fixed to make the country self sufficient in production of pulses; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SBPBK SATYANARAYANA RAO)

(a) It is a fact that the production of pulses is less than the demand of pulses in the country, because of several constraints like cultivation by small and marginal farmers, on marginal lands and under rainfed conditions.
The production and consumption of pulses in the country during the last 3 years is given below:
Year Production (Lakh Tonnes) Consumption (Lakh Tonnes) 1996-97 142.44 148.60 1997-98 129.80 133.60 1998-99 148.09 148.90

(b) To make the country self sufficient in the field of production of pulses, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme National Pulses Development Project (NPDP) is being implemented in the country for increasing the production and productivity of pulses.

(c)&(d) The Planning Commission has fixed a production target of pulses for the IX Plan i.e. 2001-2002 at 16.5 million tonnes to make the country self sufficient in pulses production. The Govt. of India is making all efforts to achieve the targetted production of pulses. For increasing the production of pulses a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Pulses Development Project (NPDP) is under implementation in 25 States/2 UTs. The scheme envisages financial assistance to the states for production and distribution of Certified Seeds, seed minikits, rhyzobium culture, sprinkler sets, improved farm implements etc. In addition, field demonstration and farmers training are also being organised for the transfer of improved production & protection technology to the farmer’s field for increasing the production of pulses.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have constituted a Minister level Committee to identify the possibilities to keep the readymade garments sector out of the reserved list;

(b) if so, the Ministers included in the said Committee and whether it is also a fact that his ministry has agreed to keep the readymade garments sector out of the reserved list; and

(c) if so, by when Government are likely to get the Committee`s report?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES

(SHRI GINGEE N. RAMACHANDRAN)

(a) to (c) The Government have constituted a Group of Ministers to formulate an integrated and balanced package of policy measures necessary to strengthen the SSI sector, particularly in the context of the dismantling of QRs and the consequent increase of international competition and to consider and evolve a road map for selective de-reservation in respect of certain products including readymade garments, presently reserved for the SSI sector, as may be considered necessary for enabling a phased and orderly transition and increasing national competitiveness. The composition of the Group of Minister is as under:

Shri L.K. Advani - Minister of Home Affairs Shri Murasoli Maran - Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Kashiram Rana - Minister of Textiles Shri Yashwant Sinha - Minister of Finance Shri K.C. Pant - Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission Smt. records.qtitle: NORMS FOR SELECTION OF COLONIES FOR REGULARISATION.
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have recently decided to regularise the unauthorised colonies in the NCT of Delhi;

(b) if so, what is the number thereof;

(c) what norms had been laid down to select the colonies to make them regularise;

(d) whether it is also a fact that a number of colonies have still remained unauthorised in Delhi which are not covered under the above norms; and

(e) if so, the number thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION

( SHRI JAGMOHAN )

(a)to(e): In early 1993, Govt. of National Capital Territory of Delhi decided to recommend to the Government of India for regularisation of unauthorised colonies in Delhi which had come up before March 31, 1993. Soon thereafter, a public interest writ petition was filed by the Common Cause in the Delhi High Court against this proposal/recommendations. The High Court, in its interim orders, stayed action or decision by the Government for regularising these colonies.
On the directions of the Court, a High Powered Committee headed by Secretary, Ministry of Urban Development was constituted to go into the entire gamut of issue on unauthorised colonies. On the basis of the report of this Committee, the High Court asked the Government to submit its view to the Court in respect of regularisation of the colonies and the terms and conditions on which such regularisation could be done. After consulting all the local authorities including the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi, a draft proposal was prepared. This proposal was sent to Delhi Government and the Government of Delhi conveyed its agreement to the draft proposal in October, 1999. Thereafter, the Government of India formulated its views and these views are being submitted to the High Court through an affidavit. The High Court, after considering these views and holding further proceedings in the matter, will take appropriate decision. The Government will take further action in accordance with the directions/orders of the High Court.

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) As per the data available with Central Government the number of Primary Health Centres and Community Health Centres functioning in the country as on 30.6.99 is indicated below: Primary Health Centres - 22975 Community Health Centres - 2935

(c) These Centres are established and maintained by respective State Governments out of the funds provided under Minimum Need Programme/Basic Minimum Services and the Additional Central Assistance provided for the purpose. During Ninth Plan period, an allocation of Rs. 14433.85 crores has been made under State Sector Health Outlay, which includes provision for MNP/BMS.

records.qtitle: USE OF COAL IN PRODUCTION OF CHEMICAL FERTILIZERS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the possibilities to use coal, instead of natural gas and naphtha, in the production of chemical fertilizers in the country are being explored;

(b) if so, the action taken by Government in this direction;

(c) whether it is a fact that the use of coal would reduce the production cost of fertilizers; and

(d) if so, the estimated percentage of reduction in the cost of production?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS

(SHRI RAMESH BAIS)

(a) & (b): In the context of dwindling supply of natural gas, which is the preferred feedstock for production of nitrogenous fertilizers and increase in the price of naphtha based on import parity prices, Government is exploring use of alternative feedstock like coal. Government have, therefore, constituted a Task Force on 7th March 2000 under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Department of Fertilizers consisting of the representatives of Ministry of Science & Technology, Ministry of Coal, Ministry of Power, Fertilizer Association of India, Council of Scientifc and Industrial Research, Projects & Development India Ltd. etc. to explore the possibility of coal based technology for fertilizer sector. The Task Force has been asked to submit its report by 31st August 2000.

(c) & (d): Comparative cost of production of nitrogenous fertilizer based on coal as feedstock can be established only after a Detailed Feasibility Report is prepared in this regard.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
-

(a) whether Government have so far, made any assessment of the creation of new employment opportunities in the Information Technology sector;

(b) if so, the estimate of the total number of new employment opportunities to be created, as per this assessment;

(c) whether Government have also made an estimate of the availability of persons who can utilise these opportunities in the country; and

(d) if so, the details of such estimate togetherwith the details of the plan with regard to the supply as per the demand?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

(SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN)


(a) and (b): The Government has made such projections and the estimated demand of IT professionals in the country by 2008 is 2.2 million numbers in the software sector and an additional 4.8 million numbers in the area of hardware. In the case of software professionals the requirement for high level professionals with B.Tech/MCA qualification would be around 1.1 million persons. In the case of the hardware sector the requirement of high level professionals would be less than 10% of the numbers projected above.


(c): The IT industry currently employs 3,40,000 high-level software professionals, while the employment in the hardware sector is currently around 5,00,000. The current outurn of high level professionals with M.Tech/B.Tech/MCA qualifications in all disciplines is around 2,00,000 numbers, while those with diploma level qualifications is 2.25 lakhs per annum. Potentially both these categories are capable of utilising the opportunities offered by the IT sector.


(d): A high level committee has been appointed by Government to look into the entire range of issues relating to the provision of IT manpower for the growing IT sector.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have prepared a Coal Sector Rehabilitation Project for expansion and development of coal industry;

(b) if so, the details thereof together with the amount to be spent on the project;

(c) when the project was finally cleared; and

(d) whether orders have also been placed to purchase machines worth Rs.20,000 crores approximately for this project; if so, the dates when the orders were placed together with the names of the companies to whom the same were placed?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COAL

(SHRI T.N.SHANMUGAM)

(a): Yes, Sir. The Coal Sector Rehabilitation Project(CSRP) has been conceived to cater for investment towards increasing coal production in the 24 sub- project under five subsidiaries i.e. Central coalfields Limited(CCL), Mahanadi Coalfields Limited

(MCL), Western Coalfields Limited (WCL), South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) and Northern Coalfields Limited(NCL) of Coal India Limited (CIL) .The main objectives of the CSRP is to make CIL commercially viable , self-sustaining and increase coal production for meeting the future demand of the country.

(b): The total investment in the project is estimated US$ 1.695 billion, out of which US $ 1.03 billion will be co-financed by the World Bank(IBRD) and the Japan Bank for International Co-operation on 50:50 ratio. The balance amount will be financed by the subsidiaries of Coal India Limited i.e. CCL,MCL,WCL,SECL and NCL . The project consists of an investment component, technical assistance and training component. The investment component is to finance procurement of Heavy Earth Moving Machinery(HEMM) in 24 profitable mining sub- projects and also construction of Coal handling Plants(CHPs) in four of them. The technical assistance
-2- component is envisaged to finance Coal India’s institutional capacity development in the project implementation , mining operations and management.

(c): The project was approved by the World Bank in september,1997 and the loan became effective in June,1998 and disbursement for the project was started in July,1998.

(d): Coal India Limited has already placed the orders for purchasing the Heavy Earth Moving Machinery(HEMM) of US$ 477.89 million (equivalent of Rs. 1964.42 crores). for the five subsidiaries companies. The details of the orders/contracts for purchasing the equipments is given at Annexure.

records.qtitle: CONSENSUS ON THE DRAFT OF NATIONAL WATER POLICY .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that no consensus have been reached on the draft of National Water Policy;

(b) if so, the main reasons therefor; and

(c) what steps Government propose to take in this direction?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a) Yes Sir.

(b)&(c) The draft of revised National Water Policy was placed before the fourth meeting of the National Water Resources Council under the Chairmanship of the Hon’ble Prime Minister held on 7th July, 2000 for consideration/adoption. The deliberations established a broad consensus among the states on most of the issues contained in the proposed policy, however, some of the areas of differences were as under:-
i) Legislation for developing standardized national information system.
ii) Establishing appropriate River Basin Organisations with statutory powers.
iii) Water Allocation amongst States, and
iv) Amendment of Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956. In order to achieve greater convergence and agreement on these issues, the council has decided for constitution of a Working Group of Ministers of all the States/UTs chaired by Hon’ble Minister of Water Resources

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the amount of non-performing assets of the banks had arisen to Rs.51,710 crores till the end of March, 2000;

(b) if so, the details in this regard; and

(c) what steps have so far been taken by the Government to recover the said amount ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI BALA SAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a)&(b): While gross NPAs of the public sector banks have gone up from Rs.51710 crore as on 31st March, 1999 to Rs.52593.52 crore (Provisional ) as on 31st March, 2000, in percentage term it has come down from 15.89% to 14.28% (Provisional) of gross advances. Net NPAs for the same period at Rs.24211.49 crore (8.13% of net advances) as on 31.3.1999 have gone up to Rs.25840.51 crore (8.20% of net advances) (provisional) as on 31.3.2000.

(c): The Banks take all possible steps to recover their dues from defaulters through various means such as close follow up, filing of suits etc. Also Government of India/Reserve Bank of India/Banks have taken several steps for recovery of bank dues which include framing and implementation of recovery policy by banks, filing of suits with Civil Courts, filing cases with Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs), strengthening and setting up more DRTs and DRATs compromise settlement through Settlement Advisory Committees and monitoring and follow up of non performing accounts. Reserve Bank of India have issued guidelines for recovery of bank dues in NPAs accounts up to Rs.5 crore which have been classified as doubtful/loss on a pre-determined cut-off date. Chief Executives of Public Sector Banks have been asked to personally monitor and follow-up recovery in higher value accounts in accordance with the policy laid down by the respective Boards.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there have been wide changes in the contribution of various sources in the gross domestic product of the country after adopting the policy of globalization and liberalisation;

(b) if so, whether the above changes have resulted in new job avenues in new industries whereas job opportunities in conventional industries have declined; and

(c) if so, the Government`s reaction in this regard?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF LABOUR

(DR. SATYA NARAYAN JATIYA)
a), b) & c): A statement is laid on the table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 61 BY SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND DR. D. MASTHAN REGARDING JOB PROSPECTS IN NEW INDUSTRIES DUE FOR REPLY ON 27.7.2000.
Percentage distribution of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by economic activity at 1993-94 prices reveals an increasing trend in respect of manufacturing; electricity, gas and water supply; trade, hotel and restaurants; transport storage and communication; financing, insurance, real estate and business services; and community, social and personal services. Decreasing trend has been observed in respect of agriculture, forestry and fishing, and mining & quarrying. There has been a steady increase in GDP in recent years after adopting economic reforms. Estimates of employment and unemployment are obtained from the comprehensive surveys conducted by National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO). From the last two comprehensive surveys on employment and unemployment conducted by NSSO during 1987-88 and 1993-94 (latest available) a positive annual growth rate of employment has been observed in all the sectors of the economy. However, the annual growth rate of employment was significant (more than 3.5 per cent p.a.) in respect of electricity, gas and water Sapply; trade, hotel and restaurants; transport, storage and communication. financing, insurance, real estate and business services; and community, social and personal services. As per current trends, employment opportunities particularly in manufacturing sector may not grow significantly but at the same time new opportunities are being created in the services sectors such as hotel & restaurants, tourism, and information technology.

records.qtitle: (clubbed) RETURN OF KOHINOOR DIAMOND FROM BRITAIN .
records.name: C. NARAYANA REDDY
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have requested the British Government for the return of the World famous Kohinoor Diamond;

(b) whether it is a fact that the British Government is entertaining a doubt on the ownership of the diamond; and

(c) if so, what measures are being taken by Government to ensure the return of the Kohinoor, which rightfully belongs to India?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF TOURISM & CULTURE [SHRI ANANTH KUMAR]


(a) to (c) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF STARRED QUESTION NO.40 FOR 25.7.2000 BY DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY REGARDING `RETURN OF KOHINOOR DIAMOND FROM BRITAIN`.


As per the information provided by the Ministry of External Affairs, the Culture, Media and Sports Committee of British House of Commons, which is chaired by Gerald Kaufman is presently conducting an enquiry entitled `Cultural Property: Return and Illicit Trade`. The objective of the enquiry is to make recommendations with regard to issues relating to claims for return of cultural properties, which were historically removed and policies of museums on such claims including solutions other than return. The Committee is not, however, expected to make any recommendations on individual claims.
The Indian High Commission in London discussed the matter with the Kaufman Committee.

records.qtitle: RECONSIDERATION OF DECISION REGARDING FREE TELEPHONE .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether attention of government has been drawn to news item captioned `Muft Phone Ka Vit Mantri Ne Virodh Kiya, Sanchar Ayog Ne Manzoori Di` published in the Nav Bharat Times dated the 8th June, 2000;

(b) whether free telephones to employees in Telecom Department and Telecom Services Department have been sanctioned;

(c) the loss of revenue;

(d) whether the Cabinet would reconsider and withdraw such facilities limited to a particular class of particular Department; and

(e) if not, the reasons not to give such facilities to all Central Government employees? ................
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a) Sir, Government is aware of the various news items appearing in the newspapers against the decision of Department to provide the concessional telephone facility to the serving employees of DoT.

(b) No Sir.

(c) Estimated recurring loss of revenue will be between Rs. 78.30 crore (for Low Calling) to Rs. 99.90 crore(for High Calling) per annum. Most of them are likely to fall under low calling subscriber category. As such, the implications are likely to be to the extent of Rs. 78.30 crore. In addition to this, non-recurring loss would be Rs. 24 Crore on account of installation charges.

(d) & (e) There is no proposal to refer the matter to the Cabinet. The decision has been taken by the Telecom Commission. Which is competent for this purpose under the executive and financial powers vested in it. This decision has been taken in the wake of increased competitive environment which has emerged in the telecom sector. The decision is meant to motivate its employees and increase their availability. It is thus an operational decision taken by the Telecom Commission and therefore it does not impact other Departments. However, formal orders for implementation of this scheme have not been issued so far in view of the interim stay given by Kerala High Court. ............

records.qtitle: STEPS TO RAISE DOMESTIC PRODUCTION OF CRUDE OIL
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have taken any steps to raise the domestic production of crude oil keeping in mind the ever increasing demand during last so may years;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether as a result of these steps the import of crude oil has declined during these years;

(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and

(e) the percentage of demand expected to be fulfilled each by domestic production and imports in the country during the current year?
records.ans_text:
Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas

(Shri Ram Naik)

(a & b): Yes, Sir. A number of steps have been taken to increase the production of crude oil in the country which include:-

(i) Optimizing production from existing field by better reservoir management through 3-D seismic surveys, infill drilling; better pressure maintenance by redistributing water injector, installation/optimisation of artificial lift system and use of advanced & cost effective technologies for sand control, water shut off etc.
-: 2 :-

(ii) Faster development of newly discovered oilfields.

(iii)Finding new hydrocarbon reserves through intensified exploration activities such as : Exploration at greater depths in existing fields. Extending exploration activities to deep waters and frontier areas. Increased private participation in exploration and production activities.

(c): No Sir.

(d): The domestic crude oil production during the last few years has remained more or less constant and the requirement of crude oil in the country during the same period has increased.

(e): During the current year (2000-01), about 25.4% of the requirement of crude oil is estimated to be met from domestic production and the balance 74.6% from imports.

records.name: Swaraj Kaushal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news-item captioned `Dhanabhav se nahin, Lal pheetashahi se prabhaavit hai sainya taiyari; Malik` as published in Dainik Jagaran of 17th February, 2000;

(b) whether Government have prepared any scheme to avoid the loss to army because of procedure and delay in this process instead of lack of fund; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)


(a) to (c): The Defence Procurement Procedure was formulated and prescribed in 1992 by the Government. The procedure is comprehensive and includes measures to ensure that a conclusive and objective view is taken while selecting a weapon/weapon system and that extraneous factors do not influence the decision. The procedure is designed for procuring equipment against Qualitative Requirements specified, approved and confirmed by the user, through a system of trials and evaluation by the Services and through a process of competitive tendering to ensure cost advantages. Government is fully alive to the needs of the country`s defence preparedness and all steps are being taken to streamline the procurement process and to minimise the time taken in decision making. The Government have considered the comments made in certain quarters that Defence Procurement Procedures are coming in the way of time bound acquisition by the Armed Forces. In order to further streamline the procedure, a committee has been set up under Chairmanship of Vice Chief of Army Staff to examine the existing Defence Procurement Procedure in its entirety with a view to suggest specific measures for speedier processing of procurement cases.

records.ans_text:

( SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY )

(c) The State Governments formulate plans and take up irrigation projects from their own plan allocations and as per their own priorities. records.ans_text:

( ) (SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a) Yes Sir. The provisional rate of inflation (point to point) based the wholesale price index was 4.64% in the week ending on 8th April, 2000

(d): the percentage of increase in the prices of drugs which do not fall under the purview of the said Order?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI RAMESH BAIS)

(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): In the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995, promulgated on 6.1.1995, 76 bulk drugs were kept under price control as mentioned in the First Schedule of the said Order. (c) and (d): Price fixation/revision of prices of drugs is an ongoing and continuous process. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority, an attached office of the Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals, have between the period August, 97 to March, 2000, fixed/revised price of 965 formulation packs. Of the 965 packs, prices have been reduced for 402 and raised for 408 packs. (c) whether Government have ascertained the possibility of increasing this percentage; and

(d) if so, the facts in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES

(SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)


(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.






STATEMENT ATTACHED TO REPLY TO STARRED QUESTION NO. 654 FOR REPLY ON 11.05.2000 IN THE RAJYA SABHA


(a): Yes, Sir.

(b): The share of SSI production in total industrial production was 39.07% in 1998-99.

(c) & (d): The SSI Sector has been continuously growing. In order to ensure its sustained growth in the future, Government has taken several steps which will ensure the increase of production in the SSI sector. Credit is one of the prime inputs for production. To improve the flow of credit, Government has raised the limit of composite loans under single window scheme from Rs. 5 lakhs to Rs. 10 lakhs, the limit of loans without collaterals from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh and have announced the launching of the Credit Guarantee Scheme. 391 specialized bank branches have been set up. In order to enhance productivity, Government has strengthened the technology upgradation programme and facilities available through Tool Rooms, Product-cum-Process Development Centres, Regional Testing Centres, financial assistance for acquiring ISO-9000 certification etc. The operation of the Technology Development Modernization Scheme has been extended for another three years. In addition, Government has been helping the States in their endeavour of small scale industrial development by implementing various schemes such as Prime Minister`s Rozgar Yojana, Integrated Infrastructure Development, Computerization of District Industry Centres, facilities for entrepreneurship development etc.

records.qtitle: POWER GENERATION IN HYDRO AND THERMAL SECTORS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to revise the existing ratio of power generation in hydro and thermal sectors from 26:74 to 40:60 in the country;

(b) if so, by when the power generation as per the above average is proposed to be started in the country;

(c) whether Government have made any assessment of benefits of power production to be obtained as per the above average; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

( SHRI P.R. KUMARAMANGALAM )

(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.






STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 640 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 10.5.2000 REGARDING POWER GENERATION IN HYDRO AND THERMAL SECTORS.

(a) to (d) : Despite hydro-electric projects being recognised as the
most economic and preferred source of electricity, share of hydro
power has been declining steadily since 1963. The constraints which
have affected hydro development are technical (difficult
investigation, inadequacies in tunneling methods), financial

(deficiencies in providing long term financing), tariff related issues
and managerial weaknesses (poor contract management). The hydro
projects are also affected by geological surprises (especially in the
Himalayan region where underground tunneling is required),
inaccessibility of the area, problems due to delay in land
acquisition, and resettlement of project affected families, law and
order problem in militant infested areas.

The Government had announced a Policy on Hydro Power
Development in August, 1998 with the objective of accelerating the
pace of hydro power development in the country. An improvement in the
hydel-thermal mix is proposed to be achieved by
(i) completion of the
on-going hydro-electric projects
(ii) initiating advance action for
obtaining necessary approvals in respect of new hydro-electric
projects for which Detailed Project Report (DPR) is available; and

(iii) initiating work on survey and investigation in respect of new
green field sites to enable preparation of DPR so that necessary
approvals could be obtained and projects taken up for execution in a
phased manner.

Advance action has been taken on fresh starts under
Central Sector, as a result of which a number of new hydro projects
have been approved namely Tuirial (60 MW) Mizoram; Chamera-II

(300 MW) H.P.; Teesta-V (510 MW); Loktak Downstream (90 MW) Manipur;
Koteshwar (400 MW) U.P.; Development of Projects in the Parbati Basin

(2051 MW); and Dihang and Subansiri Basin (20700 MW). National
Thermal Power Corporation has also entered into an agreement with
Himachal Pradesh for execution of Kol Dam Project (800 MW).
Simultaneously, advance action has been initiated on a number of other
hydro electric projects namely Kameng (600 MW) Arunachal Pradesh;
Tuivai (210 MW) Mizoram; Tipaimukh (1500 MW) Manipur; Lower Kopili

(150 MW) Assam; Teesta Projects Stage-III, IV and VI (2055 MW) Sikkim;
Pala Maneri (416 MW) U.P.; Lohari Nag (520 MW) U.P.; Rampur (800 MW)
H.P., which will all yield capacity of more than 25,000 MW during the
time frame of 11th Plan (2007-12) and beyond.

Efforts are also being made to arrive at a consensus
amongst basin states regarding location of power projects locked up
due to inter-state disputes, namely, Shivasamudram 270 MW, Mekedatu
550 MW, Rasimanal 200 MW and Hogenakkal 120 MW in Cauvery basin.
Similarly, Renuka Dam Project 60 MW and Kishau Multipurpose Project

(600 MW) are also being pursued for an early execution.

Government is also committed to complete hydro-electric
schemes languishing for a number of years for want of funds. An MOU
with Government of U.P. has been signed recently in pursuance of which
Government of U.P. will jointly execute Maneri Bhali Stage-II (304 MW)
and Lakwar Vyasi (420 MW) with THDC and NHPC respectively.

A massive thrust is proposed to be given for hydro
development by starting work on preparing DPRs in respect of hydro
projects involving capacity of about 30000 MW in the next 5 years.

records.qtitle: REPLACING PARTS MACHINERY IN POWER GENERATING UNITS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that power generation in the projects can be increased by replacing plants/machinery in power generating units in the country;

(b) whether Government have conducted any survey to replace plants/machinery in the projects engaged in existing power generation; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and total amount likely to be spent thereon together with the annual increase in power generation?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER

( SHRIMATI JAYAWANTI MEHTA )

(a) : Yes, Sir. It is fact that power generation in the projects can be increased by undertaking Renovation & Modernisation

(R&M).

(b) & (c) : Government of India recognised the importance of R&M in 1984 to improve the performance of old thermal generating units. Based on the performance analysis, 34 thermal power stations having 163 units with a total installed capacity of 13570 MW were identified for carrying out R&M during 7th Plan period. A total amount of Rs. 1066 crores was incurred resulting into an additional generation of about 10,000 Million Units/Year. Subsequently, 44 thermal power stations having 198 generating units were identified under Phase-II programme during 8th Plan at an estimated cost of Rs. 2383 crores. The programme is at various stages of completion and on all-India basis, about 75% works have been completed resulting into an additional generation of 5000 Million Units per year after completion of partial works. Further, a large number of thermal units have completed/nearing completion their useful economic life and to keep these units in economical operation for another 15-20 years, many parts of the plants will need to be replaced under R&M/Life Extension programme.
Similarly, 55 hydel schemes with an aggregate installed capacity of 9653 MW were identified at an estimated cost of Rs. 1493 crores to accure benefits of 2531 MW/7181 MUs.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have offered to hold talks with the terrorist groups to bring them into the mainstream of society;

(b) if so, the details of the groups selected for talks;

(c) whether government have received the reaction of these groups; and

(d) if so, the details of reaction?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(SHRI CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)


(a),(b),(c) & (d): During his visit to Jammu and Kashmir on 26-27 July, 1997, the then Prime Minister had made an appeal to the misguided youth of the State, who have joined the militant ranks, to give up their guns, and said that the Government was prepared to have unconditional talks with them, to enable them to rejoin the mainstream. The Government is committed to the said offer of talks, within the constitutional frame work.
The Prime Minister of India had spelt out the parameters for initiating a peace dialogue with militant outfits in the North East on 15 April, 1998 at Guwahati declaring :
`To all those who have strayed from the paths of togetherness, whether in Assam or other States of the North East, I extend an invitation; come forward ; let us discuss, my Government is committed to holding talks, to a restoration of peace; let us do so within the four corners of our Constitution.`
Unstarred Question No. 3982 for 3.5.2000



Cease fire and peace talks with the NSCN(IM) are underway since 1 August, 1997. Suspension of operations with the Bodo Liberation Tiger (BLT) was also announced earlier this year. NSCN(K) have also issued a Press Release Offering a formal `cease fire` with the Government of India and political talks.
The offer for talks have been made by the Government in view of its commitment to resolve all issues through negotiations. The Government are firmly of the view that violence has no place in a democratic polity and the people by and large want peace and an end to violence.

(b) if so, the details in this regard;

(c) whether the incidence of firing from Pakistan at the border has also increased these days; and

(d) if so, the number of Indians killed during one year?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF DEFENCE

(SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES)


(a) & (b): There are no reports of increase of force levels along India-China border. Pakistan Army has carried out certain readjustments and reinforcements on the Line of Control. Some reserve formations have also been moved from their permanent locations closer to the Line of Control.

(c) & (d): There has been an increase in firing along the Line of Control. During the one year period from 1st April 1999 to 31st March 2000, 56 Indian Army personnel including 4 Officers were killed due to Pakistani firing/shelling along the Line of Control (excluding OP Vijay casualties).

records.qtitle: ANNUAL AVERAGE GROWTH RATE OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the annual production rate of agriculture was 3.1 per cent in the decade of 80`s has come down now to almost 2 per cent in 90`s;

(b) if not, the assessment of Government in this regard; and

(c) the reasons for this decline and the estimated rate likely to be gained in the first decade of 21st century?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OFAGRICULTURE

(SHRI SBPBK SATYANARAYANA RAO)

(a)&(b) The annual compound growth rates of agriculture production during the decade of 80`s and 90`s have been 3.72% and 2.21% per annum respectively.

(c) The deceleration in growth rate of production of agricultural crops taken as a group is mainly on account of deceleration in the rate of growth of yield rates.
The growth rate of production of agricultural crops depends upon a large number of factors such as agro-climatic conditions, performance of monsoon, timely application of seeds, fertilizers, managerial abilities of farmers, level of investment etc. Therefore, it is not possible to estimate at this stage, gain in growth rate in the first decade of 21st century. However, to increase production and productivity and thus growth rate of agricultural crops in the country, the Government is implementing centrally sponsored Integrated Cereal Development Programmes in rice/wheat/coarse cereals Based Cropping System Area, National Pulses Development Project etc. Under these programmes/project, incentives are provided to farmers for use of high yielding varieties of seeds, application of integrated pest management, propagation of scientific water management including micro irrigation and use of improved farm implements. Research is also being continuously undertaken to develop improved technologies so as to enhance the productivity and production of foodgrains in India. Field demonstrations on farmers` holdings including training of farmers and farm labourers is being organised for effective transfer of technology.

records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that after the declaration of new Communication Policy, 1999 certain companies functioning under private sector have not made payment of Government dues outstanding against them so far?

(b) if so, the names of such companies alongwith the amount of funds outstanding against them; and

(c) whether Government have also taken any action against them for not making the payment of outstanding amount, if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS

(SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR)

(a) to (c) Defaults in payment of license fee dues as per the prevailing license agreements had taken place before the declaration of the New Telecom Policy, 1999 (NTP-99). The NTP-99 specifically provided for satisfactory resolution of existing operators` problems in a legally tenable manner consistent with their contractual obligations. Accordingly on 22.7.99 the government offered a package to existing cellular and basic services licensees to migrate to the revenue sharing regime under NTP-99. Under the terms and conditions. of this package the licensees had, inter-alia, to clear the dues outstanding on the cut-off date of 31.7.1999 within a specified time frame. Forty licensees of Cellular and Basic cervices came under the process of migration, and all of them have paid the dues in terms of the migration package by the extended date(s).

Six cellular licenses were not covered by the migration package since by 22.7.99 these had been already terminated for non-payment of the dues. Further, two defaulting cellular licensees in Uttar Pradesh -(East) did not come under the process of migration because-one of them did not accept the package and hence an essential condition, that all the licensees in a Service Area accept the package, remained unsatisfied. Their licenses were not terminated In the absence of a fall back arrangement for their subscribers.

A modified migration package has been offered to seven of the above-mentioned eight license-holders in April 2000 with. enhanced penalties, etc. ` For the `eighth company (M/s. JT Mobile, Punjab) also it .has been decided, in principle, to offer a package for migration loathe revenue Sharing regime under NTP-99. The dues in respect of these eight licenses are given in Annexure. On 2.9.99, a migration package was similarly offered to Radio Paging licensees. However, as the terms and conditions of the package were not fulfilled, implementation of the package did not proceed further and the outstanding dues continue to persist, as detailed in the Annexure.

Outstanding dues against other value added service providers are also indicated in the Annexure. The government has taken steps from time to time to realise the amounts due from the defaulters. These have included, inter alia, issue of notices, invocation and encashment of Bank Guarantees, and even termination of licenses.

(a) whether Government have permitted Federal Bureau of Investigation of America to set up its office in India for working independently;

(b) if so, when it was permitted and by when the office of the said institution is likely to be set up; and

(c) what are the reasons for which Government have permitted this American intelligence agency to work in India?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

( SHRI AJIT KUMAR PANJA)

(a ) It has been decided by mutual consultations to allow the US Embassy in New Delhi to augment its strength for opening a Legal Attache Office. Such offices are normally manned by two FBI Officers. Government of India has similar representation in its Embassy in Washington. There is however no proposal for setting up an independent office of the FBI in India.

(b ) The decision was taken in February 2000 and the US Government is in the process of implementing it shortly.

(c ) The decision was taken in the context of growing Indo-US bilateral co-operation on counter-terrorism. While necessary mechanism to counter terrorism is already in place with the Extradition Treaty and the Joint Working Group on Counter-terrorism, the opening of the Legal Attache Office will enable more effective co-ordination between our law enforcement agencies. It will also signal greater commonality of interests between the two countries in the fight against terrorism. This will in turn exert pressure on extremist groups operating across borders.

records.qtitle: POLICY FOR PROPER MANAGEMENT OF WATER .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that water crisis is deepening day-by- day in the country due to the shortage of water supply;

(b) whether Government would formulate a well planned and definite water policy for proper management of water in the country; and

(c) if so, by when and whether Government have identified the fundamental bases and priorities for preparing the water policy; if so, the details thereof ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES

(SMT. BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY)

(a) to (c) The per capita water availability is reducing progressively due to increasing population. It is estimated that the average annual per capita water availability may come down from about 1869 cu. m. at present to 1350 cu. m. by 2025 A. D. at the national level. According to international criteria any situation of yearly water availability or less than 1000 cu. m. per capita is considered as scarcity condition. Therefore, even by the end of 2025 A. D., India is not likely to face water scarcity situation at the national level, though uneven water availability may cause local water scarcity in some parts of the country. A National Water Policy already exists which provides for planning and management of country’s water resources on a sustainable basis. However, since the adoption of the National Water Policy in 1987, a number of problems/challenges have emerged in the development and
..2
..2.. management of the Water Resources Sector. As such, the existing National Water Policy has been reviewed by the National Water Board (NWB) in the context of existing problems/emerging challenges and also in the light of the experiences of the last 13 years of its implementation. The updated draft National Water Policy finalished by NWB in October, 1998 provides for multi- sectoral perspective and participatory approach towards resources planning and management; integration of quantity, quality and environmental aspects and private sector participation in the water resources management, mandatory operation and maintenance, funding and related policies for revenue generation; and reforms related to legislations, institutions, environment and technology etc., under the Water Resources Sector. However, declaration of the new National Water Policy depends on its adoption by the National Water Resources Council.

(a) what criteria have been set for selecting the places for upgradation of airports; and

(b) the names of the international airports which are operating in the country at present?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV)

(a):- The criteria for setting up of international airports are as under:

(i) There should be a demand for international operations;

(ii) There should be facilities for customs, immigration, health, plant quarantine, etc.

(iii) The runway length should be minimum 9000 feet of adequate strength for operation of Medium Capacity Low Range

(MCLR) aircraft which constitute majority of the aircraft now for international operations; and

(iv) Adequate communication, navigation and surveillance and landing aids for all weather operations.

(b):- Till recently, there were five international airports at Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Calcutta and Thiruvananthapuram. It has now been decided to declare existing domestic airports at Bangalore, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Goa, Amritsar, Guwahati and the new Cochin Airport at Nedumbassery also as international airports.

Further, Prasar Bharati, in July, 1999, has engaged a marketing consultancy firm namely Quadra Advisory to update the report submitted by the Expert Committee and elaborate on measures for operationalising its main recommendations. The firm has submitted its report and actions on its recommendations are being taken by Prasar Bharati. Future steps contemplated by Prasar Bharati(Doordarshan) include:

(i) Modification of programming mix;

(ii) Improvement of signal quality ;

(iii) Invitation to both TAM and INTAM and participation in the rating process by subscribing to the better of the two agencies; and

records.qtitle: . COMPUTATION OF RATE OF INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to include the production of 543 items to determine the rate of index of industrial production;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is also a fact that so far 342 items were included to determine the rate of the index of industrial production; and

(d) if so, what is the reason for including these new items and the names of these items?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN) ) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.



STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 146 FOR ANSWER ON 6.3.2000

(a) to (d) The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is a monthly index compiled and released by Central Statistical Orgamsation(CSO) to measure changes in the volume of production in physical terms. In order to accurately reflect the growth rate in the industrial sector, the base period of the index has been changed from time to time to reflect the changing structure of the industrial economy. The latest revision has made the base year 1993-94 from the earlier base year l980-81. The revised indices were released on 27th May, 1998. The revision of the coverage of items and industries as well as the technique of construction has changed. Consequently, 543 items have been included compared to 352 items in the earlier IIP (Base 1980-81). m the revised series of IIP with the base 1993-94, the items were selected on the basis of the criteria that each item so selected should account for at least Rs. 80 crore of Gross Value of Output (GVO) at the overall manufacturing level and Gross Value Added (GVA) of Rs.20 crore at the ultimate digit level of NIC. The criteria were applied flexibly in the case of industry groups which were not adequately represented. Therefore, items of importance are included and unimportant items are dropped m the new item basket. The list of new item groups alongwith the corresponding individual items included in the revised series of IIP is enclosed.

(d) if so, the details thereof;
records.ans_text:
MINISTER FOR COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)

(a) and (b) Yes Sir. For the purpose of recognition as Export House/ Trading House/ Star Trading House/ Super Star Trading House, triple weightage is given on FOB or net foreign exchange on the export of product manufactured and exported by units in the Small Scale Industries (SSI)/ Tiny Sector/ Cottage Sector and double weightage on FOB or net foreign exchange to merchant exporter exporting products reserved for SSI units and manufactured by units in the Small Scale Industry (SSI)/Tiny sector/Cottage Sector . For promoting exports of SSI products, 2% additional Special Import License is also given to Export House, Trading House, Star Trading House and Super Star Trading House.

(c) and (d) As per information compiled by the Export Promotion Councils and Commodity Boards, export figures in respect of small scale sector for the year 1998-99 have been estimated at Rs.48979.23 crores. Exports from small scale during the year 1997-98 were estimated at Rs.44442.18 crores. Accordingly, exports during 1998-99 have shows an increase of 10.20% over the year 1997-98. The figures for the year 1999-2000 are not available yet.

records.ans_text:

records.qtitle: POWER GENERATION FROM RESIDUUM OF SUGARCANES .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that power can be generated in the country from the residuum of sugarcanes after the process of crushing thereof in sugar-mills;

(b) whether Government have made any assessment of power generation capacity by the above process; and

(c) if so, the production capacity in the financial year 1998-99 alongwith the assessment of average cost of power generation?
records.ans_text:

records.qtitle: FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESERVES IN THE COUNTRY
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the details of maximum and minimum amount of the foreign exchange reserves during first 10 months of the financial year 1999-2000; and

(c) the amount received from the resources from which is included in the said foreign exchange reserves together with the amount received from these sources during the said period while having the maximum amount in the reserve?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)

(a) : India`s foreign exchange reserves, including gold and SDRs, as on February 18, 2000 amounted to US$ 35193 million, which is considered adequate, judged in terms of critical indicators such as, import cover of reserves and debt service payments.

(b) : During the first ten months (April 1999 to January 2000) of the financial year 1999-2000, the level of foreign exchange reserves was maximum at US $ 35170 million on January 21, 2000 and it was minimum at US $ 32535 million on April, 1,1999.

(c) : Movements in foreign exchange reserves reflect the net outcome of inflows and outflows of foreign exchange on account of transactions in the current and capital accounts of India`s balance of payments. Therefore, it is not possible to establish one-to-one correspondence between changes in reserves and movement in each of these transactions. However, it can be stated that the build up of foreign exchange reserves in the current financial year so far has been made possible largely because of sharp recovery of exports, buoyancy in invisible receipts, sharp turnaround in portfolio investments by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) and significant net accretions to Non-Resident Indian (NRI) deposits.

records.qtitle: AGREEMENT BETWEEN AMERICA AND INDIA TO REMOVE RESTRICTIONS H
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that an agreement has been entered into between America and India recently to the effect that all the restrictions imposed on India, so far, will be removed by 1st April, 2001;

(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that as per the agreements of World Trade Organisation these restrictions are to be removed by the year 2003;

(c) if so, the reasons for removing these restrictions two years earlier; and

(d) the expected benefits to be accrued to the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)

(a)to (d): India has been maintaining Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) on imports for Balance of Payments (BOP) reasons. In January 1997, following an improvement in its BOP position the `Committee on BOP Restrictions` of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) invited India to present a phase out Plan for elimination of its remaining QRs maintained for BOP purposes. India presented a nine year phase out plan for removal of its QRs, which was further reduced to seven years but even this was not acceptable to a number of India`s trading partners. Consequently, the Committee concluded its consultations without any decision.
Subsequently, India held consultations and signed bilateral agreements with Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Switzerland, European Union and Japan for a six year phase out of its QRs on BOP grounds by 31/3/2003. However, such consultations with USA did not fructify and the USA initiated a dispute against India in the WTO. The Dispute Settlement Panel and the Appellate Body ruled against India holding that India was not justified in maintaining its QRs on BOP grounds. Following adoption of these reports by the Dispute Settlement Body (DSB), a reasonable period of time (RPT) had to be determined for India to implement the rulings and recommendations of the DSB. The RPT can be determined either through arbitration where the maximum period normally granted is 15 months or through bilateral agreement between parties to the dispute. India and the USA have signed a bilateral agreement for determining the RPT, which would be of little over 18 months. As per the agreement, all the existing QRs on BOP grounds would have to be removed by 1/4/2001.

records.qtitle: REGULATORY AUTHORITY FOR SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.min_name: SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND RURAL AND AGRO INDUSTR
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES

(SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE)

(a)&(b) Yes, Sir. The Indian Council of Small Scale Industries (ICSI) has submitted a memorandum which, inter-alia, suggests setting up of a Regulatory Authority/Commission to eliminate sickness in small scale industries (SSIs). The major demands in the memorandum are:- implementation of the Nayak Committee recommendations, feasibility of fixing separate targets for SSI, tiny and village industries, encouraging factoring services and availability of credit through hypothecation, allowing friends/relatives to finance SSIs, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to advise the banks to adopt a specific time frame to clear loan applications, mechanism to easily liquidate non-viable sick units, setting up Sub-committees of State Level Inter Institutional Committee (SLIIC) to look into the specific individual cases of rehabilitation, setting up of Regulatory Authority/Commission to eliminate sickness in industry and certain fiscal suggestions.


(c)&(d) The demands of ICSI were considered by the Government.
(i) All the major recommendations of the Nayak Committee have been accepted by the RBI and the banks have been advised to implement them. Periodical special studies conducted by the RBI have also revealed that the Committee’s recommendations are being progressively implemented by the banks;
(ii) Banks have been advised by the RBI that out of the funds made available to SSIs, 40% should be made available for the units with investments in plant and machinery upto Rs. 5.00 lakhs, 20% for units with investment between Rs. 5.00 lakhs and Rs. 25.00 lakhs and remaining 40% for the other SSI units;
(iii) Factoring services are already available through the Canara Bank and SBI. Credit on hypothecation is being provided by banks;
(iv) There is no bar against borrowing money from friends and relatives of the promoters of the SSIs;
(v) The RBI has issued guidelines to the banks that loan applications upto a credit limit of Rs. 25,000/- should be disposed of within a fortnight and those for over Rs. 25,000/- within 8 or 9 weeks;
(vi) The system of one time settlement and compromise settlement exists for liquidation of dues of the non-viable sick units;
(vii) Under SLIIC, there exists a Sub-Committee at the State level to look into the viability and rehabilitation aspects of individual sick units, under the Chairmanship of Director (Industries) of the State. There also exists in each district a Sick Units Rehabilitation Committee headed by Deputy Commissioner/District Collector to look into the rehabilitation of sick units;
(viii) Regarding setting up of a Regulatory Authority, the RBI has advised that it will be of little assistance in eliminating sickness in SSIs as sickness can be caused by various factors and it may not be possible to eliminate it altogether. The data on sickness compiled by the RBI upto March, 1998 shows that sickness has been coming down during the last three years and constant dialogue and interaction with the representatives of SSIs is going on. Constant efforts are being made to solve their problems.

(c) whether Government have taken any concrete action to make this method foolproof; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS.

(SHRI ARUN SHOURIE)

(a)&(b): The estimates of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) are compiled using basic data available from different sources. The sources of data include agricultural output based on the area statistics, productivity and prices provided by the State governments, industrial and services statistics from Annual Survey of Industries and Enterprise Surveys, conducted specifically to collect these data, annual reports and budget documents of public sector undertakings and government departments. The data collection methods have remained more or less unchanged. Over the years deficiencies have crept in. Moreover, data about the same head collected from different sources have come to show considerable discrepancies.

(c)&(d): The Government has established a National Statistical Commission on 19.1.2000 headed by Dr. C. Rangarajan to critically examine the deficiencies of the present statistical system with a view to recommending measures for a systematic revamping of the system, so as to improve the availability and quality of basic statistics. There is also a proposal for modernising the Indian Statistical System with possible external assistance.

ANNEX -II
Handloom Sector:

(i) Workshed-cum-housing Scheme for Handloom Weavers: This is a production-cum-welfare oriented scheme and it was introduced in 1985-86 with the objective of providing a dwelling unit and a suitable workplace to weavers to improve their productivity and earnings. The scheme is being implemented by the respective State Handloom Corporations, primary societies or other specialized agencies nominated by the Government

(ii) Project Package Scheme (PPS) for Handloom Weavers: The PPS aims to provide infrastructural support for increasing production, productivity and marketing of handloom products, protect traditional ethnic and languishing crafts and adopt an area development approach for development of handlooms in hilly and sparsely populated areas. The scheme is being funded on the basis of equal sharing of contribution by Central and State Government/implementing agency.

(iii) Handloom Development Centres and Quality Dyeing Units: The aim of setting up of HDCs and QDUs is to make necessary arrnagements for procurement of hank yarn, preparing production plans keeping in view the market demand and set up marketing outlets.

(iv) Group Insurance Scheme: The Group Insurance Scheme was introduced in 1992-93 in order to meet socio-economic obligation of weavers towards their family and the uncertainty of their working capacity, particularly in old age. Under the scheme a weaver is provided with insurance coverage of Rs. 10,000 for an annual premium of Rs.120. The premium is shared equally among the beneficiary, Central Government and the State Government.

(v) New Insurance Scheme: A new insurance package scheme for handloom weavers was introduced in 1997-98. The new scheme provides for enhanced coverage against various types of risks at the same premium of Rs. 120. However, the share of the Central Government has been increased from Rs. 40 to Rs. 60 per annum and the share of weavers has been reduced from Rs. 40 to Rs. 20 per annum.

(vi) Health Package Scheme : The Health Package Scheme was introduced in 1992-93 with the objective of ameliorating some of the health problems related to the profession of handloom weaving. Under the scheme the weavers are provided financial assistance for treatment of diseases like asthama, TB, etc. and for meeting the cost of testing of eyes and spectacles, supply of drinking water, maternity problems.

(vii) Thrift Fund Scheme: The Thrift Fund Scheme was introduced in 1985-86 as a welfare scheme for handloom weavers and it was modified in the year 1991-92. The scheme aims at creation of a fund in the nature of provident fund with 8% of wages earned as contribution from the weaver and 4% of the wages each from Central Government and the State Governments. The fund earns saving bank interest rate.

(viii) Market Development Assistance: The Market Development Assistance Scheme provides marketing assistance to the handloom sector. This is in lieu of Share Capital Assistance Scheme to Apex Societies and Corporations, Share capital and managerial subsidy to Primary Societies and Special Rebate Scheme. Apart from providing assistance to State Handloom Weavers Cooperative Societies, it also envisages providing assistance to national level handloom organisations viz. All India Handloom Fabrics Marketing Cooperative Societies Ltd., Delhi; North Eastern handicrafts and Handloom Development Corporation, Guwahati; Rehabilitation Industries Corporation, New Delhi, etc. The MDA assistance to the state organisation is shared equally by the respective State Governments and Central Government.

(ix) Janata Cloth Scheme: This scheme was launched in 1976 and continued after 1993 till 1997-98 with modifications. The aim of the revised scheme (1993) was (1) to provide sustained income to handloom weavers particularly, the semi-skilled weavers by partially off-setting the cost disadvantage of handloom sector; (2) to enable handloom weavers graduate to production of higher value textile goods so as to earn higher wages; and (3) to provide alternate employment to handloom weavers displaced on account of phasing out of Janata Cloth Scheme.

(x) Mill Gate Price Scheme: The Mill Gate Price Scheme is operated through National Handloom Development Corporation (NHDC) and is meant for supply of hank yarn to handloom weavers at mill gate prices.In order to help marketing of handloom textiles by various agencies and to make available handloom items under one roof in various townships having potential for marketing of handloom items, the concept of group merchandizing in the form of marketing complexes has been designed and National Handloom Development Corporation has been entrusted with the task of implementation of the concept.

(xi) Development of Exportable Products and their Marketing: In order to give substantial impetus to the export of handloom fabric, made-ups and other handloom items from the country, Scheme for Development of Exportable Products and their marketing has been introduced during 1996-97. Under the Scheme, assistance is available for developing exportable products, for building up of production capability for export and thereafter marketing it. The project cost in respect of the agencies sponsored by the State Government is shared by the State Government itself or by the beneficiary agency. The agencies sponsored by Central Government are entitled to 100% assistance from the Government of India under the Scheme.

(xii) Publicity and Exhibition: To provide marketing support to handloom agencies and the individual weavers, the office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms organizes the National Handloom Expos, District Level Events, Craft Melas, etc. in different parts of the country. For this purpose, the financial support is provided to the implementing agency towards infrastructure, publicity, etc. These activities are supportive to the handloom agencies, weavers and also to the consumer as it provides them an opportunity to purchase the handloom products of various states under one roof. Powerloom Sector:

(a) Powerloom Service Centre(PSC): Under this scheme Powerloom Service Centres have been established at important locations. These Centres are responsible not only for imparting training to powerloom weavers but also for creating new designs and providing testing facilities. Till date 43 PSCs have been set up.

(b) Powerloom Workers` Insurance Scheme: The Government of India introduced a Group Insurance Scheme for Powerloom workers in association with the Life Insurance Corporation of India during the year 1992-93. All Powerloom workers of age between 18 and 60 years and those who work during the year are eligible for insurance under this Scheme. A weaver, who had earned at least minimum average pay of Rs. 700 per month during a year, can join the Scheme. The Scheme envisages an annual premium to be shared equally by the Central Government, the State Government and the Powerloom worker.

(c) Computer Aided Design Centres: For providing facilities for design development and product diversification for the powerloom sector, Computer Aided Design Centres are being set up at important powerloom centres. Research & Development The Government has taken up a programme for providing facilities to meet the testing needs of the country. Under this programme existing laboratories are being upgraded and wherever required new laboratories are being established. The prime objective is to provide testing facilities at easy distance to the textile industry.

Government is aware of the sinister designs of the ISI and has taken all necessary measures to curb its evil designs. It has been regularly sharing he inputs and sensitizing the concerned state Government and agencies regarding the activities of ISI.
