records.qtitle: . POWER PRODUCTION IN THE HYDRO ELECTRIC SECTOR
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to promote the production of power in hydro-electric sector;

(b) if not, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether Government have found out the possibilities of utilization of capacity of power production in the hydro-electric sector in northern, eastern, western and southern regions of the country; and

(d) if so, the total amount of un-utilised power production capacity in each region and what are the schemes to utilize the same?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER ( SHRI P.R. KUMARAMANGALAM )



(a) to (d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.






STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 246 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 15.12.1999 REGARDING POWER PRODUCTION IN THE HYDRO-ELECTRIC SECTOR.


(a) & (b) : Yes, Sir. The Government had announced a policy on hydro power development in August, 1998 with the objective of accelerating the pace of hydro power development in the country. The share of hydro power has been continuously declining during the last three decades. As against an ideal hydel - thermal mix of 40:60, the share has gone down from 44% in 1970s to 25% in 1999. An improvement in the hydel thermal mix is proposed to be achieved by
(i) completion of the on-going hydroelectric projects;
(ii) initiating advance action for obtaining necessary approvals in respect of new hydroelectric projects for which DPR is available; and
(iii) initiating work on survey and investigation in respect of new green field sites to enable preparation of DPR so that necessary approvals could be obtained and projects taken up for execution in a phased manner.


(c) & (d) : The Central Electricity Authority on the basis of assessment carried out during 1978-87 had assessed the economically exploitable hydro potential of the country at 84,044 MW at 60% load factor. The region-wise position as on 1.12.1999 with regard to assessed potential, potential developed and under development is indicated in Annexure-I.
There is a substantial scope for promoting hydroelectric projects in North Eastern and Northern regions. A list of hydroelectric projects under execution is at Annexure-II. The region-wise list of hydroelectric projects in the Central Sector which are proposed to be taken up for benefits during the 10th Plan is at Annexure-III. The region-wise list of projects to be taken up in the Central Sector in respect of which survey and investigations are proposed to be taken up in order to enable preparation of DPRs is at Annexure-IV.
In the Southern region, efforts are being made in consultation with the Governments of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu to promote hydroelectric projects in the Cauvery basin which could not be taken up due to inter-state river dispute.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE) PLANNING, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBIC GRIEVANCES IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS.

(a) & (b) : As per the information available with the Ministry of Finance, the estimated strength of the Central Government employees as on 1 March, 1999 was 39,02,303.


(c), (d), (e) & (f): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.



STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (c),(d),(e) &

(f) OF RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 949 FOR ANSWER ON 9TH DECEMBER, 1999.

The Government has been taking measures from time to time to improve and re-organise its administrative set up to promote efficiency, keeping in view the needs of changing environment. The steps taken in the recent past include the following:

(i) Several Ministries/Departments/Organisations with considerable public interface have introduced Citizens` Charters indicating broadly the quality of service, the public would be entitled to, within a specified time frame. Information and Facilitation Counters have been set up by 45 Ministries/Departments/Central Government Organisations to provide information on procedures and the schemes of the concerned organisation as well as to access information pertaining to the status of individual cases.

(ii) Steps have also been taken to strengthen the existing machinery for redress of public grievances. Most of the Ministries/Departments have fixed time limits for handling grievances received from the Members of Parliament, and the names of the officers handling grievances have been publicised. A system of categorising all the grievances and their computerised monitoring has been installed in various Ministries/Departments and this is linked to the main terminal in the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances.

(iii) The Government has also taken up simplification of laws, rules and procedures for improving efficiency in the organisations. Towards this end, over 40 Departments have undertaken, through expert Task Forces or by internal exercises, a detailed review of laws, regulations and procedures administered by them.

(iv) A Commission on Review of Administrative Laws was set up on 8 May, 1998 under the Chairmanship of Shri P.C. Jain with a view to identify proposals for amendment/repeal of existing laws, regulations and procedures having inter-sectoral impact so as to make them objective, transparent and predictable. The Commission submitted its report on 30 September, 1998. The important recommendations of the Commission include repeal of almost 50% of Central Laws (1382 out of 2500 Laws), expeditious amendments to a critical list of 109 identified Acts, documentation of administrative laws (rules, regulations, executive instructions) by all the Ministries/Departments, harmonisation of statutes and laws with reference to the perspective of domestic and foreign investors, trade and industry, consumers, exporters and importers, and development of a viable alternative disputes resolution machinery. The Government has constituted a Standing Committee under the Chairmanship of Secretary(Personnel) for monitoring the follow-up action on implementation of the recommendations contained in the report. The Committee has held fifteen meetings with different Ministries/Departments in groups. Most of the Ministries/Departments have initiated action to make suitable amendments/modifications to or repeal the Acts and Laws being administered by them with a view to improve service delivery and bring about transparency in the functioning of Government.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SURFACE TRANSPORT

(DR.DEBENDRA PRADHAN )

(a) to (d) Cargo handling in ports depends on the cargo handling capacity of ports and not the number of ports. The total cargo handling capacity of the major ports in the country as on 31.3.99 is 240 million tonnes. Against this capacity, major ports handled 251.72 million tonnes of cargo during the year 1998-99. Steps have been taken to create additional capacity in the existing major ports under various plan schemes as well as through private sector investment to meet growing demand of the trade. A new port at Ennore, 25 kms. north of Chennai, is being constructed at an estimated revised cost of Rs.927.10 crores with assistance from Asian Development Bank with a capacity to handle 16 million tonnes of coal. The port is expected to be commissioned by July, 2000.

records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SBPBK SATYANARAYANA RAO)

(a): Pulses are one of the major sources of protein. The per capita requirement of protein per day is assessed by Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) at 60 gms for man and 50 gms for woman out of which contribution of pulses is about two-thirds i.e. 33 gms. per day. 65% of the weight of pulses contain protein. Thus to obtain 33 gms per capita per day of proteins, 53 gms pulses are required per capita per day. At this rate the annual requirement works out to about 180 lakh Metric tonnes. As against this, the availabliity is 158.9 lakh Metric tonnes.

records.qtitle: SIMPLIFICATION OF PROCEDURE FOR FOREIGN CAPITAL INVESTMENT
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have recently simplified the procedure regarding foreign capital investment;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the said facilities regarding foreign capital investment in certain sectors are not available; and

(d) if so, the names of such sectors in this regard?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance

( Balasaheb Vikhe Patil )

(a) & (b) : In furtherance of the ongoing liberalisation efforts, Government has taken initiatives to boost inflow of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) like conveying decision on all FIPB proposals within 30days, allowing 100% foreign equity in construction & maintenance of roads, highways, vehicular tunnels, ports & Harbour subject to certain minimum conditions. Prior approval of RBI for FDI proposals under the automatic as well as FIPB route have been dispensed with.

Foreign Investment Implementation Authority has been constituted which overseas the implementation of FIPB approvals.

Certain initiatives to attract portfolio investments from FIIs have recently been taken which include simplification in registration requirements of sub-accounts and permissions for tendering securities directly in terms of takeovers, for trading in derivative contracts and for hedging foreign exchange risk through purchase of forward cover on incremental equity investments. The 100% Debt Fund FIIs have been permitted to invest in unlisted debt securities in addition to listed debt securities.

Certain policy initiatives have also been taken with a view to simplify procedure for NRI investment in mutual funds, extending screen-based automated trading overseas, revising portfolio investment ceiling for NRIs/PIOs/OCBs from 1% to 5% and 5% to 10% respectively, simplifying procedure for extension of validity for NRIs/PIOs/OCBs and introduction of one stage approval for all schemes following under RBI approval mechanism.

Guidelines on Euro Issues have been relaxed permitting unlisted company for floating issues, removal of stipulation of validity period and permitting Information Technology Service companies to issue ADR/GDR linked stock option to their employees.

(c ) & (d) : Certain sectors like Arms and ammunition and allied items, Defence equipment, Atomic Energy, Real Estate, Housing, Agriculture and Plantation etc. are not open for Foreign Direct Investment.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, the total diametrical area affected by this destructive earthquake; and

(c) the details of the diametrical areas of heavy, light and mild tremors, separately, which inflicted heavy, light and negligible damages ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI)

(a&b): Yes Sir. An earthquake of magnitude 6.8 on Richter scale occurred on 29.3.1999 at 00 hrs 35 min. 1ST in Chamoli District of Uttar Pradesh. The six districts viz. Chamoli, Rudraprayag, Tehri Garhwal, Bageshwar, Uttar Kashi and Pauri Garhwal were affected by the earthquake.

(c): The impact of the earthquake was comparatively more severe in the districts of Chamoli and Rudraprayag. The survey conducted so far by GSI in the Garhwal Himalayas has shown that damage in the form of large cracks, failure of individual structural elements, collapse of partition walls, particularly those made of mud mortar, has been observed in an approximate area of 1800 sq. km spread in Chamoli, Rudraprayag and Tehri districts. The reinforced concrete structures have suffered minor damages only. The estimated intensity in this area is VII on MSK scale. The maximum intensity noted in the narrow epicentral tract including Chamoli is VIII. Studies are continuing to constrain various isoseismal zones in the area being surveyed.

records.qtitle: ROLE OF UNO IN REGARD OF NATO S ATTACKS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that the U.N. Security Council was not able to play a satisfactory role in peace keeping at the recent attacks on Yugoslavia by the NATO countries;

(b) if so, the reaction of Government in this regard;

(c) Whether Government have considered the necessity of bringing comprehensive improvement in the present structure and working of the U.N.O.; and

(d) if so, the action taken in this regard ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT SINGH)
a. The UN Security Council had been considering the developments in & b. the 
autonomous province of Kosovo, Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. It had authorised 
the Contact Group on the former Yugoslavia to deal with the situation in Kosovo. 
However, without due authorisation of the Council, NATO launched attacks against 
the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Government has been closely following these 
developments and expressed its serious concern on March 24 and 25, 1999. Our 
statements have categorically expressed themselves against any action unilateral 
or otherwise, in contravention of the UN Charter. This unilateral action has 
seriously undermined the authority of the entire UN system. We have called for 
the resolution of crisis through peaceful means within the framework of the 
sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
C & d: India supports expansion of the UN Security Council with a view to 
enhance representation of developing countries in permanent as well as 
non-permanent members` category. Expansion and reform should be integral parts 
of a common package. India is taking active part in the discussions of the 
Open-Ended Working Group of the UN General Assembly on Security Council 
restructuring.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether any action has been taken by Government to contain the continuous losses to the Delhi Milk Scheme;

(b) if so, whether possibilities have been explored to have a cut on various existing items like expenditure on management, distribution, administration, processing and purchasing, etc.;

(c) if so, the details thereof and the names of such items alongwith the possible cuts on each item; and

(d) if no action has been taken in this regard the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SOMPAL)

(a) to (d): The main reason of continuous losses to Delhi Milk Scheme is the huge difference between me cost price and selling price of milk. At present, the average cost price of the processed milk of Delhi Milk Scheme (April, 98 to January, 99) is Rs.12.84 per litre (Toned in polypack) and Rs.11.59 per litre

(Double Toned in polypack) whereas its selling price is Rs.7/- and Rs.6/- per litre respectively which was fixed by the Government in September, 1992. The same milk (Toned in polypack) is being sold by Mother Dairy @ Rs.13/- per litre. Apart from it, to contain the amount of losses, continuous possible efforts are made by the Ministry as well as by the Scheme. The possibilities to reduce the cost price of the milk are worked out constantly and are implemented to the maximum possible extent. It is obvious that the scheme will earn profit instead of loss, if the milk is sold at the rate equivalent to the price being charged by the Mother Dairy.

records.qn_text:

(b) if so, tile names of items, alongwith the amount of concessions decided to be given, on each item; and

records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Railways, Minister of State in the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and Minister of State in the Ministry of Planning & Programme Implementation (SHRI RAM NAIK) (a) to (c): A Statement is attached, statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (c) of Unstarred Question No. 1998 by SHRI KAPIL SIBAL AND SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH for answer in Rajya Sabha on 12.3.1999 regarding Concessions in freight.

(a) & (b):- Yes, Sir. The Railways have announced tike Volume Discount Scheme and certain other concessions to attract more traffic to Rail. The details are as follows :-
(i) Grant of 10% discount on incremental traffic offered under the Volume Discount Scheme for the second half of the year 1998-99 as compared to first six months of the financial year in respect of Cement, Iron and Steel, Iron Ore, Sponge Iron and Clinker subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions.
(ii) The General Managers of Southern and Western Railways have recently been authorised to grant a freight concession of upto 10% on non-programmed imported coal traffic originating on their Railway subject to fulfilment of the stipulated conditions.

(in)The General Managers of the Zonal Railways have also been authorised to quote reduced Station to Station rates on commercial consideration in accordance with the norms laid down for the purpose.

(c):- The concessions have been introduced as a marketing strategy to attract more traffic and generate additional earnings.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the water of perennially flowing rivers in the country is utilised for domestic, irrigation and industrial purposes;

(b) if so, the annual quantity of water of these rivers estimated to be utilised for above mentioned purposes, separately;

(c) the quantity of water which flows into the sea without being used;

(d) whether Government have formulated any scheme to utilise water, flowing unused into the sea; and

(e) if so, the estimated quantity of water likely to be utilised out of the same?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND WATER RESOURCES

(SHRI SOMPAL)

(a) to (e) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (e) OF STARRED QUESTION N0.227 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA SABHA ON 11.03.1999 The average annual flow available in rivers is around 1869 billion cubic metres. Owing to the topographic, hydrological and other constraints, the utilisable water resources is assessed at 1122 billion cubic metres, consisting of 690 billion cubic metres of surface water and about 432 billion cubic metres from the annual replenishable ground water resources. Full utilisation of rain water is not possible due to topographical and environmental constraints, evaporation and vegetation losses and for allowing certain amount of water to flow in the river for maintaining the river regime. The demand of water for various uses for the year 2000 is estimated as under:- Sl. Use Water demand assessed fop 2000 A.D. No. Billion Cubic Meter

1. Domestic 33

2. Irrigation 630

3. Industry 30

4. Energy 27

5. Other 30 Total 750 Keeping in view the future needs of water, the Government has taken various policy and programme initiatives. These include adoption of National Water Policy (1987), Command Area Development Programme, preparation of National Perspective Plan for transfer of water from surplus basins to water deficit areas, water management practices promoting efficient and economic use of water for various purposes, emphasis on water conservation through various methods including use of latest technologies and peoples` participation in management of water for diverse uses setting up of National Commission for Integrated Water Resources Development Plan in September, 1996 as well as launching of Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme since 1996-97 for expeditious completion of selected ongoing major and medium irrigation and multipurpose projects. Government is also promoting rain water harvesting and watershed management to replenish groundwater. Planning, formulation and execution of water resources schemes is the responsibility of the State Government. Since the beginning of the Plan era, various steps have been taken for exploitation of available water resources. A number of small and large dams were taken up and as a result of this, the total live storage capacity has increased from 15.64 BCM at the beginning of plan era to about 177 BCM in 1995. Besides, an additional live storage capacity of 75 BCM will be created through dams under various stages of construction. In addition, dams under formulation/consideration will provide an additional live average of 132 BCM.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government propose to make a standing arrangement for extending the benefits of new agricultural research conducted in laboratories to the cultivators of the country; and

(b) if so, the outlines of the arrangement; and if not, the reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SOMPAL)

(a)&(b): Standing arrangements do exist for extending the benefits of agricultural research to the farmers, the outlines of the existing arrangement comprise the following; The State extension agencies besides in-field guidance, organize trainings, demonstrations, exposure visits to educate the farmers about adoption of new technologies evolved by the research system. Such efforts are supplemented through exhibitions, Kisan Melas, field days, group meetings as also through print and electronic media support. Krishi Vigyan Kendras, Farmers Training Centre, State Agricultural Universities, Non-governmental Organizations, Cooperatives, Corporate Sector, Input agencies also participate in the dissemination process.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the power transmission and distribution losses increased in 1997-98, as compared to 1993-94;

(c) whether the percentage of such losses in Delhi is highest among all the States of the country; and

(d) if so, the estimated quantity of such losses at present and the reasons for this highest loss?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER, PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND NON-CONVEFTIONAL ENERGY -SOURCES

( SHRI P.R. KUMARAMANGALAM )

(a) : The figures of power transmission and distribution losses for the year 1997-98 are not yet available. It is a fact that T&D losses (including theft/pilferage} have increased from 1993-94. The losses are provisionally estimated to be 23.41% on all-India basis for the year 1996-97, which is the latest year for which losses are available.

(b) : The T&D losses, including theft/pilferage, in the year 1993-94 and 1996-97 are given below: Year % of T&D loss (all India) 21.41% 23.41% (provisional) 1997-98 not available

(c) & (d) : Yes, Sir, the percentage transmission and distribution loss, including theft/pilferage, in Delhi Vidyut Board for the year 1996-97 {latest year for which date is available) was 49% as compared to the national average of 23.41% for the same period. The reasons for high T&D losses are given below:
(i) Inadequate investment in transmission and distribution system.
(ii) Inadequate reactive compensation at the load point;
(iii) Inadequate maintenance of equipment.
(iv) Willful tampering and by-passing of energy meters, non-functioning energy meters, defective meters, errors in meter readings, pilferage and theft of energy, unauthorised connections etc.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have recently accorded sanction for export of herbal products;

(b) if so, the details of such products and herbs used for them;

(c) whether Government have fixed the maximum limit for export of such products; and

(d) if not, the reasons therefor and details of annual production and consumption of such herbs in the country ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE SHRI RAMAKRISHNA HEGDE)

(a)to(d) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. Statement referred to in reply to Parts (a)to(d) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.175 for answer on 8th March, 1999. Regarding `Export of Herbal Products`. ## Under the Exim Policy 1997-2002 export of herbal products is freely allowed. Export of only certain species of plants, plant portions and their derivatives and extracts obtained from the wild has been prohibited. However, export of cultivated varieties of these species including their derivatives and extracts

(including value added herbal formulations), except that of Red Sanders, is freely allowed subject to production of certificate of Cultivation from the designated authorities. List of such species of plants is available under Appendix 2 Schedule 2 of the book titled` ITC(HS) Classification of Export and import Items 1997-2002` which is a published document. No maximum limit for export of such items has been fixed. Most of the species listed in the ITC(HS) Classification book are found as naturally growing stock in the wild and their cultivation outside the forest is almost negligible. It is for this reason that annual production and consumption of such herbs is not assessed and the data thereof is not maintained.

records.name: Kapil Sibal

(a) whether it is a fact that no benefit is being derived by the respective sections of the society from the findings of research and invention being successfully carried out in the laboratories in the country;

(b) whether it is also a fact that no information network is available the country on permanent basis order to implement the successful findings of these researches and inventions; and

(c) if the answer to part

(b) above be in the negative; what are the details thereof? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF SCIENCE ANDTECHNOLOGY(DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI) {a),{b) and(c): No, Sir. A number of technologies developed in the laboratories in the area of agriculture, drugs and pharmaceuticals, industrial catalysts, food processing , construction materials, leather processing and products, etc. have been successfully transferred for application in the society. The national laboratories have their own mechanisms for transfer of successful findings and technologies to the society. Information systems like National Information System for Science and Technology (NISSAT), Ocean Observation and Information Services (OOIS), Bio-Informatic Center, Technology Information System

(TIFACLINE), National Research Development Corporation (NRDC) Krishi Vigyan Kendras, etc play key role in dissemination of successful findings and inventions in the country.

records.qtitle: HARMFUL EFFECTS OF TERMINATOR SEEDS ON AGRICULTURE
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that foodgrain production by using the terminator seeds in agriculture sector in the country have proved damaging;

(b) if not, what is Government`s reactions thereto; and

(c) what risks are likely to be involved using terminator seeds in agriculture sector? A N S W E R
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE

(SHRI SOMPAL)

(a)&(b): A patent on `Control of plant gene expression` US patent No.5723765 has been taken jointly by the Delta and Pine Land Company and the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) for controlling the viability of seeds produced without adversely affecting the crop. This method is termed as `Terminator Technology`. The seeds containing the terminator technology has not been allowed to enter into India through legal channels. Hence, its damaging effects on the country`s foodgrain production have not been tested.

(c): The risks likely to be associated with terminator seeds in agriculture sector include:
(i) the farmers will not be in a position to use seeds saved from the previous crop and will have to buy seeds for each sowing;
(ii) it will threaten the farmer`s expertise in seed selection and traditional conservation methods of carrying forward the seeds;
(iii) it will have implications on crop biodiversity.

records.qtitle: SCHEME FOR DEVELOPMENT AND EXPANSION OF TEXTILE INDUSTRY .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:

(b) if so, whether Government have also formulated any action-plan regarding research and exploration of new techniques for utilisation of the textile industry in the country; and

(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, me reasons therefor ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI KASHIRAM RANA)

(a) to (c) There are 8 Textile Research Associations me functioning of which is jointly funded by Government of India, State Governments and industry. These Textile Research Associations generally undertake activities pertaining to Research and Development, providing services based on R&D including testing, and imparting technical education. They also carry out innovative work and render consultancy services to industry on various aspects of textile technology, including human resource development, and the application of scientific methodology in the textile industry to improve its technological performance and profitability. The research and services are intended also to reduce the costs and improve the quality and durability of fabrics, reduced pollution, conserve energy, utilise waste, and adopt new technology or improve existing technologies. .Government has approved launching of Textile Upgradation Fund Scheme under which loans at applicable rate of interest would be available to the eligible textile and jute units. Under this Scheme, interest to the extent of 5%, interest points would be reimbursed to the lending nodal agencies (IDBI, SIDBI & IFCI) by the Ministry of Textiles.

(c) the norms fixed by Government for envisaging this amount of share?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI KASHIRAM RANA)

(a)&(b): Government has decided to launch a Technology Upgradation Fund (TUF) under which units of the identified sectors of textile and jute industry would be eligible for loans from nodal agencies at an eligible rate of interest, the difference in rate of interest would be reimbursed by the Government to the nodal agencies concerned. No share has been fixed for any particular sector of textile industry such as handloom, power-loom or mill sector.

(c): Does not arise.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news-item which appeared in the `Business Standard` of 27th November, 1999, under the caption `Loan Defaulter to be tracked on line`;

(b)s if so, whether Government propose to adopt a. policy against those people who don`t repay the loans in the stipulated period so that they are debarred from taking further loan: and

(c) if so, the details of the action being taken by Government in this regard ?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI K.M.R. JANARTHANAN)

(a), (b) & (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to Rajya Sabha Question No.331 for 22.12.98 regarding action against loan defaulters by S/Shri Kapil Sibal, M.P. and Raj Mohinder Singh, M.P

(a). Yes, Sir,

(b) & (c): In order to alert the banks and Financial Institutions (FIs) and put them on guard against the defaulters to other tending institutions, RBI has put in place a scheme to collect details about borrowers of banks and FIs with outstanding aggregating Rs-1 crore and above which are classified as `Doubtful` or `Loss` of where suits are filed, as on 31` March and 30th September each year. records.qtitle: (clubbed) . LOANS BY IRFC FROM THE FOREIGN FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS .
records.name: Barjinder Singh Hamdard
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian Railway Finance Corporation seeks loans from foreign financial institutions;

(b) if so, the total amount of loan taken from abroad by the end of March, 1998, the amount of interest on loan paid by the Corporation during 1995-96. 1996-97 and 1997-98 and the maximum and minimum rates of interest thereon; and

(c) whether the Corporation has taken loans from the foreign financial institutions during the current financial year; if so, the total amount thereof, togetherwith the amount of instalment of loan during the current year?
records.ans_text:
Minister of State in the Ministry of Railways, Minister of State in the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and Minister of State in the Ministry of Planning & Programme Implementation

(SHRI RAM NAIK)

(a) Yes, Sir. The Indian Railway Finance Corporation Limited (IRFC) had entered into a Loan Agreement with the Export-Import Bank of Japan for Japanese Yen 15 billion and a Line of Credit Agreement with the Export Development Corporation of Canada for US Dollar 52 million.

(b) An amount of Japanese Yen 11.779 billion was drawn as loan from the Export-Import Bank of Japan. Interest amounting to about Rs. 7.20 crore, Rs. 12.01 crore and Rs. 16.42 crore was paid on this loan during the years 1995-96, 1996-97 and 1997-98 respectively. The rate of interest applicable was fixed at 5.3 per cent per annum. No amount has so far been drawn from Export Development Corporation, Canada.

(c) It is scheduled to draw an amount of Japanese Yen 8.855 billion under an Agreement signed with ABN Amro Bank and the State Bank of India to refinance the existing outstanding loan from Export Import Bank of Japan and an amount of about US Dollars 40 million under the Line of Credit Agreement with Export Development Corporation, in the current financial year.

records.qtitle: STORAGE OF CRUDE OIL AND OTHER PETROLEUM PRODUCTS .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the capacity of storage of crude oil and other petroleum products in the country is not sufficient;

(b) if so, the total storage capacity of crude oil in the country at present; and

(c) whether it is also a fact that due to lack of sufficient storage facility companies have to pay huge demurrage; if so, the average amount which the Oil India Ltd. have to pay annually as demurrage?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PETROLEUM ADD NATURAL GAS(SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR )

(a) to (c) : The storage capacity of crude oil (imported and indigenous) in the country is around 6327 TMT. Imports of petroleum products are made in line with the approved plan to meet the demand. infrastrucural constraints result in congestion at the ports. Demurrage is incurred on this account and due to floating inventory in the high sea. Oil India Limited does not import crude oil or petroleum products and hence they do not incur any demurrage on account of such imports.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news item captioend `Babus Messed Up Reforms says G.V.R.` which appeared in the Economic Times dated 27th June, 1998;

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that construction cost of the power project is assessed in the international market at Rupees 2.2 crore per megawatt in terms of auctionwhile it is assessed in India at Rupees 4 crore per MW or more; and

(c) if not,the details thereof and the reasons for more cost of construction in the country?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER

(SHRI P.R.KUMARMANGALAM)

(a) to (c) : The cost of the power plant depends upon its type, capacity site conditions, type of fuel, the detailed scope of the plant and the type of financing. While the completed cost for coal based thermal power plants recently cleared by CEA is of the order to Rs. 4.2 crores/MW the cost for naphtha based combined cycle plant cleared by CEA varies from Rs- 3.0 crores/MW to Rs. 3.5 crores/MW. The cost being cleared by CEA includes duties and taxes as well as high cost of financing. Further, the Indian ambient conditions lead to power output from the same plant particularly in case of Gas Turbine Plants. This further increases the cost of power plants per MW in India. The cost being cleared by CEA is the completed cost as installed including all civil works and all other infrastructural facilities required for construction of power plants such as external water system, external fuel handling system, fuel storage etc. After allowing for all the factors mentioned above the cost of the power plants being cleared by CEA is comparable with the internationally quoted prices for the power plants which are in the range of Rs 2.0-2.3 crores/MW in case of combined cycle plants and Rs. 2.6- 3.5 crores/MW for coal based plants.

records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(SHRI K.M.R. JANARTHANAN)

(a), (b) & (c): Presumably the reference is to bad debts written-off by the public sector banks. A statement indicating the bad debts written-off by the public sector banks during the years 1994-95, 1995-96 and 1996-97 is given in the Annexure.

(d) & (e): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had advised the banks that all possible steps to recover the dues should be taken and if there are no further prospects of recovering the debt, the decision to write-off may be taken in the larger interest of the bank. With a view to expediting decision making, the Boards of Directors of individual banks have delegated suitable powers for write-off of bad debts/losses subject to prescribed safe-guards/conditions and reporting system to various functionaries.

records.name: Barjinder Singh Hamdard
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF FINANCE

(SHRI YASHWANT SINHA)

(a) & (b) The Staff Inspection Unit was constituted in April, 1964 by renaming the previous Special Reorganisation Unit of the Department of Expenditure.

(c)&(d) The work of SIU is of a continuous nature. Every year, a timetable is drawn up for inspecting selected Ministries/Departments/Offices of the Government- The purpose of the inspection is to study and determine the manpower requirements of the organisation inspected, on the basis of the total workload and in the process identify surplus staff if any. At times, though rarely, an organisation might also be found to be inadequately staffed due to increased workload etc. SUI studies of Ministries/Departments/Offices of the Government upto the end of the year 1997-98 had identified a surplus of 96,099 posts as against a total number of 6,46.175 posts covered by the studies. These are the figures mentioned in the Annual Report of the Ministry of Finance for the year 1997-98.

(c&d): Keeping` in view the urban enemployment problem in the country the Ministry of Urban Affairs & Employment has launched the Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar yojana (SJSRY), which replaced the earlier Nehru Rozgar Yojana (NRY).and Prime Minister`s integrated Urban Poverty Eradication Programme ( PMI UPEPI w.e.f. 1.12.97. seeking to provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed or under employed poor through encouraging the setting up of self-employment ventures or provision of wage-employment by utilising their labour, for construction of socially and .economically useful public assets`. This programme targets the urban poor read upto 9th standard and living below the poverty line, as defined from time to time. The SJSRY rests on foundation of Community Organisation-and Structure to provide supporting and facilitating mechanism for Local Development. The Community Development Societies (CDSs) to be set up under this programme would function as the nodal agency for implementation of the scheme. records.qn_text:

(c) if so, by when and the details of the measures taken; and

(d) whet is the number of cases in which a final decision has since been taken alongwith the cases which are still under dispute? ANSWER THE MINSTER OF STAE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE(SHRI SOMPAL)

(a) A case pertaining to the Ravi and Beas water dispute is under consideration of Ravi & Beas Waters Tribunal.

(b) to

(d) Since Punjab and Haryana, after re-organisation of Punjab could not arrive at an agreement on sharing of surplus Ravi and Beas waters within a stipulated period of two years, Government of India through a Notification dated 24th March, 1976 allocated shares of Punjab and Haryana and also that of Delhi, Rajasthan and Jammu and Kashmir in surplus Ravi-Beas waters. Punjab however, challenged the validity of this notification by filing suit in the Supreme Court. Efforts were thereafter made to resolve the issue and thus on 31.12.1981 an agreement was signed by the Hon`ble Chief Ministers of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan in the presence of then Hon`ble Prime
records.ans_text: Minister of India. The issue pertaining to sharing of waters between Punjab and Haryana was reopened consequent to the signing of the Punjab Settlement on 24.7.85 (Rajiv-Longowal Accord).  As a sequel to this settlement, Ravi and Beas  Waters Tribunal (RBWT) was constituted by Government of India to inter-alia adjudicate the claims of Punjab and Haryana regarding their shares in the remaining waters.  RBWT gave its report on 30.1.1987 setting out facts as found by it.  Thereafter, the references of Central Government as well as of the State Governments of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan on the report of RBWT were forwarded to the Tribunal on 19.08.1987 for seeking explanation/guidance.  The issue is still under the consideration of RBWT.

records.ans_text:
THE.MINISTER OF_STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONMEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (BANKING, REVENUE AND INSURANCE)

(SHRI KADAMBUR M.R.JANARTHANAN)

records.qtitle: PRIVATE SECTOR. PARTICIPATION TO BOOST CRUDE OIL EXPLORATION .
records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that Government have decided to invite participation of private sector to boost crude oil production in the country;

(b) if so, when the final decision was taken;

(c) whether it is also a fact that Government have formulated a new exploration licensing policy for this purpose; (d} if so, the date on which this policy was formulated; together with the comprehensive details thereof; and

(e) whether it has been decided to grant permission to 48 oilfields only at present, if so, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS

( SHRI SANT0SH KUMAR GANGWAR )

(a) & (b) Yes, Sir. The current phase of private participation began in 1991 with the invitation of bids for exploration blocks. Therefore, small and medium discovered fields were also offered for development by private companies and joint ventures in 1992 and 1993.

(c) to (e) New Exploration Licensing Policy was approved by the Government of India in March`97. The main features of the policy are: Allotment of blocks on open acreage system Level playing field to National Oil Companies vis-à-vis private oil companies. No blocks reserved for NOCs. No compulsory participating or carried interest by national oil companies (NOCs). International price of oil for discoveries made. No payments of signature, discovery of production bonus. No custom duty. Freedom to sell crude oil and natural gas in domestic market at market related prices. No cess on crude oil production. Royalty payment on ad-valorem basis. 12.5% for onland crude oil 10% for offshore crude oil 10% on natural gas both onshore and offshore. Half the rate of royalty on production from deep offshore blocks for first seven years after commencement of commercial production. Petroleum Tax Code to be in place. Provision for Hydrocarbon Development Fund. Beside, Govt. has given infrastructure status to E&P sector which allows 7 years Tax Holiday. Under the first round of NELP, 48 blocks are proposed to be offered for bidding. These blocks have been identified based on various considerations including geological data.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Centre for Science and Environment has observed in its report that 52,000 people in the country are losing their lives every year owing to air- pollution;

(b) if so, whether Government have assessed the abovesaid observations in the report; and

(c)

(c) if so, the reaction of Government thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS

(SHRI BABU LAL MARANDI)

(a) & (b) An article published by the Centre for Science & Environment (CSE), a non-governmental organisation, estimated that nearly52,000 premature deaths in 36 Indian cities have occurred in 1995 due to air pollution. There is no conclusive data to confirm these figures. c) The steps taken by the Government to reduce environmental pollution include the following:

1. The Government has formulated a comprehensive Policy Statement for Abatement of Pollution which envisages integration of environmental and economic aspects of development planning, lays stress on preventive aspects of pollution, promotion of cleaner technologies to reduce pollution and health related aspects;

2. Fiscal incentives are provided for installation of pollution control equipment and also for the shifting of industries from congested areas.

3. Low lead petrol had been introduced in the four metro cities of Delhi, Mumbai, Calcutta and Chennai w.e.f. June 1994. Subsequently, unleaded petrol and catalytic converter fitted vehicles were introduced in the above mentioned 4 cities with effect from 1.4.1995;

4. The Government is implementing a major plan of action for introduction of unleaded petrol and catalytic converter fitted vehicles and introduction of low sulphur diesel for cleaner diesel vehicles in a phased manner. Fuel quality standards for petrol and diesel have been notified.


5. Gross emission standards for on-road vehicles and mass emissions standards for all categories of new vehicles have been notified under the Central Motor Vehicles Rutes.1989 and are being enforced by the Departments of Transport of the various States.
6. For control of pollution from vehicles, emission norms for both petrol and diesel driven vehicles at the manufacturing stage were introduced for the first time in 1990 and made tighter in 1996. More stringent emission norms have also been notified and will come info effect from 1.4.2000.

7 Surveys have been conducted by the Central Pollution Control Board on the vehicular emissions in the major cities and towns in the country. The findings of the survey have been used for taking mitigative measures,

8. The ambient air quality of various cities and towns are being monitored regularly through a network of 290 monitoring stations under the National Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Program.

9. Emission from highly polluting industrial units and thermal power plants are regularly monitored by the Central Pollution Control Board and State Pollution Control Boards and action is taken against the defaulting units.
10. Emissions and ambient air quality standards have been notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

(b) if so, what are these schemes togetherwith the detailed outlines of each of the schemes;

(c) whether any decision has so far been taken by the Commission regarding giving clearance to these schemes; and

(d) if not, what are the reasons therefor and by when any decision is likely to be taken with regard to these schemes in future?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS. MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION

(SHRI RAM NAIK)

(a) to (d): Reference presumably is to the programme mentioned below:

1. Integrated Cereals Development Programme in Rice Based Cropping System Areas (ICDP-Rice)- 2- Integrated Cereals Development Programme in Wheat Based Cropping System Areas (ICDP-Wheat)- 3- Integrated Cereals Development Programme in Coarse Cereals Based Cropping System Areas (ICDP-Coarse Cereals). These are on`-going and continuing programmes, crucial for achievement of target of foodgrains production which for the current year has been fixed by the Planning Commission at 210 million tonnes. There is nothing pending in the Planning Commission which could come in the way of implementing these programmes or achieving the target.

records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than 1.4 crore applications have been received till 3lst October, 1998, for the allotment of permanent account number (PAN):

(b) if not, what is the actuall number of these applications and whether any deadline has been fixed to allot permanent account number to the applicants;

(c) if so, what date has been fixed in this regard and if not the reasons therefor: and

(d) what steps have been taken to do away with the inconvenience being caused due to delayed allotment of PAN ? A N S W E R
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE

(a) to (d) : A statement is laid on the Table of the House. STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PARTS (a), (b), (c) and (a) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 26 FOR THE 1ST DECEMBER., 1998 `ON ALLOTMENT OF PERMANENT ACCOUNT NUMBER`.

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) A total number of 1,51,07,026 applications for allotment of PAN have been received over the entire country as on 31.10.98. Targets have been fixed to allot PAN to these applicants

(c) In Delhi Mumbai and Chennai all applications received `by the Regional Computer Centres were to be allotted Permanent account Number under new series by 31.10.1998 and all other applicants are to be allotted Permanent account Number through On-line System by 31.03.1999. In the rest of! the country 70% of the applicants are to be allotted PN under new series by 31.03.1999.

(d) With a view to avoiding inconvenience to the persons who had applied for allotment of Permanent Account Number and have not-yet been allotted the same under first proviso to Rule 114B a person is allowed to quote General Index Register Number till such time PAN is allotted to him. Further under third proviso to Rule 114B any person who has not been allotted a PAN or who does not have a General Index Register Number and who makes a payment in cash or otherwise than by a crossed cheque drawn on a bank or by a crossed bank draft in respect of any specified transactions where quoting of Permanent account Number of General Index Register Number has been made mandatory he can make a simple declaration in Form 60 giving therein the particulars of such transaction.

(a) whether it is a fact that the rate of payment of tariff of electricity used in industrial sector in our country is higher than the average rate of tariff of electricity in other developed and developing countries in the world;

(b) if not, the average rate of tariff of electricity for industrial use in Spain, Germany, U.K., U.S.A., France, Canada, Italy, Sweden, Australia, Indonesia, Thailand and South Africa etc.; and

(c) to what extent it is more than that of in India and what is the average of electricity tariff in India?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER ( SHRI P.R. KUMARAMANGALAM )

(a) to (c) : The average Power Tariff in the country is dependent upon its cost of supply, (cost of generation plus cost of transmission and distribution), electricity pricing laws and regulation. The cost of supply is dependent upon many factors such as technology, funding pattern, interest rate, hydro mix, price and source of fuel, completed cost, the geographical area, load density, taxes and duties etc. These factors render comparability of the tariffs of different countries difficult. records.name: Kapil Sibal
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the news-item captioned `the high cost of wrong reform` which appeared in The Economic Times dated 16th September, 1998;

(b) if so, whether it is a fact that a common consumer will have to pay an estimated tariff of Rs. 7/- per unit en the power to be produced in the proposed new power houses; and

(c) if not. Government`s assessment in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.R. KUMARAMANGALAM }

(a) : Yes, Sir.

(b) & (c) : The Government of India have enacted the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998 for setting up Electricity Regulatory Commissions both at the Centre and in the States with the primary aim of rationalising power tariff and transparent policies regarding subsidies. It is hoped that these Regulatory Commissions will help in formulation of tariff policy which shall be fair to the consumers and facilitate mobilisation of adequate resources for the power sector.
